it-alto-adige-penon-kofl.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-pinzon.name: Pinzon
it-alto-adige-pinzon.grapes: Pinot Bianco, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Nero
it-alto-adige-pinzon.summary: Pinzon is a hamlet above Montan, near the Franz Haas and Pfitscher estates, giving Pinot Bianco, Sauvignon and Pinot Nero from slopes that rival Mazon across the valley floor.
it-alto-adige-pinzon.terroir: Porphyry and calcareous soils, west-facing. The official boundary, in Montagna/Montan, reaches from about 300 to 550 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Pinot Bianco, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Nero.
it-alto-adige-pinzon.nerd_note: UGA wines must come entirely from the named site, at yields at least 25 percent below the DOC maximum, with one to five permitted varieties per UGA, and must carry the Consorzio's UGA symbol on the label.
it-alto-adige-pinzon.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-pinzon-gebach.name: Pinzon-Gebach
it-alto-adige-pinzon-gebach.summary: Pinzon-Gebach is a small Montan site reserved for Sauvignon Blanc.
it-alto-adige-pinzon-gebach.terroir: Porphyry and moraine. The official boundary, in Montagna/Montan, lies at about 370 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Sauvignon Blanc.
it-alto-adige-pinzon-gebach.nerd_note: UGA wines must come entirely from the named site, at yields at least 25 percent below the DOC maximum, with one to five permitted varieties per UGA, and must carry the Consorzio's UGA symbol on the label.
it-alto-adige-pinzon-gebach.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-planitzing.name: Planitzing
it-alto-adige-planitzing.grapes: Pinot Bianco, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Nero
it-alto-adige-planitzing.summary: Planitzing is a hamlet on the upper slopes of Kaltern, known for crisp Pinot Bianco and Sauvignon, and Pinot Nero.
it-alto-adige-planitzing.terroir: Limestone debris and moraine at the foot of the Mendola. The official boundary, in Caldaro/Kaltern, reaches from about 400 to 620 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Pinot Bianco, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Nero.
it-alto-adige-planitzing.nerd_note: UGA wines must come entirely from the named site, at yields at least 25 percent below the DOC maximum, with one to five permitted varieties per UGA, and must carry the Consorzio's UGA symbol on the label.
it-alto-adige-planitzing.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-plantaditsch.name: Plantaditsch
it-alto-adige-plantaditsch.summary: Plantaditsch is a Kaltern site for Chardonnay, Schiava and Merlot.
it-alto-adige-plantaditsch.terroir: Moraine and gravel on the slopes above the lake. The official boundary, in Caldaro/Kaltern, lies at about 300 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Chardonnay, Schiava, Merlot.
it-alto-adige-plantaditsch.nerd_note: UGA wines must come entirely from the named site, at yields at least 25 percent below the DOC maximum, with one to five permitted varieties per UGA, and must carry the Consorzio's UGA symbol on the label.
it-alto-adige-plantaditsch.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-plon.name: Plon
it-alto-adige-plon.summary: Tramin-Plon is the official long form of the Plon UGA above Tramin, giving aromatic whites, Gewürztraminer above all.
it-alto-adige-plon.terroir: Calcareous debris and moraine. The official boundary, in Termeno/Tramin, lies at about 300 m (terrain model).
it-alto-adige-plon.nerd_note: Tramin is the village whose name Gewürztraminer carries, and its slopes remain the variety's reference in Italy.
it-alto-adige-plon.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-prazoll.name: Prazöll
it-alto-adige-prazoll.summary: Prazöll is one of the hamlets of the St. Magdalena hill east of Bolzano, the classic zone of Santa Maddalena, where Schiava is often softened with a dash of Lagrein. Pergolas climb the porphyry-and-moraine slope above the city.
it-alto-adige-prazoll.terroir: Morainic sand and gravel over quartz porphyry, south-facing. The official boundary, in Bolzano/Bozen, reaches from about 270 to 860 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Schiava, Lagrein.
it-alto-adige-prazoll.nerd_note: UGA wines must come entirely from the named site, at yields at least 25 percent below the DOC maximum, with one to five permitted varieties per UGA, and must carry the Consorzio's UGA symbol on the label.
it-alto-adige-prazoll.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-punggl.name: Punggl
it-alto-adige-punggl.summary: Punggl is a Margreid site on the valley floor, giving Chardonnay, Pinot Grigio and Merlot.
it-alto-adige-punggl.terroir: Alluvial gravel. The official boundary, in Magrè/Margreid, reaches from about 210 to 500 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Chardonnay, Pinot Grigio, Merlot.
it-alto-adige-punggl.nerd_note: UGA wines must come entirely from the named site, at yields at least 25 percent below the DOC maximum, with one to five permitted varieties per UGA, and must carry the Consorzio's UGA symbol on the label.
it-alto-adige-punggl.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-putznai.name: Putznai
it-alto-adige-putznai.summary: Putznai lies on the border of Tramin and Kaltern, a warm site for Schiava, Lagrein and Cabernet.
it-alto-adige-putznai.terroir: Gravel and moraine. The official boundary, in Termeno/Tramin and Caldaro/Kaltern, lies at about 220 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Schiava, Lagrein, Cabernet.
it-alto-adige-putznai.nerd_note: UGA wines must come entirely from the named site, at yields at least 25 percent below the DOC maximum, with one to five permitted varieties per UGA, and must carry the Consorzio's UGA symbol on the label.
it-alto-adige-putznai.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-rain.name: Rain
it-alto-adige-rain.summary: Rain lies in the middle band of Kurtatsch's slopes, giving Pinot Grigio, Sauvignon and Gewürztraminer.
it-alto-adige-rain.terroir: Calcareous moraine. The official boundary, in Cortaccia/Kurtatsch, reaches from about 350 to 620 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Pinot Grigio, Sauvignon Blanc, Gewürztraminer.
it-alto-adige-rain.nerd_note: Kurtatsch's vineyards climb from about 220 m on the valley floor to over 900 m, so the village can grow Cabernet and Merlot at the bottom and Müller-Thurgau at the top within a few kilometres.
it-alto-adige-rain.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-rentsch.name: Rentsch
it-alto-adige-rentsch.summary: Rentsch lies at the foot of the St. Magdalena hill on Bolzano's eastern edge, giving fragrant, cherry-scented Santa Maddalena and Lagrein. Several family estates of the classic zone have their farmhouses here.
it-alto-adige-rentsch.terroir: Morainic and alluvial soils over porphyry. The official boundary, in Bolzano/Bozen, lies at about 300 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Schiava, Lagrein.
it-alto-adige-rentsch.nerd_note: UGA wines must come entirely from the named site, at yields at least 25 percent below the DOC maximum, with one to five permitted varieties per UGA, and must carry the Consorzio's UGA symbol on the label.
it-alto-adige-rentsch.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-ritten.name: Ritten
it-alto-adige-ritten.grapes: Pinot Bianco, Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Nero
it-alto-adige-ritten.summary: The Ritten UGA covers the vineyards on the lower slopes of the Ritten plateau, the mountain shelf north-east of Bolzano. At altitude the classic reds give way to Pinot Bianco, Chardonnay, Sauvignon and Pinot Nero, crisp and aromatic.
it-alto-adige-ritten.terroir: Porphyry and morainic soils on steep south and south-west slopes, cooled by air from the plateau. The official boundary, in Renon/Ritten, reaches from about 380 to 1050 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Pinot Bianco, Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Nero.
it-alto-adige-ritten.nerd_note: UGA wines must come entirely from the named site, at yields at least 25 percent below the DOC maximum, with one to five permitted varieties per UGA, and must carry the Consorzio's UGA symbol on the label.
it-alto-adige-ritten.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-rosengarten.name: Rosengarten
it-alto-adige-rosengarten.summary: Rosengarten at Algund is a Schiava site on the slopes west of Meran.
it-alto-adige-rosengarten.terroir: Gneiss and moraine. The official boundary, in Lagundo/Algund, reaches from about 300 to 790 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Schiava.
it-alto-adige-rosengarten.nerd_note: UGA wines must come entirely from the named site, at yields at least 25 percent below the DOC maximum, with one to five permitted varieties per UGA, and must carry the Consorzio's UGA symbol on the label.
it-alto-adige-rosengarten.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-rungg.name: Rungg
it-alto-adige-rungg.summary: Rungg is a hamlet on the gentler slopes south of Tramin towards Kurtatsch, a warm site for Gewürztraminer and red varieties.
it-alto-adige-rungg.terroir: Moraine and calcareous gravel. The official boundary, in Termeno/Tramin and Cortaccia/Kurtatsch, reaches from about 230 to 580 m (terrain model).
it-alto-adige-rungg.nerd_note: Tramin is the village whose name Gewürztraminer carries, and its slopes remain the variety's reference in Italy.
it-alto-adige-rungg.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-salurn-pfatten.name: Salurn-Pfatten
it-alto-adige-salurn-pfatten.summary: Salurn-Pfatten lies on the valley floor at Salurn, the southernmost village of Alto Adige near the linguistic border with Trentino, giving Chardonnay and Pinot Grigio.
it-alto-adige-salurn-pfatten.terroir: Alluvial gravel of the Adige plain. The official boundary, in Salorno/Salurn, reaches from about 200 to 300 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Chardonnay, Pinot Grigio.
it-alto-adige-salurn-pfatten.nerd_note: UGA wines must come entirely from the named site, at yields at least 25 percent below the DOC maximum, with one to five permitted varieties per UGA, and must carry the Consorzio's UGA symbol on the label.
it-alto-adige-salurn-pfatten.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-sauders.name: Sauders
it-alto-adige-sauders.summary: Sauders is a Villanders site reserved for Grüner Veltliner, a variety that has found a second home in the Eisacktal.
it-alto-adige-sauders.terroir: Quartz phyllite on steep slopes. The official boundary, in Villandro/Villanders, reaches from about 540 to 840 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Grüner Veltliner.
it-alto-adige-sauders.nerd_note: The Eisacktal is Alto Adige's white-wine valley, with steep terraces up to about 900 m and soils of quartz phyllite, granite and moraine; Cantina Valle Isarco in Klausen and the abbey of Neustift are its anchors.
it-alto-adige-sauders.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-schrambach.name: Schrambach
it-alto-adige-schrambach.summary: Schrambach is a Feldthurns site reserved for Sylvaner, on the sunny east side of the Eisacktal.
it-alto-adige-schrambach.terroir: Quartz phyllite and granite debris. The official boundary, in Velturno/Feldthurns, lies at about 660 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Sylvaner.
it-alto-adige-schrambach.nerd_note: The Eisacktal is Alto Adige's white-wine valley, with steep terraces up to about 900 m and soils of quartz phyllite, granite and moraine; Cantina Valle Isarco in Klausen and the abbey of Neustift are its anchors.
it-alto-adige-schrambach.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-siebeneich.name: Siebeneich
it-alto-adige-siebeneich.grapes: Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Lagrein, Merlot, Cabernet
it-alto-adige-siebeneich.summary: Siebeneich ('seven oaks') lies on the warm valley floor of Terlan towards Bolzano, a site for reds and whites: Chardonnay, Sauvignon, Lagrein, Merlot and Cabernet.
it-alto-adige-siebeneich.terroir: Alluvial and porphyry debris. The official boundary, in Terlano/Terlan, reaches from about 240 to 500 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Lagrein, Merlot, Cabernet.
it-alto-adige-siebeneich.nerd_note: UGA wines must come entirely from the named site, at yields at least 25 percent below the DOC maximum, with one to five permitted varieties per UGA, and must carry the Consorzio's UGA symbol on the label.
it-alto-adige-siebeneich.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-sirmian.name: Sirmian
it-alto-adige-sirmian.summary: Sirmian lies above Nals on the way to Tisens, and is the source of Cantina Nals Margreid's Pinot Bianco Sirmian, one of Alto Adige's reference whites. The UGA allows Pinot Bianco, Chardonnay and Sauvignon.
it-alto-adige-sirmian.terroir: Porphyry and morainic soils on steep slopes up to about 900 m. The official boundary, in Tesimo/Tisens and Nalles/Nals, reaches from about 290 to 900 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Pinot Bianco, Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc.
it-alto-adige-sirmian.nerd_note: UGA wines must come entirely from the named site, at yields at least 25 percent below the DOC maximum, with one to five permitted varieties per UGA, and must carry the Consorzio's UGA symbol on the label.
it-alto-adige-sirmian.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-soll.name: Söll
it-alto-adige-soll.summary: Söll is a hamlet on the slopes above Tramin and the heart of Alto Adige Gewürztraminer. Hofstätter's Kolbenhof and many of Cantina Tramin's top lots, including Nussbaumer, come from these warm, steep pergolas. The wines are intensely aromatic, with rose, lychee and spice, but surprisingly fresh.
it-alto-adige-soll.terroir: Limestone and dolomite debris over moraine on steep south-east-facing pergola slopes. The official boundary, in Termeno/Tramin, reaches from about 270 to 850 m (terrain model).
it-alto-adige-soll.nerd_note: Tramin is the village whose name Gewürztraminer carries, and its slopes remain the variety's reference in Italy.
it-alto-adige-soll.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-st-anna.name: St. Anna
it-alto-adige-st-anna.grapes: Pinot Bianco, Chardonnay, Pinot Grigio, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Nero
it-alto-adige-st-anna.summary: St. Anna lies on the Eppan slopes near the lakes, giving Pinot Bianco, Chardonnay, Pinot Grigio, Sauvignon and Pinot Nero.
it-alto-adige-st-anna.terroir: Morainic soils. The official boundary, in Appiano/Eppan, lies at about 410 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Pinot Bianco, Chardonnay, Pinot Grigio, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Nero.
it-alto-adige-st-anna.nerd_note: UGA wines must come entirely from the named site, at yields at least 25 percent below the DOC maximum, with one to five permitted varieties per UGA, and must carry the Consorzio's UGA symbol on the label.
it-alto-adige-st-anna.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-st-jacob.name: St. Jacob
it-alto-adige-st-jacob.summary: St. Jacob takes its name from the Romanesque church of St. Jakob in Kastelaz above Tramin, whose frescoes of monsters are famous. Elena Walch's Kastelaz Gewürztraminer grows on the steep terraces beneath it.
it-alto-adige-st-jacob.terroir: Steep limestone and dolomite debris facing south-east. The official boundary, in Termeno/Tramin, lies at about 360 m (terrain model).
it-alto-adige-st-jacob.nerd_note: Tramin is the village whose name Gewürztraminer carries, and its slopes remain the variety's reference in Italy.
it-alto-adige-st-jacob.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-st-josef.name: St. Josef
it-alto-adige-st-josef.summary: St. Josef am See lies on the shore of the Kalterer See (Lago di Caldaro), the warmest corner of the Überetsch, where Schiava, Lagrein, Merlot and Cabernet ripen easily. The lake gave its name to Kalterersee, once Austria-Hungary's favourite red; Manincor's estate stands here.
it-alto-adige-st-josef.terroir: Morainic gravel and lake sediments on slopes around the water, which stores heat. The official boundary, in Caldaro/Kaltern, reaches from about 220 to 450 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Schiava, Lagrein, Merlot, Cabernet.
it-alto-adige-st-josef.nerd_note: UGA wines must come entirely from the named site, at yields at least 25 percent below the DOC maximum, with one to five permitted varieties per UGA, and must carry the Consorzio's UGA symbol on the label.
it-alto-adige-st-josef.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-st-justina.name: St. Justina
it-alto-adige-st-justina.summary: St. Justina is a hamlet on the porphyry slopes above Bolzano, in the heart of the Santa Maddalena classico zone, giving perfumed Schiava and firm Lagrein. Heinrich Plattner's Waldgries estate is based here.
it-alto-adige-st-justina.terroir: Weathered quartz porphyry and moraine on steep pergola terraces. The official boundary, in Bolzano/Bozen, reaches from about 300 to 720 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Schiava, Lagrein.
it-alto-adige-st-justina.nerd_note: UGA wines must come entirely from the named site, at yields at least 25 percent below the DOC maximum, with one to five permitted varieties per UGA, and must carry the Consorzio's UGA symbol on the label.
it-alto-adige-st-justina.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-st-nikolaus.name: St. Nikolaus
it-alto-adige-st-nikolaus.grapes: Pinot Bianco, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Nero
it-alto-adige-st-nikolaus.summary: St. Nikolaus is a hamlet high above Kaltern, a cool site where Pinot Bianco, Sauvignon and Pinot Nero keep their freshness.
it-alto-adige-st-nikolaus.terroir: Calcareous debris from the Mendola range over moraine. The official boundary, in Caldaro/Kaltern, reaches from about 390 to 840 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Pinot Bianco, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Nero.
it-alto-adige-st-nikolaus.nerd_note: UGA wines must come entirely from the named site, at yields at least 25 percent below the DOC maximum, with one to five permitted varieties per UGA, and must carry the Consorzio's UGA symbol on the label.
it-alto-adige-st-nikolaus.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-st-peter.name: St. Peter
it-alto-adige-st-peter.summary: St. Peter lies on the slopes north of Bolzano near the entrance to the Sarntal, giving Schiava, Lagrein and a little Sauvignon from steep pergola vineyards.
it-alto-adige-st-peter.terroir: Porphyry rock and morainic debris on south-facing slopes. The official boundary, in Bolzano/Bozen, lies at about 330 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Sauvignon Blanc, Schiava, Lagrein.
it-alto-adige-st-peter.nerd_note: UGA wines must come entirely from the named site, at yields at least 25 percent below the DOC maximum, with one to five permitted varieties per UGA, and must carry the Consorzio's UGA symbol on the label.
it-alto-adige-st-peter.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-steinacker.name: Steinacker
it-alto-adige-steinacker.summary: Steinacker ('stone field') lies on the warm valley floor below Tramin, giving Chardonnay, Lagrein and Merlot.
it-alto-adige-steinacker.terroir: Stony alluvial gravel. The official boundary, in Termeno/Tramin, reaches from about 210 to 360 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Chardonnay, Lagrein, Merlot.
it-alto-adige-steinacker.nerd_note: UGA wines must come entirely from the named site, at yields at least 25 percent below the DOC maximum, with one to five permitted varieties per UGA, and must carry the Consorzio's UGA symbol on the label.
it-alto-adige-steinacker.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-terlano.name: Terlano
it-alto-adige-terlano.grapes: Pinot Bianco, Chardonnay, Sauvignon, Pinot Grigio, Riesling, Müller-Thurgau
it-alto-adige-terlano.summary: Terlano is the most famous white-wine village of Alto Adige, between Bolzano and Merano. Its cooperative, the Cantina Terlano (1893), holds back wines for 10 to 30 years before release, proving that Pinot Bianco and Sauvignon from porphyry soils can age like great Burgundy. Terlaner Classico comes from the steep porphyry slopes above the village.
it-alto-adige-terlano.terroir: Red quartz porphyry, sandy and mineral, on south-facing slopes up to about 900 m.
it-alto-adige-terlano.nerd_note: Cantina Terlano's 'Rarity' series releases wines that have spent more than a decade on fine lees in steel tanks.

it-alto-adige-terlano-classico.name: Alto Adige Terlano classico
it-alto-adige-terlano-classico.summary: The classico core of the Terlano subzone, covering the porphyry slopes of Terlan, Nals and Andrian, the historic home of Terlaner white blends, Pinot Bianco and Sauvignon renowned for their longevity.
it-alto-adige-terlano-classico.terroir: Quartz porphyry with sandy topsoil on steep south-facing slopes. The official boundary, in Terlano/Terlan, Nalles/Nals and Andriano/Andrian, reaches from about 240 to 1780 m (terrain model).

it-alto-adige-tirol.name: Tirol
it-alto-adige-tirol.grapes: Pinot Bianco, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Nero
it-alto-adige-tirol.summary: Tirol is the village above Meran that gave its name to the whole Tyrol through its castle, Schloss Tirol. Its UGA allows Pinot Bianco, Sauvignon and Pinot Nero.
it-alto-adige-tirol.terroir: Gneiss, mica schist and moraine on steep slopes. The official boundary, in Tirolo/Tirol, reaches from about 320 to 750 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Pinot Bianco, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Nero.
it-alto-adige-tirol.nerd_note: UGA wines must come entirely from the named site, at yields at least 25 percent below the DOC maximum, with one to five permitted varieties per UGA, and must carry the Consorzio's UGA symbol on the label.
it-alto-adige-tirol.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-unterfennberg-hofstatt.name: Unterfennberg-Hofstatt
it-alto-adige-unterfennberg-hofstatt.summary: Unterfennberg-Hofstatt lies on the Fennberg, a mountain terrace at nearly 1,000 m above Margreid, and is reserved for Müller-Thurgau. Tiefenbrunner's Feldmarschall von Fenner, one of Italy's most famous Müller-Thurgaus, grows on this plateau.
it-alto-adige-unterfennberg-hofstatt.terroir: Limestone and dolomite on a high, cool terrace with large day-night temperature swings. The official boundary, in Magrè/Margreid, lies at about 970 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Müller-Thurgau.
it-alto-adige-unterfennberg-hofstatt.nerd_note: It is one of the highest vineyard UGAs of Alto Adige.
it-alto-adige-unterfennberg-hofstatt.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-val-venosta.name: Val Venosta
it-alto-adige-val-venosta.grapes: Riesling, Pinot Bianco, Pinot Nero, Müller-Thurgau, Kerner, Gewürztraminer
it-alto-adige-val-venosta.summary: The dry, high Vinschgau west of Merano, famous for apples, has a small number of vineyards at 500 to 900 m that make taut Riesling and Pinot Noir. Castel Juval, owned by the mountaineer Reinhold Messner, and Falkenstein (Franz Pratzner) are its best-known estates.
it-alto-adige-val-venosta.terroir: Gneiss and schist on the sunny northern side of a rain-shadow valley with very low rainfall.
it-alto-adige-val-venosta.nerd_note: Reinhold Messner, the first man to climb all 14 eight-thousanders, owns Castel Juval and its vineyard.

it-alto-adige-valle-isarco.name: Valle Isarco
it-alto-adige-valle-isarco.grapes: Sylvaner, Kerner, Müller-Thurgau, Grüner Veltliner, Riesling, Gewürztraminer, Pinot Grigio, Zweigelt
it-alto-adige-valle-isarco.summary: The Isarco (Eisack) valley north of Bolzano toward Bressanone and the Brenner Pass is Italy's northernmost wine zone, a land of steep terraces, monasteries and crisp, aromatic whites. Kerner, Sylvaner and Grüner Veltliner are specialities; Bressanone (Brixner) and Klausen are sub-areas. The Abbazia di Novacella (founded 1142) and the Cantina Valle Isarco co-op dominate, with growers like Kuenhof (Peter Pliger), Manni Nössing and Köfererhof.
it-alto-adige-valle-isarco.terroir: Schist, quartz-phyllite and glacial moraine at 500 to 900 m; cool, with strong day-night swings.
it-alto-adige-valle-isarco.nerd_note: Kerner, a Schiava x Riesling cross bred in Württemberg in 1929, found its best home in Italy here.

it-alto-adige-valle-isarco-klausner-leit.name: Alto Adige Valle Isarco Klausner Leitacher
it-alto-adige-valle-isarco-klausner-leit.summary: Klausner Leitacher is a traditional red-wine name within the Valle Isarco subzone, a Schiava-based red from the slopes around Klausen, the only red wine with its own name in this white-wine valley.
it-alto-adige-valle-isarco-klausner-leit.terroir: Quartz phyllite and moraine on the slopes around Klausen. The official boundary, in Chiusa/Klausen, Barbiano/Barbian, Velturno/Feldthurns and Villandro/Villanders, reaches from about 510 to 1060 m (terrain model).

it-alto-adige-vetzaner.name: Vetzaner
it-alto-adige-vetzaner.summary: Vetzan, near Schlanders, is the westernmost UGA of Alto Adige, at around 650 to 900 m in the upper Vinschgau. It gives taut Pinot Bianco, Riesling and Pinot Nero.
it-alto-adige-vetzaner.terroir: Gneiss and mica schist with sandy moraine, very dry and sunny. The official boundary, in Silandro/Schlanders, reaches from about 670 to 890 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Pinot Bianco, Riesling, Pinot Nero.
it-alto-adige-vetzaner.nerd_note: The Vinschgau is one of the driest valleys of the Alps, with under 500 mm of rain a year in places; growers once irrigated with the 'Waale', medieval channels cut along the slopes.
it-alto-adige-vetzaner.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-vorberg.name: Vorberg
it-alto-adige-vorberg.summary: Vorberg rises above Terlan towards Mölten and is the source of Cantina Terlano's Pinot Bianco Vorberg Riserva, a famously long-lived white. Terlan's whites are known for their ability to age decades, a quality the cooperative proves with its 'Rarity' releases.
it-alto-adige-vorberg.terroir: Quartz porphyry (Bozen volcanic rock) with sandy topsoil on steep south-facing slopes. The official boundary, in Terlano/Terlan and Meltina/Mölten, reaches from about 250 to 1030 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Pinot Bianco, Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc.
it-alto-adige-vorberg.nerd_note: Terlano keeps old vintages on the lees in steel for ten years or more before release as 'Rarity'.
it-alto-adige-vorberg.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-wadleith.name: Wadleith
it-alto-adige-wadleith.grapes: Chardonnay, Pinot Grigio, Sauvignon Blanc, Lagrein, Cabernet
it-alto-adige-wadleith.summary: Wadleith lies on the warm slopes of Kaltern towards the lake, giving Chardonnay, Pinot Grigio, Sauvignon, Lagrein and Cabernet.
it-alto-adige-wadleith.terroir: Morainic gravel. The official boundary, in Caldaro/Kaltern, lies at about 290 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Chardonnay, Pinot Grigio, Sauvignon Blanc, Lagrein, Cabernet.
it-alto-adige-wadleith.nerd_note: UGA wines must come entirely from the named site, at yields at least 25 percent below the DOC maximum, with one to five permitted varieties per UGA, and must carry the Consorzio's UGA symbol on the label.
it-alto-adige-wadleith.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-barbaresco-albesani.name: Albesani
it-barbaresco-albesani.summary:
A large MGA north-west of Neive village on south-facing slopes. It contains the vineyard of Santo Stefano, owned by Castello di Neive and made famous by Bruno Giacosa, who bought its grapes for decades; Giacosa's Santo Stefano Riservas of the 1970s and 1980s are among the legendary Barbarescos.

Castello di Neive bottles Albesani Santo Stefano, and Piero Busso and Cantina del Pino also farm here. The wines are rich and supple, with Neive's ripe fruit and a firm finish.
it-barbaresco-albesani.terroir: South-facing slopes of Tortonian marl north-west of Neive, close to the Barbaresco border. On the official MGA map the digitised outline covers about 74 ha at roughly 155 to 250 m. (Approximate outline; total area, not vines; elevations from the Copernicus DEM.)
it-barbaresco-albesani.classification: MGA (menzione geografica aggiuntiva) of Barbaresco DOCG: one of the 66 named vineyard areas written into the disciplinare in 2007. The name may follow "Barbaresco" on the label only if all the grapes come from inside it; it is a place name, not a quality rank.

it-barbaresco-asili.name: Asili
it-barbaresco-asili.summary:
Asili is the most perfumed of the great Barbaresco crus: about 14 ha of slope facing south-west at roughly 200 to 280 m, a short walk south of Barbaresco village, between Martinenga and Secondine. Silty loam, clay and sand over Tortonian marl give wines of violets, rose and red cherry with silky, fine-grained tannin, closer to a grand Burgundy in texture than to the muscular end of Nebbiolo, yet they age for decades.

Bruno Giacosa bought vines here in 1996 and his red-label Asili Riserva is one of the great wines of Piedmont. Ceretto's Bricco Asili, Produttori del Barbaresco's Asili Riserva, Ca' del Baio, Cascina Luisin, Michele Chiarlo and Roagna are classics, so Asili shows the same slope through very different cellars.
it-barbaresco-asili.terroir: South-west-facing slope of silty loam, clay and sand over Tortonian Sant'Agata marl. On the official MGA map the digitised outline covers about 15 ha at roughly 210 to 280 m, facing broadly south-west. (Approximate outline; total area, not vines; elevations from the Copernicus DEM.)
it-barbaresco-asili.nerd_note: Produttori del Barbaresco, the village cooperative founded in 1958, makes its nine single-MGA Riservas, Asili among them, only in good years.
it-barbaresco-asili.classification: MGA (menzione geografica aggiuntiva) of Barbaresco DOCG: one of the 66 named vineyard areas written into the disciplinare in 2007. The name may follow "Barbaresco" on the label only if all the grapes come from inside it; it is a place name, not a quality rank.

it-barbaresco-bric-micca.name: Bric Micca
it-barbaresco-bric-micca.summary: A large, high MGA in the south-east of Neive near Bricco di Neive, at about 240 to 370 m, at the eastern edge of the zone.
it-barbaresco-bric-micca.terroir: On the official MGA map the digitised outline covers about 103 ha at roughly 240 to 365 m, facing broadly north. (Approximate outline; total area, not vines; elevations from the Copernicus DEM.)
it-barbaresco-bric-micca.classification: MGA (menzione geografica aggiuntiva) of Barbaresco DOCG: one of the 66 named vineyard areas written into the disciplinare in 2007. it-barbaresco-bricco-di-neive.name: Bricco di Neive

it-barbaresco-bricco-di-treiso.terroir: On the official MGA map the digitised outline covers about 30 ha at roughly 315 to 400 m, facing broadly west. (Approximate outline; total area, not vines; elevations from the Copernicus DEM.)

it-barbaresco-ca-grossa.terroir: On the official MGA map the digitised outline covers about 40 ha at roughly 185 to 280 m, facing north-east to east. (Approximate outline; total area, not vines; elevations from the Copernicus DEM.)

it-barbaresco-canova.terroir: On the official MGA map the digitised outline covers about 165 ha at roughly 220 to 355 m, facing broadly north-north-east. (Approximate outline; total area, not vines; elevations from the Copernicus DEM.)

it-barbaresco-cars.name: Cars

it-barbaresco-cars.terroir: On the official MGA map the digitised outline covers about 28 ha at roughly 175 to 260 m, facing north to north-east. (Approximate outline; total area, not vines; elevations from the Copernicus DEM.)
it-barbaresco-cars.classification: MGA (menzione geografica aggiuntiva) of Barbaresco DOCG: one of the 66 named vineyard areas written into the disciplinare in 2007. The name may follow "Barbaresco" on the label only if all the grapes come from inside it; it is a place name, not a quality rank.

it-barbaresco-casot.name: Casot

it-barbaresco-casot.terroir: On the official MGA map the digitised outline covers about 18 ha at roughly 245 to 355 m, mostly south-west-facing. (Approximate outline; total area, not vines; elevations from the Copernicus DEM.)
it-barbaresco-casot.classification: MGA (menzione geografica aggiuntiva) of Barbaresco DOCG: one of the 66 named vineyard areas written into the disciplinare in 2007. The name may follow "Barbaresco" on the label only if all the grapes come from inside it; it is a place name, not a quality rank.

it-barbaresco-castellizzano.name: Castellizzano

it-barbaresco-cavanna.classification: MGA (menzione geografica aggiuntiva) of Barbaresco DOCG: one of the 66 named vineyard areas written into the disciplinare in 2007. The name may follow "Barbaresco" on the label only if all the grapes come from inside it; it is a place name, not a quality rank.

it-barbaresco-cotta.terroir: On the official MGA map the digitised outline covers about 87 ha at roughly 195 to 330 m, facing broadly north. (Approximate outline; total area, not vines; elevations from the Copernicus DEM.)

it-barbaresco-curra.name: Currà
it-barbaresco-curra.summary: A small, steep site in Neive near the Barbaresco border, next to Gallina, on sandy marl. Sottimano and Bruno Rocca bottle Currà as an intense, spicy single-vineyard Barbaresco.
it-barbaresco-curra.terroir: On the official MGA map the digitised outline covers about 24 ha at roughly 225 to 320 m, facing north-west to west. (Approximate outline; total area, not vines; elevations from the Copernicus DEM.)
it-barbaresco-curra.classification: MGA (menzione geografica aggiuntiva) of Barbaresco DOCG: one of the 66 named vineyard areas written into the disciplinare in 2007. The name may follow "Barbaresco" on the label only if all the grapes come from inside it; it is a place name, not a quality rank.

it-barbaresco-faset.name: Faset

it-barbaresco-faset.classification: MGA (menzione geografica aggiuntiva) of Barbaresco DOCG: one of the 66 named vineyard areas written into the disciplinare in 2007. The name may follow "Barbaresco" on the label only if all the grapes come from inside it; it is a place name, not a quality rank.

it-barbaresco-fausoni.name: Fausoni

it-barbaresco-gaia-principe.terroir: On the official MGA map the digitised outline covers about 73 ha at roughly 180 to 275 m, facing broadly north-west. (Approximate outline; total area, not vines; elevations from the Copernicus DEM.)

it-barbaresco-gallina.name: Gallina
it-barbaresco-gallina.summary:
A south and south-west-facing hill north-west of Neive village toward Barbaresco, giving rich, ripe wines with dark fruit and a firm structure. La Spinetta's Gallina, Ugo Lequio's Gallina and Oddero's Gallina are the best known, and Piero Busso farms here.

Gallina is one of the Neive sites that reached a wide audience in the 1990s through La Spinetta's dark, polished bottlings, while Ugo Lequio's, aged in large casks, shows its classic side.
it-barbaresco-gallina.terroir: Calcareous marl with a sandy component, on a hill that collects heat from the south and south-west. On the official MGA map the digitised outline covers about 55 ha at roughly 175 to 255 m, facing broadly west-south-west. (Approximate outline; total area, not vines; elevations from the Copernicus DEM.)

it-barbaresco-martinenga.name: Martinenga
it-barbaresco-martinenga.summary:
A natural amphitheatre of about 12 ha between Asili and Rabajà, facing south and south-west, and a monopole of the Marchesi di Grésy, whose family has owned it since the eighteenth century. Alberto di Grésy began bottling it in 1973, among the early single-vineyard Barbarescos.

The two best parcels are bottled separately in good years: Camp Gros is the fuller and longer-lived, Gaiun the more fragrant. The straight Martinenga combines both sides of its neighbours: Asili's perfume and Rabajà's grip.
it-barbaresco-martinenga.terroir: Calcareous Tortonian marl with sand and clay, in a sheltered bowl facing south and south-west. On the official MGA map the digitised outline covers about 18 ha at roughly 190 to 265 m, mostly south-west-facing. (Approximate outline; total area, not vines; elevations from the Copernicus DEM.)
it-barbaresco-martinenga.classification: MGA (menzione geografica aggiuntiva) of Barbaresco DOCG: one of the 66 named vineyard areas written into the disciplinare in 2007. it-barbaresco-meruzzano.summary: The southernmost part of the Barbaresco zone around the hamlet of Meruzzano, high and cool at up to about 490 m.
it-barbaresco-meruzzano.terroir: On the official MGA map the digitised outline covers about 162 ha at roughly 270 to 485 m, mostly west-facing. (Approximate outline; total area, not vines; elevations from the Copernicus DEM.)

it-barbaresco-montaribaldi.name: Montaribaldi

it-barbaresco-montaribaldi.terroir: On the official MGA map the digitised outline covers about 16 ha at roughly 180 to 310 m, facing south-west to south. (Approximate outline; total area, not vines; elevations from the Copernicus DEM.)

it-barbaresco-montefico.name: Montefico
it-barbaresco-montefico.summary:
North-east of Barbaresco village beside Montestefano, on white, calcareous marl. Montefico is tight, mineral and deeply structured, with a stony, austere edge in youth and great length.

Roagna's Montefico Vecchie Viti, from vines more than 50 years old and given very long macerations, and the Produttori del Barbaresco Montefico Riserva are the benchmarks; La Cà Növa also bottles it.
it-barbaresco-montefico.terroir: White, calcium-rich marl on low, sheltered slopes beside Montestefano; early to ripen, yet the soil keeps the wine tight. On the official MGA map the digitised outline covers about 8.1 ha at roughly 175 to 245 m, facing east to south-east. (Approximate outline; total area, not vines; elevations from the Copernicus DEM.)
it-barbaresco-montefico.nerd_note: Montefico and Montestefano, side by side, are the two most structured crus of the Barbaresco commune.
it-barbaresco-montefico.classification: MGA (menzione geografica aggiuntiva) of Barbaresco DOCG: one of the 66 named vineyard areas written into the disciplinare in 2007. it-barbaresco-montersino.village: Alba (San Rocco Seno d'Elvio) and Treiso
it-barbaresco-montersino.summary: A large MGA on the border of Treiso and the San Rocco Seno d'Elvio part of Alba, the only part of the city's territory inside the Barbaresco zone, on steep slopes facing south-west.
it-barbaresco-montersino.terroir: On the official MGA map the digitised outline covers about 84 ha at roughly 225 to 390 m, facing broadly west-south-west. (Approximate outline; total area, not vines; elevations from the Copernicus DEM.)

it-barbaresco-montestefano.name: Montestefano
it-barbaresco-montestefano.summary:
A steep slope east of Barbaresco village facing south and south-east, with a high calcium content, which gives the most structured and tannic wines of the commune, slow to open and very long-lived.

Prunotto released the first labelled Montestefano in 1961, among the earliest single-vineyard bottlings of the Langhe. Produttori del Barbaresco's Montestefano Riserva and Serafino Rivella's tiny production are references; La Cà Növa and Luigi Giordano also bottle it.
it-barbaresco-montestefano.terroir: Steep slopes facing south and south-east, of calcium-rich Sant'Agata marl, a little higher and more exposed than the crus by the river. On the official MGA map the digitised outline covers about 10 ha at roughly 175 to 260 m, facing broadly south-east. (Approximate outline; total area, not vines; elevations from the Copernicus DEM.)

it-barbaresco-muncagota.summary: South of Barbaresco village near Rabajà, on steep slopes. Produttori del Barbaresco bottles a Muncagota Riserva in good years, one of its nine single-MGA wines.
it-barbaresco-muncagota.terroir: On the official MGA map the digitised outline covers about 8.4 ha at roughly 240 to 295 m, mostly east-facing. (Approximate outline; total area, not vines; elevations from the Copernicus DEM.)

it-barbaresco-nervo.name: Nervo
it-barbaresco-nervo.summary: A high slope west of Treiso facing south and south-west, known for fresh, sinewy wines.
it-barbaresco-nervo.terroir: On the official MGA map the digitised outline covers about 22 ha at roughly 230 to 340 m, facing south to south-west. (Approximate outline; total area, not vines; elevations from the Copernicus DEM.)

it-barbaresco-ovello.name: Ovello
it-barbaresco-ovello.summary:
A large MGA north-east of Barbaresco village on the hill above the Tanaro, with slopes facing several ways, cooler and later-ripening than the crus south of the village. Ovello wines are firm, fresh and long, with red fruit, tobacco and a savoury, slightly austere finish.

Produttori del Barbaresco's Ovello Riserva and Cantina del Pino's Ovello are classics; Cascina Morassino and Rocca Albino also bottle it.
it-barbaresco-ovello.terroir: The hill north-east of the village faces the Tanaro on several sides; breezes off the river and heavier soils make it one of the later-ripening sites of Barbaresco. On the official MGA map the digitised outline covers about 76 ha at roughly 165 to 275 m. (Approximate outline; total area, not vines; elevations from the Copernicus DEM.)
it-barbaresco-ovello.nerd_note: Ovello is one of the nine Produttori del Barbaresco Riservas, and often the most austere of them in youth.
it-barbaresco-ovello.classification: MGA (menzione geografica aggiuntiva) of Barbaresco DOCG: one of the 66 named vineyard areas written into the disciplinare in 2007. The name may follow "Barbaresco" on the label only if all the grapes come from inside it; it is a place name, not a quality rank.

it-barbaresco-paje.name: Pajè
it-barbaresco-paje.summary:
A small slope just south-west of Barbaresco village. Roagna's Pajè is one of the great old-school Barbarescos, fermented for weeks and aged for years in large casks, and Produttori del Barbaresco makes a Pajè Riserva; Secondo Pasquero Elia also bottles it.

Pajè sits close to the Tanaro, and its calcareous marl gives a firm, savoury wine with more grip than its size and position suggest.
it-barbaresco-paje.terroir: On the official MGA map the digitised outline covers about 7.3 ha at roughly 215 to 265 m, facing west to south-west. (Approximate outline; total area, not vines; elevations from the Copernicus DEM.)
it-barbaresco-paje.nerd_note: Pajè is one of the nine MGAs that Produttori del Barbaresco bottles separately as a Riserva.
it-barbaresco-paje.classification: MGA (menzione geografica aggiuntiva) of Barbaresco DOCG: one of the 66 named vineyard areas written into the disciplinare in 2007. The name may follow "Barbaresco" on the label only if all the grapes come from inside it; it is a place name, not a quality rank.

it-barbaresco-pajore.name: Pajorè
it-barbaresco-pajore.summary:
Treiso's most historic cru, on the border with Barbaresco north-west of the village, facing south-west. Pajorè was famous in the nineteenth century, when its grapes fetched premium prices.

Sottimano and Rizzi have restored its reputation: Sottimano's Pajorè is perfumed, mineral and fine, and Rizzi's shows the cooler, sinewy side of Treiso.
it-barbaresco-pajore.terroir: Calcareous marl with sand on the Treiso side of the Barbaresco border, higher than the crus by Barbaresco village, which keeps the wines taut. On the official MGA map the digitised outline covers about 42 ha at roughly 195 to 325 m, mostly south-west-facing. (Approximate outline; total area, not vines; elevations from the Copernicus DEM.)
it-barbaresco-pajore.nerd_note: Treiso is the highest of the Barbaresco communes, and its wines are usually the most delicate and fragrant of the zone.
it-barbaresco-pajore.classification: MGA (menzione geografica aggiuntiva) of Barbaresco DOCG: one of the 66 named vineyard areas written into the disciplinare in 2007. The name may follow "Barbaresco" on the label only if all the grapes come from inside it; it is a place name, not a quality rank.

it-barbaresco-pora.name: Pora
it-barbaresco-pora.summary:
South-west of Barbaresco village toward the Tanaro, facing south-west at about 170 to 230 m, one of the lower crus of the commune. Pora gives a lighter, fragrant style, quick to charm, with red berries and fine tannin.

Produttori del Barbaresco bottles a Pora Riserva and Ca' del Baio a Pora; Musso also farms here.
it-barbaresco-pora.terroir: Low, warm slopes close to the Tanaro on calcareous marl with sand; among the earliest-ripening sites of the commune. On the official MGA map the digitised outline covers about 23 ha at roughly 165 to 230 m, mostly south-west-facing. (Approximate outline; total area, not vines; elevations from the Copernicus DEM.)
it-barbaresco-pora.nerd_note: Like Asili and Pajè, Pora is one of the nine single-MGA Riservas of Produttori del Barbaresco, released only in good years.
it-barbaresco-pora.classification: MGA (menzione geografica aggiuntiva) of Barbaresco DOCG: one of the 66 named vineyard areas written into the disciplinare in 2007. The name may follow "Barbaresco" on the label only if all the grapes come from inside it; it is a place name, not a quality rank.

it-barbaresco-rabaja.name: Rabajà
it-barbaresco-rabaja.summary:
Rabajà lies south of Asili and Martinenga, about 15 to 20 ha facing south and south-west at roughly 250 to 310 m, on limestone-rich marl with sand and clay. It gives a fuller, more muscular Barbaresco than Asili, with black cherry, liquorice and spice and firm, ripe tannin.

Bruno Rocca's winery sits in Rabajà and his Rabajà is a benchmark of the modern style; Produttori del Barbaresco's Rabajà Riserva, Giuseppe Cortese (a traditional reference), Castello di Verduno and Cascina Luisin also bottle it.
it-barbaresco-rabaja.terroir: Limestone-rich Sant'Agata marl with sand and clay, a little higher than Asili. On the official MGA map the digitised outline covers about 16 ha at roughly 250 to 310 m, mostly south-west-facing. (Approximate outline; total area, not vines; elevations from the Copernicus DEM.)

it-barbaresco-rabaja-bas.terroir: On the official MGA map the digitised outline lies at roughly 270 to 290 m, mostly west-facing. (Approximate outline; total area, not vines; elevations from the Copernicus DEM.)

it-barbaresco-rio-sordo.name: Rio Sordo
it-barbaresco-rio-sordo.summary:
South of the village beyond Rabajà, on the slope down to the 'silent stream' (*rio sordo*) toward Treiso, with sandier soils. Rio Sordo wines are aromatic and supple, with a softer frame than Rabajà next door.

Produttori del Barbaresco makes a Rio Sordo Riserva, and Cascina Bruciata, Brovia and Musso bottle it.
it-barbaresco-rio-sordo.terroir: Sandier marl than Rabajà, on slopes falling toward the stream that gives the site its name; the sand lightens the tannin and lifts the aromatics. On the official MGA map the digitised outline covers about 25 ha at roughly 195 to 310 m. (Approximate outline; total area, not vines; elevations from the Copernicus DEM.)
it-barbaresco-rio-sordo.nerd_note: Rio Sordo is one of the nine MGAs that Produttori del Barbaresco bottles separately as a Riserva, only in good years.
it-barbaresco-rio-sordo.classification: MGA (menzione geografica aggiuntiva) of Barbaresco DOCG: one of the 66 named vineyard areas written into the disciplinare in 2007. The name may follow "Barbaresco" on the label only if all the grapes come from inside it; it is a place name, not a quality rank.

it-barbaresco-secondine.name: Secondine
it-barbaresco-secondine.summary:
Between Barbaresco village and Asili, facing south-west. It is the source of Gaja's Sorì San Lorenzo, a parcel the Gajas bought in 1964 and named after the patron saint of Alba's cathedral, whose chapter once owned it. With Sorì Tildin and Costa Russi it was one of the three single-vineyard wines that made Angelo Gaja's name from the late 1960s and 1970s.

Gaja labelled the three as Langhe Nebbiolo for years because they included a little Barbera, then returned them to Barbaresco DOCG as pure Nebbiolo in the 2010s. Ada Nada also farms in Secondine.

it-barbaresco-serraboella.name: Serraboella

South-east of Neive village toward Bricco di Neive, facing west. Fratelli Cigliuti and Paitin (whose Sorì Paitin lies here) are the reference estates; Paitin claims a Barbaresco bottled under its own name in 1893.

Serraboella's high, ventilated slopes give perfumed, firm and long-lived Barbaresco.
it-barbaresco-serraboella.terroir: Calcareous Tortonian marl on high, wind-exposed slopes in the south-east of Neive, close to Bricco di Neive; the altitude keeps acidity and aromatics fresh, and the wines usually need a few years in bottle to open. On the official MGA map the digitised outline covers about 56 ha at roughly 260 to 315 m, facing broadly west. (Approximate outline; total area, not vines; elevations from the Copernicus DEM.)

it-barbaresco-starderi.name: Starderi
it-barbaresco-starderi.summary:

It is the source of La Spinetta's Starderi, one of the Rivetti family's three single-vineyard Barbarescos launched in the 1990s alongside Gallina and Valeirano, which made the estate a symbol of modern, barrique-aged Barbaresco.

Starderi gives a darker, denser wine than most of Neive, with ripe black cherry and firm tannin.
it-barbaresco-starderi.terroir: Calcareous Tortonian marl on open slopes facing south-west and west, north of Neive village. On the official MGA map the digitised outline covers about 98 ha at roughly 185 to 260 m, facing broadly west. (Approximate outline; total area, not vines; elevations from the Copernicus DEM.)
it-barbaresco-starderi.nerd_note: La Spinetta began as a Moscato estate; the Rivetti family's single-vineyard Barbarescos arrived in the mid-1990s and changed the estate's image.

it-barbera-d-asti-colli-astiani.name: Colli Astiani
it-barbera-d-asti-colli-astiani.village: Asti (Montemarzo, San Marzanotto), Isola d'Asti, Mongardino, Vigliano d'Asti, Montegrosso d'Asti, Montaldo Scarampi, Rocca d'Arazzo, Azzano d'Asti
it-barbera-d-asti-colli-astiani.summary: The hills just south of Asti, from the city's own frazioni of Montemarzo and San Marzanotto through Mongardino, Vigliano, Montegrosso, Montaldo Scarampi, Rocca d'Arazzo and Azzano, plus the left side of Isola d'Asti; also labelled 'Astiano'. The rules mirror Tinella's: 90% Barbera, 7 t/ha, two years of ageing from 1 October with six months in wood and six in bottle, south-facing hillsides only.
it-barbera-d-asti-colli-astiani.terroir: Clayey-sandy marl and sandstone hills south of Asti and the Tanaro, about 150 to 350 m.
it-barbera-d-asti-colli-astiani.nerd_note: When Nizza left to become its own DOCG, Tinella and Colli Astiani remained as Barbera d'Asti's only subzones.
it-barbera-d-asti-colli-astiani.classification: Sottozona of Barbera d'Asti DOCG, usable only for Barbera d'Asti Superiore: at least 90% Barbera, 7 t/ha (49 hl/ha), 12.5% potential alcohol, Guyot-trained vines on sunny hillsides facing south-east to south-west, and 24 months of ageing from 1 October after the harvest, with at least six in wood and six in bottle. The vintage is compulsory and only cork closures are allowed.

it-barbera-d-asti-tinella.name: Tinella
it-barbera-d-asti-tinella.village: Costigliole d'Asti, Calosso, Castagnole delle Lanze, Coazzolo, Isola d'Asti
it-barbera-d-asti-tinella.summary: Named after the Tinella stream, this subzone covers the hills of Costigliole d'Asti, Calosso, Castagnole delle Lanze and Coazzolo, plus the part of Isola d'Asti right of the Asti-Montegrosso road, on the border with the Langhe. Its marly-sandy clays and layered sandstones give Barbera of depth and freshness; the rules demand Guyot-trained vines on sunny slopes, 7 t/ha and two years of ageing with six months in wood and six in bottle.
it-barbera-d-asti-tinella.terroir: South-west to south-east facing hills of clayey-sandy marl and stratified sandstone, about 200 to 400 m, between the Tanaro and the Langhe.
it-barbera-d-asti-tinella.nerd_note: Calosso, inside Tinella, is the home of Gamba di Pernice, a rare local red named for the partridge-red colour of its stalks.
it-barbera-d-asti-tinella.classification: Sottozona of Barbera d'Asti DOCG, usable only for Barbera d'Asti Superiore: at least 90% Barbera, 7 t/ha (49 hl/ha), 12.5% potential alcohol, Guyot-trained vines on sunny hillsides facing south-east to south-west, and 24 months of ageing from 1 October after the harvest, with at least six in wood and six in bottle. The vintage is compulsory and only cork closures are allowed.

it-barolo-arborina.name: Arborina
it-barolo-arborina.summary:
A gentle, south-east-facing slope north of the Annunziata valley, below the hamlet of Arborina. Elio Altare's Arborina, from vines around his house, was one of the founding wines of the modernist movement. After visiting Burgundy he cut short macerations, used new barriques and, in the early 1980s, famously took a chainsaw to his father's old casks, a rupture that split his family and the village.

Arborina wines are fragrant and supple, with sweet red fruit, and drink earlier than the steep sites nearby. Mauro Veglio and Gianfranco Bovio also bottle it.

it-barolo-bricco-boschis.summary:

The family has farmed here since 1928 and bottled its own wine since 1948, and the Cavallotto siblings are among the most respected traditionalists of the zone, with long macerations, large Slavonian casks and grassed vineyards.

Vigna San Giuseppe, the steep heart of the hill, gives their Riserva, a dense, long-lived Barolo; the main Bricco Boschis bottling is more open and perfumed. Cavallotto were early converts to grassed vineyards and natural methods.

it-barolo-bricco-delle-viole.name: Bricco delle Viole
it-barolo-bricco-delle-viole.summary:
Bricco delle Viole is the high ground of the Barolo commune, around 400 to 480 m near the chapel of San Pietro delle Viole above the hamlet of Vergne, on the ridge road toward La Morra. The wines live up to the name: ethereal, rose- and violet-scented Barolo with fine, cool tannin and bright acidity.

For most of the twentieth century such high sites ripened Nebbiolo only in warm years and were often planted to Dolcetto. Warmer summers have reversed that, and Bricco delle Viole has climbed the informal hierarchy since the 2000s. G.D. Vajra's Bricco delle Viole, from vines the family has farmed since the 1970s, is the benchmark; Mario Marengo and Sylla Sebaste also bottle it.
it-barolo-bricco-delle-viole.terroir: Tortonian Sant'Agata marls with sandier layers on the upper slopes; a cool, ventilated position at the top of the commune. On the official MGA map the digitised outline covers about 43 ha at roughly 395 to 460 m, facing broadly south-east. (Approximate outline; total area, not vines; elevations from the Copernicus DEM.)
it-barolo-bricco-delle-viole.nerd_note: Aldo Vaira founded G.D. Vajra in 1972 and planted at Bricco delle Viole when high sites were still considered second-rate; the estate's Barolo Bricco delle Viole is now its flagship.

it-barolo-brunate.name: Brunate
it-barolo-brunate.summary:
Brunate is one of the two or three greatest crus of the western Barolo zone: about 25 to 28 ha of steep slope facing south to south-east below the little Brunate chapel, straddling the La Morra and Barolo border just east of Cerequio. It is the exception to the rule that La Morra makes soft, early Barolo. The calcareous Sant'Agata marls here are compact and rich in limestone, and the wines have the depth, dark fruit and firm tannin usually associated with the eastern communes, wrapped in La Morra's perfume.

The site is split among many owners, so it can be tasted through very different hands. Giuseppe Rinaldi's Brunate, from the Barolo side, is a benchmark of the traditional school; Roberto Voerzio's low-yield Brunate and Marcarini's long-lived bottling are references from La Morra; Ceretto (Bricco Brunate), Vietti, Oddero and Francesco Rinaldi also make it.
it-barolo-brunate.terroir: Steep south to south-east-facing slopes of compact, limestone-rich Sant'Agata marls (Tortonian). On the official MGA map the digitised outline covers about 27 ha at roughly 230 to 375 m. (Approximate outline; total area, not vines; elevations from the Copernicus DEM.)
it-barolo-brunate.nerd_note: Giuseppe Rinaldi once blended Brunate with Le Coste; the MGA rule against two names on a label ended the 'Brunate-Le Coste' bottling, and the Brunate is now on its own.

it-barolo-bussia.name: Bussia
it-barolo-bussia.summary:
With almost 300 ha, Bussia is the largest MGA in Barolo and the clearest case of how an MGA is a place name, not a quality rank. It sweeps from the Barolo border through a series of amphitheatres toward Castiglione Falletto, with every exposure and a long span of altitudes, from warm, steep bowls to cool upper slopes.

The historic heart, Bussia Soprana, faces south-west, and there Aldo Conterno's Colonnello, Cicala and Romirasco parcels give some of the most complete Barolo of Monforte: powerful, dark-fruited and long-lived, from Serravallian sandstone and marl. Outer sectors such as Munie are less prized. Prunotto's Bussia of 1961 was one of the first single-vineyard Barolos ever labelled, and Poderi Colla, Giacomo Fenocchio, Oddero, Silvano Bolmida and Barale also bottle Bussia.

Because one name covers so much, many producers add a vigna name (Bussia Vigna Colonnello, Bussia Vigna Mondoca) to tell their parcel apart.
it-barolo-bussia.terroir: Serravallian marls and Diano sandstone; amphitheatres facing south-west, west and north-west across a wide altitude range. On the official MGA map the digitised outline covers about 280 ha at roughly 245 to 445 m. (Approximate outline; total area, not vines; elevations from the Copernicus DEM.)
it-barolo-bussia.nerd_note: Oddero's Bussia Vigna Mondoca Riserva and Aldo Conterno's Granbussia (a blend of Romirasco, Cicala and Colonnello) show how differently the same MGA can be read.

it-barolo-cannubi.name: Cannubi
it-barolo-cannubi.summary:
Cannubi is the most famous name in Barolo and the first to appear on a label: a bottle marked 'Cannubi 1752' is said to survive. The long, low hill runs north-east out of Barolo village toward the Alba road, a single whaleback ridge standing apart from the hills on either side, which is why it was planted and named so early.

Its crest is a geological seam: the Tortonian blue-grey marls that dominate La Morra meet the sandier Serravallian layers of the eastern zone, and Cannubi wines combine the two, with the perfume and red fruit of the west and a firmer, finer tannic frame than most Barolo-village sites. Cannubi rarely gives the biggest Barolo of a vintage, but often the most complete, and it ages for decades without losing its fragrance.

The historic core, about 15 ha, faces south-east at roughly 250 to 320 m. When the MGAs were drawn in 2010 the whole hill (about 34 ha) was allowed to use the Cannubi name, alone or hyphenated with Boschis, Muscatel, San Lorenzo or Valletta. A group of core growers challenged this; the TAR Lazio upheld them, but on 3 October 2013 the Consiglio di Stato reinstated the 2010 rule, so the hill-wide name stands.
it-barolo-cannubi.terroir: South-east-facing slopes of the historic core on Tortonian Sant'Agata marls with sandy Serravallian layers near the crest. On the official MGA map the digitised outline covers about 19 ha at roughly 225 to 295 m. (Approximate outline; total area, not vines; elevations from the Copernicus DEM.)
it-barolo-cannubi.classification: MGA (menzione geografica aggiuntiva) of Barolo DOCG: one of the 170 named vineyard areas listed in the disciplinare from the 2010 vintage (plus 11 village names). The name may follow "Barolo" on the label only if all the grapes come from inside it; it is a place name, not a quality rank.

it-barolo-cannubi-boschis.name: Cannubi Boschis
it-barolo-cannubi-boschis.summary:
The north-eastern end of the Cannubi hill, facing east and south-east above the road to Alba. Luciano Sandrone made it famous with his first Barolo, the 1978 Cannubi Boschis, made in a garage while he still worked as cellar master at Marchesi di Barolo. Bottled young, ripe and polished, it became one of the defining wines of the modernist years and proved that a small grower could outshine the old houses.

Cannubi Boschis gives slightly darker, more generous wine than the core of the hill, with the same fine-grained tannin. Since the 2013 vintage Sandrone has labelled his wine 'Aleste', a play on the names of his grandchildren Alessia and Stefano, because the MGA rules folded the old name into the Cannubi family; E. Pira (Chiara Boschis) and Francesco Rinaldi also bottle it.
it-barolo-cannubi-boschis.terroir: On the official MGA map the digitised outline covers about 12 ha at roughly 220 to 260 m, facing south-east to east. (Approximate outline; total area, not vines; elevations from the Copernicus DEM.)
it-barolo-cannubi-boschis.nerd_note: Under the 2010 rules its wines may be labelled either 'Cannubi Boschis' or simply 'Cannubi'.
it-barolo-cannubi-boschis.classification: MGA (menzione geografica aggiuntiva) of Barolo DOCG: one of the 170 named vineyard areas listed in the disciplinare from the 2010 vintage (plus 11 village names). Its warm, sheltered bowl collects heat, and the wines are among the ripest and most opulent of the western zone, broad-shouldered and spicy but with the fine tannin of Tortonian marl.

Cerequio was a symbol of the 1990s modernist peak through Roberto Voerzio's tiny-yield bottling. Michele Chiarlo owns the largest share and built the Palas Cerequio wine resort here; Gaja's Conteisa comes from Cerequio vines the family bought in 1995, and Batasiolo and Giuseppe Contratto bottle it too.

Ettore Germano's Cerretta, Giovanni Rosso's Cerretta and Elio Altare's Cerretta Vigna Bricco (from vines bought in 2007, Altare's first move to Serralunga) are the best known; Schiavenza also bottles it.

it-barolo-falletto.name: Falletto
it-barolo-falletto.summary:
Bruno Giacosa's estate vineyard, bought in 1982, in the south of Serralunga below the village toward Francia and Vignarionda. Giacosa had built his name as a buyer of grapes from the best growers; Falletto was his first major vineyard of his own, and the upper sector became Le Rocche del Falletto, whose Riserva, released under Giacosa's red label only in the finest years, is among the most coveted Barolos made.

Calcareous Serravallian marl gives austere, slow-maturing wines of great depth, which Giacosa and his long-time winemaker Dante Scaglione shaped in large oak. Since Bruno Giacosa's death in 2018 his daughter Bruna has run the estate.

it-barolo-francia.name: Francia
it-barolo-francia.summary:
Francia is Giacomo Conterno's 14-ha monopole in the south of Serralunga, bought by Giovanni Conterno in 1974 from the estate of Cascina Francia. It is the source of Monfortino, made here since the 1978 vintage, and of Barolo Cascina Francia, labelled simply 'Francia' since the MGA rules. Both are made in the same traditional way, with long macerations and years in large oak; Monfortino gets the best lots and a longer stay in cask.

The slope faces west at about 350 to 450 m, on poor, calcareous Serravallian marl, and the wines are among the most structured and long-lived in Barolo: dark, savoury and tightly wound for a decade, then profound. Roberto Conterno has run the estate since his father Giovanni's death in 2004.

Its sub-sites are famous in their own right: Domenico Clerico's Ciabot Mentin and Pajana, Elio Grasso's Casa Maté, Conterno Fantino's Sorì Ginestra and Vigna del Gris, Paolo Conterno's Ginestra, and bottlings from Prunotto and Giovanni Manzone.

La Serra was long thought too cool to be a top site; its altitude, wind and lighter soils give taut, high-toned Barolo with fine tannin and a lifted, floral nose, and warm vintages since the 2000s have shown it off.

Roberto Voerzio's La Serra is the reference; Marcarini and Gianni Voerzio bottle it too, and the contrast between La Serra and Brunate, a few hundred metres apart, is one of the best lessons in how altitude shapes Barolo.

it-barolo-monprivato.name: Monprivato
it-barolo-monprivato.summary:
Monprivato is the clearest case in Barolo of a great site tied to one family. About 7 ha of slope just west and below Castiglione Falletto village, facing south-west, it is almost entirely owned by Giuseppe Mascarello e Figlio. The family bought its first Monprivato vines in 1904 and pieced together almost the whole slope over the following decades; Mauro Mascarello first bottled it alone with the 1970 vintage, at a time when nearly all Barolo was blended.

Clay-rich marl over limestone, at the meeting point of the zone's two geologies, gives Barolo of exquisite balance: rose and red cherry with a mineral, savoury core, tannin that is firm but never coarse, and a reputation for ageing over decades. Ca' d'Morissio, a Riserva from a selection of the old Michet clone of Nebbiolo grown in Monprivato, is made only in the greatest years.
it-barolo-monprivato.terroir: South-west-facing slope of clay-rich marl over limestone, in the transition between Tortonian and Serravallian soils. On the official MGA map the digitised outline covers about 5.1 ha at roughly 270 to 325 m, facing south-west to west. (Approximate outline; total area, not vines; elevations from the Copernicus DEM.)
it-barolo-monprivato.nerd_note: Michet is a Nebbiolo selection affected by a virus that shortens its internodes; Mascarello propagated its own old Michet vines for Ca' d'Morissio.

The grand cru of Verduno: a slope facing south and south-east below the village, on the Tanaro side of the Barolo zone, with sandy Tortonian marl. Its wines are perfumed, spicy and transparent, with wild strawberry, rose and white pepper and a fine, insistent tannin, the most aromatic style in Barolo.

G.B. Burlotto's Monvigliero, fermented with whole bunches and foot-trodden, is the famous interpretation, and its price and prestige soared through the 2010s. Paolo Scavino, Castello di Verduno, Bel Colle, Fratelli Alessandria and Diego Morra also make it. Verduno's Pelaverga Piccolo, a pale, peppery red grape, grows on the same slopes.

Long split among small growers who sold their grapes, it became sought-after when Pio Cesare and Conterno Fantino bought in, and it is known for broad, structured, black-fruited Barolo with a fresh finish from its altitude.

Pio Cesare's Mosconi, Conterno Fantino's Vigna Mosconi, Domenico Clerico's Percristina and Bruna Grimaldi's Mosconi are the references.

it-barolo-perno.name: Perno

It holds one of the great historic vineyards of Barolo, Santo Stefano di Perno, whose fruit Giuseppe Mascarello e Figlio has bottled for decades as a firmer, more austere counterpart to its Monprivato. Since the MGA rules the wine is labelled Barolo Perno Vigna Santo Stefano.

Rocche dei Manzoni's Vigna Cappella di Santo Stefano comes from the same hillside. Away from that sector Perno mixes every exposure and many lesser slopes, so the MGA name alone says little.

Elvio Cogno's estate sits on the ridge; its Ravera and the old-vine Bricco Pernice from the same slope put Novello on the map. Vietti's Ravera (first vintage 2008) quickly became one of the house's top wines, and G.D. Vajra, Giuseppe Rinaldi and Flavio Roddolo also bottle it.

it-barolo-rocche-dell-annunziata.name: Rocche dell'Annunziata
it-barolo-rocche-dell-annunziata.summary:
About 30 ha of steep, crumbling slopes (*rocche*) dropping from the hamlet of Torriglione toward the valley of the Annunziata, east of La Morra village. There are two sectors, one facing south-east and one south to south-west, on blue-grey marl veined with sand. The wines are the most perfumed and seductive of La Morra: rose, red cherry and spice, with silky but persistent tannin and great longevity in the best vintages.

Renato Ratti's Rocche dell'Annunziata, Paolo Scavino's Riserva and Roberto Voerzio's tiny bottling are famous, and Rocche Costamagna, Aurelio Settimo, Mauro Veglio, Trediberri and Fratelli Revello all bottle it. Bartolo Mascarello's blend has long included fruit from here.

it-barolo-rocche-di-castiglione.name: Rocche di Castiglione
it-barolo-rocche-di-castiglione.summary:
A narrow escarpment running south from Castiglione Falletto toward Perno, facing south-east above the valley that separates Castiglione and Monforte from Serralunga. The steep, crumbling slopes of sandstone and marl (the *rocche*) carry little topsoil, and the wines are the most elegant and aromatic of the commune: pale, high-toned, all roses, red fruit and spice, with fine but persistent tannin.

Brovia, Vietti, Oddero, Paolo Scavino and Fratelli Monchiero bottle it, and Bruno Giacosa's 1978 Rocche is a legend. The MGA continues a little way into Monforte d'Alba.

it-barolo-rocche-di-castiglione.nerd_note: Vietti's Rocche, first bottled in 1961, was one of the earliest single-vineyard Barolos on the market.

it-barolo-sarmassa.summary:

Its compact, chalky Tortonian marls make deeper-coloured, firmer and more austere wines than Cannubi across the valley, closer in build to Brunate, and they need longer in bottle.

Giacomo Brezza's Sarmassa (with the old-vine Vigna Bricco bottling) is a classic of the traditional school, aged in large Slavonian oak; Marchesi di Barolo and Roberto Voerzio also bottle it, and Giorgio Scarzello's Sarmassa Vigna Merenda is a small-production favourite of Barolo insiders.

it-barolo-vignarionda.name: Vignarionda
it-barolo-vignarionda.summary:
About 10 ha of south to south-west-facing amphitheatre at around 300 to 350 m, south of Serralunga village, on calcareous marl. Long regarded as Serralunga's greatest cru, Vignarionda (often written Vigna Rionda) gives dense, mineral, extremely long-lived Barolo, with a balsamic, liquorice and red-fruit depth and tannins that need many years.

Massolino's Vigna Rionda Riserva, aged several years before release, is the reference; Oddero's Vignarionda Riserva, Luigi Pira, Giacomo Anselma, Arnaldo Rivera (the cru line of Terre del Barolo) and Ettore Germano also bottle it. Bruno Giacosa bought Vigna Rionda grapes in the 1960s and 1970s, and his Collina Rionda bottlings, made until the early 1990s, are collector legends.

it-barolo-vignolo.summary: A small slope north-west of Castiglione Falletto village toward the La Morra side. Cavallotto's Riserva Vignolo, from vines the family owns here, is a firm, long-lived traditional Barolo.
it-barolo-vignolo.terroir: On the official MGA map the digitised outline lies at roughly 240 to 265 m, facing broadly west-north-west. (Approximate outline; total area, not vines; elevations from the Copernicus DEM.)

it-barolo-villero.summary:
Villero is a large amphitheatre south of Castiglione village, facing south-west over the valley toward Monforte, and for many growers the finest site in the commune. Its deep marl gives wines that combine the two sides of Barolo: the perfume and red fruit of the west and the weight and long, firm tannin of the east.

Vietti's Villero Riserva, made only in top vintages since 1982, is one of the most collected Barolos; Brovia, Giacomo Fenocchio, Oddero, Boroli and Giuseppe Mascarello e Figlio also bottle it, so Villero is one of the best places to compare traditional and modern hands on the same slope.
