it-cannonau-di-sardegna-capo-ferrato.name: Capo Ferrato
it-cannonau-di-sardegna-capo-ferrato.village: Castiadas, Muravera, San Vito, Villaputzu, Villasimius
it-cannonau-di-sardegna-capo-ferrato.summary: The only subzone in the south of the island, on the south-east coast in Castiadas, Muravera, San Vito, Villaputzu and Villasimius, named after the headland of Capo Ferrato. Warm, maritime and lower than the mountain subzones, it gives rounder, riper Cannonau. Cantina Castiadas, the local cooperative, is the main producer. Capo Ferrato is also the only subzone that cannot be called Classico: that mention is reserved to the provinces of Nuoro and Ogliastra, and the Sarrabus coast lies in the south.
it-cannonau-di-sardegna-capo-ferrato.terroir: Coastal hills and plains of the Sarrabus, granite sands and alluvium; hot and dry, tempered by the sea.
it-cannonau-di-sardegna-capo-ferrato.classification: Sottozona of Cannonau di Sardegna DOC (one of three: Oliena or Nepente di Oliena, Jerzu, Capo Ferrato). Ageing and bottling must take place inside the subzone, unlike the island-wide DOC, and bag-in-box or other alternatives to glass are not allowed.

it-cannonau-di-sardegna-jerzu.name: Jerzu
it-cannonau-di-sardegna-jerzu.summary: Jerzu, in the Ogliastra on Sardinia's east side, is a village of steep vineyards below the limestone tacchi (table mountains), with the subzone extending to Cardedu on the coast. Cannonau has been the village's living for generations, and the Antichi Poderi di Jerzu cooperative makes most of the wine: ripe, spicy and generous, with the grip of the mountain sites. Ageing and bottling must take place inside the subzone.
it-cannonau-di-sardegna-jerzu.terroir: Slopes from near the coast at Cardedu up to the terraces below the tacchi of Jerzu, granite and schist with limestone above; hot, dry summers and sea breezes.
it-cannonau-di-sardegna-jerzu.nerd_note: The Ogliastra around Jerzu is one of the world's 'blue zones' of exceptional longevity, where the daily glass of Cannonau is part of local lore.
it-cannonau-di-sardegna-jerzu.classification: Sottozona of Cannonau di Sardegna DOC (one of three: Oliena or Nepente di Oliena, Jerzu, Capo Ferrato). Ageing and bottling must take place inside the subzone, unlike the island-wide DOC, and bag-in-box or other alternatives to glass are not allowed.

it-cannonau-di-sardegna-oliena.name: Oliena
it-cannonau-di-sardegna-oliena.summary: Oliena lies at the foot of Monte Corrasi and the limestone Supramonte near Nuoro, and its Cannonau has a literary nickname: Gabriele D'Annunzio called it 'Nepente di Oliena', after the nepenthe, Homer's drug of forgetfulness, and the subzone may use either name. It covers the whole commune of Oliena and part of Orgosolo. The wines are dark, warm and herbal, with the firmness of mountain fruit. The Cantina di Oliena cooperative and Gostolai are leading producers.
it-cannonau-di-sardegna-oliena.terroir: Slopes below the Supramonte limestone around Oliena, roughly 200 to 600 m; limestone and granite soils, dry, sunny and windy.
it-cannonau-di-sardegna-oliena.nerd_note: D'Annunzio's tribute made Oliena's Cannonau one of the few Italian wines with a nickname written into the rules: 'Oliena o Nepente di Oliena'.
it-cannonau-di-sardegna-oliena.classification: Sottozona of Cannonau di Sardegna DOC (one of three: Oliena or Nepente di Oliena, Jerzu, Capo Ferrato). Ageing and bottling must take place inside the subzone, unlike the island-wide DOC, and bag-in-box or other alternatives to glass are not allowed.

it-chianti-classico-castellina.name: Castellina
it-chianti-classico-castellina.summary:
Castellina in Chianti, one of the three founding members of the medieval Lega del Chianti with Radda and Gaiole, sits on the ridge that splits the Pesa and Elsa valleys, at the centre of the zone. Its soils are the most varied of Chianti Classico: alberese and galestro in the east, sandstone, and Pliocene sands and clays on the western slopes toward the Elsa. The wines are balanced and fruity, between the ripeness of the south and the tension of Radda.

Castello di Fonterutoli (Mazzei), Castellare di Castellina, Rocca delle Macìe, Nittardi, Tenuta di Lilliano and Cecchi are based here.
it-chianti-classico-castellina.terroir: The UGA as a whole lies at about 205 to 575 m (Copernicus DEM).
it-chianti-classico-castellina.nerd_note: The Mazzei family has owned Fonterutoli since 1435; a Mazzei, the notary Ser Lapo, wrote the earliest known document using the name Chianti for wine, in 1398.
it-chianti-classico-castellina.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Chianti Classico DOCG, one of 11 voted by producers in June 2021 and approved by the Ministry in 2023 (DM 22 June 2023). The UGA name may appear on Gran Selezione labels; the Consorzio intends to extend it to Annata and Riserva.
it-chianti-classico-castellina.created: UGA of Chianti Classico (approved June 2021; effective 2023 rules)

it-chianti-classico-castelnuovo-berarden.name: Castelnuovo Berardenga
it-chianti-classico-castelnuovo-berarden.summary:
The southernmost and warmest UGA, where Chianti Classico runs down toward the clay hills of the Crete Senesi east of Siena. More clay, marine Pliocene sands and alberese, a lower average altitude and a warmer, drier climate give the ripest, fullest and most generous Sangiovese of the zone, dark-fruited and broad.

Fèlsina, which has labelled its wines 'Berardenga' for decades and whose Rancia is a reference single-vineyard Chianti Classico, Castell'in Villa, San Felice and Fattoria di Petroio are here.
it-chianti-classico-castelnuovo-berarden.terroir: The UGA as a whole lies at about 235 to 565 m (Copernicus DEM).
it-chianti-classico-castelnuovo-berarden.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Chianti Classico DOCG, one of 11 voted by producers in June 2021 and approved by the Ministry in 2023 (DM 22 June 2023). The UGA name may appear on Gran Selezione labels; the Consorzio intends to extend it to Annata and Riserva.
it-chianti-classico-castelnuovo-berarden.created: UGA of Chianti Classico (approved June 2021; effective 2023 rules)

it-chianti-classico-gaiole.name: Gaiole
it-chianti-classico-gaiole.summary:
Gaiole in Chianti spreads across the eastern Monti del Chianti, a high, wooded commune of castles and abbeys that includes Brolio, Coltibuono, Ama, Cacchiano and Meleto. Soils are galestro and alberese with macigno sandstone on the heights, and altitudes run from about 300 to 650 m, so the wines range from firm and structured in the south to fragrant and lean in the north.

At Brolio, Baron Bettino Ricasoli set out in 1872 the recipe on which Chianti was later based. Castello di Ama, Badia a Coltibuono, Barone Ricasoli, Riecine, Rocca di Montegrossi and San Giusto a Rentennano are leading estates.
it-chianti-classico-gaiole.terroir: The UGA as a whole lies at about 295 to 675 m (Copernicus DEM).
it-chianti-classico-gaiole.nerd_note: Ricasoli's 1872 letter recommended Sangiovese for body and aroma, Canaiolo to soften it, and Malvasia for wines meant to be drunk young.
it-chianti-classico-gaiole.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Chianti Classico DOCG, one of 11 voted by producers in June 2021 and approved by the Ministry in 2023 (DM 22 June 2023). The UGA name may appear on Gran Selezione labels; the Consorzio intends to extend it to Annata and Riserva.
it-chianti-classico-gaiole.created: UGA of Chianti Classico (approved June 2021; effective 2023 rules)

it-chianti-classico-greve.name: Greve
it-chianti-classico-greve.summary:
The Greve UGA is the commune of Greve in Chianti minus the three UGAs carved out of it (Panzano, Lamole and Montefioralle). It runs from the Greve valley floor up the slopes of the Monti del Chianti toward the high ridge of Ruffoli, so it spans a wide range of altitudes and soils: alberese and galestro, with sandstone (macigno) on the eastern heights. Greve town, with its funnel-shaped piazza, is the market centre of the northern Chianti.

Querciabella, a biodynamic pioneer in the high Ruffoli area, Castello di Verrazzano (home of the navigator Giovanni da Verrazzano) and Vignamaggio (where Lisa Gherardini, the probable sitter of the Mona Lisa, is said to have lived) are the best-known estates.
it-chianti-classico-greve.terroir: The UGA as a whole lies at about 175 to 690 m (Copernicus DEM).
it-chianti-classico-greve.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Chianti Classico DOCG, one of 11 voted by producers in June 2021 and approved by the Ministry in 2023 (DM 22 June 2023). The UGA name may appear on Gran Selezione labels; the Consorzio intends to extend it to Annata and Riserva.
it-chianti-classico-greve.created: UGA of Chianti Classico (approved June 2021; effective 2023 rules)

it-chianti-classico-lamole.name: Lamole
it-chianti-classico-lamole.summary:
The smallest and highest UGA, a hamlet of terraces high above Greve, with vineyards at roughly 450 to 650 m and the UGA as a whole reaching about 850 m. Dry-stone walls, many rebuilt by hand since the 1990s, hold the slopes, and the soils are sandstone (macigno), poor and acid-leaning, unlike the limestone of most of Chianti Classico.

The result is pale, high-toned, floral Sangiovese with bright acidity and fine tannin, closer to a mountain wine; the old bush-trained vines (*alberello*) on the terraces are a rarity in Tuscany. Castello di Lamole, Lamole di Lamole, I Fabbri and Castellinuzza e Piuca are the main producers.
it-chianti-classico-lamole.terroir: Macigno sandstone terraces, among the highest vineyards of Chianti Classico. The UGA as a whole lies at about 430 to 855 m (Copernicus DEM).
it-chianti-classico-lamole.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Chianti Classico DOCG, one of 11 voted by producers in June 2021 and approved by the Ministry in 2023 (DM 22 June 2023). The UGA name may appear on Gran Selezione labels; the Consorzio intends to extend it to Annata and Riserva.
it-chianti-classico-lamole.created: UGA of Chianti Classico (approved June 2021; effective 2023 rules)

it-chianti-classico-montefioralle.name: Montefioralle
it-chianti-classico-montefioralle.summary: A small UGA around the walled medieval village of Montefioralle on the hill just west of Greve, believed to be the family home of the Vespucci (of Amerigo Vespucci). Its slopes of alberese and galestro rise to about 500 m between the Greve and Pesa valleys and give fragrant, mid-weight Sangiovese with good acidity. With Vagliagli it is one of the two UGAs without a long history as a named wine area.
it-chianti-classico-montefioralle.terroir: Alberese limestone and galestro on the ridge west of Greve. The UGA as a whole lies at about 230 to 505 m (Copernicus DEM).
it-chianti-classico-montefioralle.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Chianti Classico DOCG, one of 11 voted by producers in June 2021 and approved by the Ministry in 2023 (DM 22 June 2023). The UGA name may appear on Gran Selezione labels; the Consorzio intends to extend it to Annata and Riserva.
it-chianti-classico-montefioralle.created: UGA of Chianti Classico (approved June 2021; effective 2023 rules)

it-chianti-classico-panzano.name: Panzano
it-chianti-classico-panzano.summary:
Panzano is the frazione in the south-west of Greve commune famous for the Conca d'Oro, the 'golden shell', a south-facing amphitheatre below the village on galestro and alberese that collects heat and gives some of the most complete Sangiovese in Tuscany: dark cherry, violets and a firm, mineral frame.

Fontodi, the Manetti family estate whose Flaccianello della Pieve is a reference for pure Sangiovese, Castello dei Rampolla, Il Molino di Grace, La Massa, Le Cinciole and Vecchie Terre di Montefili are here. Panzano's growers formed one of Italy's first organic districts, and most of the vineyard is farmed organically.
it-chianti-classico-panzano.terroir: Galestro (friable schistous clay) and alberese limestone; the Conca d'Oro faces south below Panzano village. The UGA as a whole lies at about 275 to 655 m (Copernicus DEM).
it-chianti-classico-panzano.nerd_note: Giovanni Manetti of Fontodi has chaired the Consorzio Vino Chianti Classico, which pushed the UGA project.
it-chianti-classico-panzano.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Chianti Classico DOCG, one of 11 voted by producers in June 2021 and approved by the Ministry in 2023 (DM 22 June 2023). The UGA name may appear on Gran Selezione labels; the Consorzio intends to extend it to Annata and Riserva.
it-chianti-classico-panzano.created: UGA of Chianti Classico (approved June 2021; effective 2023 rules)

it-chianti-classico-radda.name: Radda
it-chianti-classico-radda.summary:
Radda in Chianti was the capital of the medieval Lega del Chianti and is the reference for high-altitude, galestro-driven Sangiovese: vineyards at roughly 350 to 650 m among woods, cool nights and poor, stony soils of galestro, alberese and some sandstone. The wines are pale, perfumed and nervy, sometimes austere in youth, with red fruit, orange peel and a long, saline line; warmer summers have made Radda one of the most sought-after names of the 2010s.

Montevertine, whose Le Pergole Torte (1977) was one of the first pure-Sangiovese Super Tuscans, Castello di Volpaia, Monteraponi, Val delle Corti, Istine and Caparsa are references.
it-chianti-classico-radda.terroir: The UGA as a whole lies at about 350 to 725 m (Copernicus DEM).
it-chianti-classico-radda.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Chianti Classico DOCG, one of 11 voted by producers in June 2021 and approved by the Ministry in 2023 (DM 22 June 2023). The UGA name may appear on Gran Selezione labels; the Consorzio intends to extend it to Annata and Riserva.
it-chianti-classico-radda.created: UGA of Chianti Classico (approved June 2021; effective 2023 rules)

it-chianti-classico-san-casciano.name: San Casciano
it-chianti-classico-san-casciano.village: San Casciano in Val di Pesa
it-chianti-classico-san-casciano.summary:
San Casciano is the northern gateway to Chianti Classico, on the lower, gentler hills of the Val di Pesa toward Florence. Much of the commune lies below 400 m, on marine Pliocene sands and clays with river pebbles, and on alberese limestone and galestro on the higher ground to the south. The climate is the mildest of the zone, and the wines are generous, round and early to charm, with ripe cherry and softer tannin than the high sites of the Monti del Chianti.

Antinori's cellar at Bargino, dug into the hillside, and its Tignanello estate are here, as are the Castelli del Grevepesa cooperative and the villa of Sant'Andrea in Percussina, where Niccolò Machiavelli wrote The Prince in exile.
it-chianti-classico-san-casciano.terroir: Pliocene sands, clays and pebbles on the lower hills; alberese and galestro to the south. The UGA as a whole lies at about 125 to 375 m (Copernicus DEM).
producers: Marchesi Antinori (Tignanello, Antinori nel Chianti Classico)
it-chianti-classico-san-casciano.nerd_note: Tignanello was first made in 1970 as a Chianti Classico Riserva, became a table wine with the 1971 vintage and added Cabernet from 1975; it is often named among the first 'Super Tuscans'.
it-chianti-classico-san-casciano.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Chianti Classico DOCG, one of 11 voted by producers in June 2021 and approved by the Ministry in 2023 (DM 22 June 2023). The UGA name may appear on Gran Selezione labels; the Consorzio intends to extend it to Annata and Riserva.
it-chianti-classico-san-casciano.created: UGA of Chianti Classico (approved June 2021; effective 2023 rules)

it-chianti-classico-san-donato-in-poggio.name: San Donato in Poggio
it-chianti-classico-san-donato-in-poggio.summary:
This UGA joins the Chianti Classico part of Barberino Tavarnelle with the northern tip of Poggibonsi, centred on the walled village of San Donato in Poggio on the ridge between the Pesa and Elsa valleys. Alberese and galestro on the ridge, and sands and clays on the western slopes, give firm, medium-bodied Sangiovese.

Isole e Olena, whose Cepparello became a benchmark pure Sangiovese, Castello di Monsanto, whose Il Poggio (1962) is often cited as the first single-vineyard Chianti Classico, and Antinori's Badia a Passignano are here.
it-chianti-classico-san-donato-in-poggio.terroir: The UGA as a whole lies at about 210 to 450 m (Copernicus DEM).
it-chianti-classico-san-donato-in-poggio.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Chianti Classico DOCG, one of 11 voted by producers in June 2021 and approved by the Ministry in 2023 (DM 22 June 2023). The UGA name may appear on Gran Selezione labels; the Consorzio intends to extend it to Annata and Riserva.

it-chianti-classico-vagliagli.name: Vagliagli
it-chianti-classico-vagliagli.summary: A UGA in the western part of Castelnuovo Berardenga around the hamlet of Vagliagli, higher and cooler than the southern part of the commune, at roughly 250 to 470 m. Alberese limestone and sandstone give Sangiovese with more tension and perfume than the warm Berardenga, and the area is a patchwork of woods and vines. Dievole, Fattoria della Aiola and Bindi Sergardi are among its estates.
it-chianti-classico-vagliagli.terroir: Alberese limestone and sandstone, with woods covering much of the land. The UGA as a whole lies at about 255 to 465 m (Copernicus DEM).
it-chianti-classico-vagliagli.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Chianti Classico DOCG, one of 11 voted by producers in June 2021 and approved by the Ministry in 2023 (DM 22 June 2023). The UGA name may appear on Gran Selezione labels; the Consorzio intends to extend it to Annata and Riserva.
it-chianti-classico-vagliagli.created: UGA of Chianti Classico (approved June 2021; effective 2023 rules)

it-conegliano-valdobbiadene-prosecco-car.name: Cartizze
it-conegliano-valdobbiadene-prosecco-car.grapes: Glera (at least 85%), with Verdiso, Bianchetta Trevigiana, Perera and Glera lunga
it-conegliano-valdobbiadene-prosecco-car.summary:
Cartizze is the grand cru of Prosecco in all but name: a single, steep amphitheatre of about 106 ha in the frazione of San Pietro di Barbozza in Valdobbiadene, between the hamlets of San Pietro di Barbozza, Santo Stefano and Saccol. The disciplinare singles it out for its gradient and its southern exposure, which make a natural sun trap above the cold-air drainage of the valley.

It is the only sottozona of the DOCG, with its own name on the label: 'Valdobbiadene Superiore di Cartizze' (or Conegliano Valdobbiadene Superiore di Cartizze). Yields are capped at 12 t/ha, picking is by hand, and the wine must be made inside the commune of Valdobbiadene. The land is split among well over a hundred owners, many with only a few rows, and is among the most expensive vineyard land in Italy.

Tradition makes Cartizze sweeter than other Prosecco Superiore, usually labelled Dry, because the ripe, aromatic fruit (apple, pear, white flowers, wisteria, rose, as the disciplinare puts it) carries the sugar. Bisol, Ruggeri, Col Vetoraz, Bortolomiol, Nino Franco, Adami, Le Colture and Villa Sandi (from its La Rivetta vineyard) bottle it; Silvano Follador's bone-dry Brut Nature version shows a different face.
it-conegliano-valdobbiadene-prosecco-car.terroir: About 106 ha on a south-facing amphitheatre of steep slopes and terraces at San Pietro di Barbozza, Santo Stefano and Saccol. Marine sandstone and marl, shallow and well drained; sheltered by the Pre-Alps, with strong day-night swings.
it-conegliano-valdobbiadene-prosecco-car.nerd_note: Cartizze is legally a sottozona with a 12 t/ha cap, lower than both the DOCG (13.5) and the Rive (13), and its wine must be vinified inside Valdobbiadene, the only Prosecco place-name with that rule.
it-conegliano-valdobbiadene-prosecco-car.classification: Sottozona of Conegliano Valdobbiadene Prosecco Superiore DOCG (the only one), reserved for spumante: maximum 12 t/ha, hand harvest, vinification within the commune of Valdobbiadene; labelled 'Superiore di Cartizze'.

it-conegliano-valdobbiadene-prosecco-riv.name: Arfanta
it-conegliano-valdobbiadene-prosecco-riv.grapes: Glera (at least 85%), with Verdiso, Bianchetta Trevigiana, Perera and Glera lunga
it-conegliano-valdobbiadene-prosecco-riv.summary: A frazione of Tarzo in the north-eastern hills, among woods and steep vineyards. Tarzo's four Rive lie on the hills between the Soligo valley and the Revine lakes, toward Vittorio Veneto.
it-conegliano-valdobbiadene-prosecco-riv.terroir: The central Soligo valley hills sit between the steep, cool ridges of Valdobbiadene and the gentler Conegliano side, on sandstone, marl and conglomerate with morainic patches.
it-conegliano-valdobbiadene-prosecco-riv.classification: Rive: one of the 43 unità geografiche aggiuntive in Annex A of the Conegliano Valdobbiadene Prosecco Superiore DOCG rules, each a commune or frazione. A Rive wine must be spumante from grapes of that single place, hand-picked, at no more than 13 t/ha (against 13.5 for the DOCG), with the vintage on the label, released from 1 March after the harvest.

it-conegliano-valdobbiadene-prosecco-riv.name: Bagnolo
it-conegliano-valdobbiadene-prosecco-riv.grapes: Glera (at least 85%), with Verdiso, Bianchetta Trevigiana, Perera and Glera lunga
it-conegliano-valdobbiadene-prosecco-riv.summary: A frazione of San Pietro di Feletto, on the lower hills toward Conegliano. The Feletto hills north of Conegliano, with five Rive, are crossed by the Strada del Prosecco, which in 1966 became Italy's first signposted wine road.
it-conegliano-valdobbiadene-prosecco-riv.terroir: Around Conegliano the hills are lower and gentler, with more morainic and alluvial deposits mixed with marl and sandstone, and warmer, earlier ripening; wines tend to be rounder and riper in fruit than in Valdobbiadene.
it-conegliano-valdobbiadene-prosecco-riv.classification: Rive: one of the 43 unità geografiche aggiuntive in Annex A of the Conegliano Valdobbiadene Prosecco Superiore DOCG rules, each a commune or frazione. A Rive wine must be spumante from grapes of that single place, hand-picked, at no more than 13 t/ha (against 13.5 for the DOCG), with the vintage on the label, released from 1 March after the harvest.

it-conegliano-valdobbiadene-prosecco-riv.name: Bigolino
it-conegliano-valdobbiadene-prosecco-riv.grapes: Glera (at least 85%), with Verdiso, Bianchetta Trevigiana, Perera and Glera lunga
it-conegliano-valdobbiadene-prosecco-riv.summary: Bigolino lies in the south of the commune near the Piave, where the DOCG boundary follows the edge of the river terrace. Lower and more open than the frazioni under the mountains, with alluvial influence near the river. Valdobbiadene was the birthplace of Venantius Fortunatus, the 6th-century poet and bishop of Poitiers who, the disciplinare recalls, already described its hills as a land where the vine flourishes beneath the bare mountain.
it-conegliano-valdobbiadene-prosecco-riv.terroir: Lower slopes and terraces above the Piave in the south of Valdobbiadene; marl and sandstone with alluvial deposits near the river terrace.
it-conegliano-valdobbiadene-prosecco-riv.classification: Rive: one of the 43 unità geografiche aggiuntive in Annex A of the Conegliano Valdobbiadene Prosecco Superiore DOCG rules, each a commune or frazione. A Rive wine must be spumante from grapes of that single place, hand-picked, at no more than 13 t/ha (against 13.5 for the DOCG), with the vintage on the label, released from 1 March after the harvest.

it-conegliano-valdobbiadene-prosecco-riv.name: Campea
it-conegliano-valdobbiadene-prosecco-riv.grapes: Glera (at least 85%), with Verdiso, Bianchetta Trevigiana, Perera and Glera lunga
it-conegliano-valdobbiadene-prosecco-riv.summary: A frazione of Miane on steep slopes below the Pre-Alps. Bisol 1542 bottles a Rive di Campea, and Rebuli's Extra Dry 'Ieta Rebuli' also comes from here. Miane's four Rive lie on the high northern edge of the DOCG under the Pre-Alps.
it-conegliano-valdobbiadene-prosecco-riv.terroir: The central Soligo valley hills sit between the steep, cool ridges of Valdobbiadene and the gentler Conegliano side, on sandstone, marl and conglomerate with morainic patches.

it-conegliano-valdobbiadene-prosecco-riv.name: Carpesica
it-conegliano-valdobbiadene-prosecco-riv.grapes: Glera (at least 85%), with Verdiso, Bianchetta Trevigiana, Perera and Glera lunga
it-conegliano-valdobbiadene-prosecco-riv.summary: A frazione of Vittorio Veneto on the eastern hills of the DOCG, between Conegliano and Vittorio. Vittorio Veneto, at the north-eastern edge of the DOCG, gave its name to the last battle of the First World War on the Italian front (1918); its four Rive lie on the gentler hills toward Conegliano.

it-conegliano-valdobbiadene-prosecco-riv.name: Cison di Valmarino
it-conegliano-valdobbiadene-prosecco-riv.grapes: Glera (at least 85%), with Verdiso, Bianchetta Trevigiana, Perera and Glera lunga
it-conegliano-valdobbiadene-prosecco-riv.summary: Cison di Valmarino lies under the Pre-Alps in the Valmareno, below the CastelBrando castle that dominates the village. Its vineyards are on the high, steep northern side of the DOCG. Cison's two Rive lie in the Valmareno at the foot of the Pre-Alps.
it-conegliano-valdobbiadene-prosecco-riv.terroir: The central Soligo valley hills sit between the steep, cool ridges of Valdobbiadene and the gentler Conegliano side, on sandstone, marl and conglomerate with morainic patches.

it-conegliano-valdobbiadene-prosecco-riv.name: Col San Martino
it-conegliano-valdobbiadene-prosecco-riv.grapes: Glera (at least 85%), with Verdiso, Bianchetta Trevigiana, Perera and Glera lunga
it-conegliano-valdobbiadene-prosecco-riv.summary: A frazione of Farra di Soligo on the steep central ridges, home to Andreola. Andreola and Bortolomiol both bottle Rive di Col San Martino. Farra di Soligo's three Rive lie on some of the steepest central ridges of the DOCG.
it-conegliano-valdobbiadene-prosecco-riv.terroir: The central Soligo valley hills sit between the steep, cool ridges of Valdobbiadene and the gentler Conegliano side, on sandstone, marl and conglomerate with morainic patches.

it-conegliano-valdobbiadene-prosecco-riv.name: Colbertaldo
it-conegliano-valdobbiadene-prosecco-riv.grapes: Glera (at least 85%), with Verdiso, Bianchetta Trevigiana, Perera and Glera lunga
it-conegliano-valdobbiadene-prosecco-riv.summary: A frazione of Vidor on the hills north of the Piave, between Valdobbiadene and Col San Martino, with steep south-facing slopes typical of the western DOCG. it-conegliano-valdobbiadene-prosecco-riv.summary: A frazione of San Pietro di Feletto, site of a former Camaldolese hermitage, on the rolling hills north of Conegliano. The Feletto hills north of Conegliano, with five Rive, are crossed by the Strada del Prosecco, which in 1966 became Italy's first signposted wine road.
it-conegliano-valdobbiadene-prosecco-riv.terroir: Around Conegliano the hills are lower and gentler, with more morainic and alluvial deposits mixed with marl and sandstone, and warmer, earlier ripening; wines tend to be rounder and riper in fruit than in Valdobbiadene.

A Rive wine must be spumante from grapes of that single place, hand-picked, at no more than 13 t/ha (against 13.5 for the DOCG), with the vintage on the label, released from 1 March after the harvest.

Valdobbiadene was the birthplace of Venantius Fortunatus, the 6th-century poet and bishop of Poitiers who, the disciplinare recalls, already described its hills as a land where the vine flourishes beneath the bare mountain.

it-etna-alboretto-chiuse-del-signore.summary: A double-named contrada between the Rovolazzo track, the Circumetnea and the Linguaglossa commune boundary, below Vaccarile. 'Chiuse del Signore' (the lord's enclosures) recalls walled fields of a feudal estate. Linguaglossa, the north-east gateway to Etna's pine forests and ski slopes, has ten contrade strung along the Mareneve road (SP 59/IV) between the town at about 550 m and the upper DOC limit; the north and north-east sides are the wettest of the mountain, with up to about 1,200 mm of rain a year according to the disciplinare.

it-etna-allegracore-randazzo.summary: Allegracore ('happy heart') runs from the Alcantara river up to the SP 89 near Randazzo. Fattorie Romeo del Castello, the estate of Chiara Vigo, is here: in 1981 a lava flow came down the mountain and stopped at the edge of the family's vineyards, leaving a wall of black rock beside old vines. Its Etna Rosso is called Allegracore.
it-etna-allegracore-randazzo.terroir: North slope near Randazzo, from the Alcantara valley to the SP 89, roughly 650 to 750 m; old lava soils next to the 1981 flow.
it-etna-allegracore-randazzo.nerd_note: Romeo del Castello's vineyards survived the 1981 eruption by metres; the flow is now part of the landscape the wines are named after.

it-etna-arcuria-castiglione-di-sicilia.summary:
Arcuria (often written Arcurìa) lies between the SP 7-II and the Circumetnea just east of the SP 7-III, below Passopisciaro. Graci, Alberto Graci's estate in Passopisciaro (vineyards from 600 to 1,000 m in five contrade), names its Rosso and Bianco Arcurìa after it; they are benchmarks for a restrained, low-intervention Etna. Calcagno, a small family estate in Passopisciaro, also bottles an Arcurìa.

Lower than the famous contrade above the SS 120, Arcuria ripens earlier but keeps freshness from the north-slope nights.
it-etna-arcuria-castiglione-di-sicilia.terroir: North slope, below the Circumetnea (cadastral sheet 21), roughly 600 to 700 m; sandy volcanic soils on gentle terraces.

it-etna-barbabecchi-castiglione-di-sicil.summary:
Barbabecchi is a high, remote contrada above Montedolce, bounded by the Collebbasso and Dagrobosco roads, and the home of some of Etna's most extreme vineyards. Frank Cornelissen's Magma, the Belgian's cult Nerello, comes from ungrafted alberelli more than a century old at about 910 m here, picked late and fermented without additions; Graci also bottles a Barbabecchi from very old vines.

At this height the growing season is short and cool, and acidity stays high even in warm vintages.
it-etna-barbabecchi-castiglione-di-sicil.terroir: Upper north slope (cadastral sheet 77), around 900 m and above, close to the upper limit of viticulture; sandy, pumice-rich young soils on terraces.
it-etna-barbabecchi-castiglione-di-sicil.nerd_note: Cornelissen labels Magma as Terre Siciliane IGT, so one of the most famous wines from an official Etna contrada carries neither the DOC nor the contrada name in the regulated way.

Barley and wheat were grown at this height before vines, a reminder that the upper slope was once mixed farmland. Randazzo, the medieval lava-stone town at the north-western end of the DOC (about 750 m), has 25 contrade between the Alcantara valley and the 800 m contour that closes the denomination on this side.
it-etna-bocca-d-orzo.terroir: North slope, 750 to 800 m; young volcanic soils.

Cottanera makes an Etna Bianco from Carricante grown here, fermented and aged in concrete and cask, proof that the north slope's higher sites can carry whites as well as Nerello.

it-etna-calderara-sottana-randazzo.summary:
Calderara Sottana ('lower Calderara') is the part of the Calderara district that lies below the SS 120, between the state road and the old railway and SP 89, running east to the Castiglione border. With Feudo di Mezzo across the boundary it is the classic mid-slope cru of the north side, roughly 500 to 700 m.

Tenuta delle Terre Nere, whose cellar is in the Calderara district, bottles Calderara Sottana as one of its original crus, plus 'Prephylloxera La Vigna di Don Peppino', from a small plot of ungrafted vines well over a century old. Girolamo Russo works a hectare at about 700 m, including 65-year-old vines and young ones propagated from them, on older pumice; Benanti also bottles a Contrada Calderara Sottana.

Lower and a little warmer than the contrade above the road, it tends to give darker, fuller Nerello Mascalese with a firm frame.

it-etna-calderara-sottana-randazzo.nerd_note: 'Sottana' means lower: Calderara (above the SS 120) and Calderara Sottana (below it) are separate contrade in the disciplinare, and the state road is literally the line between them.

it-etna-caselle-milo.summary:
Caselle lies just north of Milo village, between the Viale della Regione, Via Fornaci and the Finaita royal track, at roughly 750 to 950 m on the east slope. It is the source of Benanti's Pietra Marina, the Etna Bianco Superiore that showed how long Carricante can age: from old alberelli, it is lean, saline and citrusy when young and turns honeyed and petrol-scented, like mature Riesling, after a decade.

Milo is the only commune where Etna Bianco Superiore (at least 80% Carricante) may be made, and Caselle is one of its most prized sites: high, facing the Ionian Sea, cool and wet. Pietradolce also sources Carricante here, at about 850 m.
it-etna-caselle-milo.terroir: East slope, about 750 to 950 m above Milo, facing the sea. Sandy volcanic soils; high rainfall (the east and north-east sides are the wettest of the mountain) and sea breezes.
it-etna-caselle-milo.nerd_note: Benanti's Pietra Marina is named after a place, but not this one: there is an official contrada called Pietra Marina in Castiglione di Sicilia, on the north slope, which has nothing to do with the wine.

it-etna-cavaliere-santa-maria-di-licodia.summary:
Cavaliere is the only contrada of Santa Maria di Licodia and the north-western anchor of the whole DOC: the boundary starts at Casale Brancato at 1,000 m in Contrada Somatorie and runs past the archaeological site of Tre Cisterne, with the Licodia gully to the west. Here on the dry south-west flank vines reach about 1,000 m.

Benanti makes both a Contrada Cavaliere Etna Rosso and a Bianco from high vineyards here, and Feudo Cavaliere, the Platania family estate, farms high vineyards in the contrada. Sunny days, very cold nights and little rain give wines of fine acidity.
it-etna-cavaliere-santa-maria-di-licodia.terroir: South-west slope, roughly 800 to 1,000 m. Dry (about 600 mm a year), with strong day-night swings; sandy, stony volcanic soils.
it-etna-cavaliere-santa-maria-di-licodia.nerd_note: Cavaliere is a single contrada for an entire commune, while Castiglione di Sicilia has 46: the 2011 list reflected which growers asked for names, not a uniform survey of the mountain.

it-etna-dafara-galluzzo-castiglione-di-s.summary:
Dafara Galluzzo lies just above the SS 120 at Rovittello, between the Vitalba and Battiati roads and the Sciara-Picciolo track. Benanti, the Viagrande house that relaunched Etna in the 1990s, bottles a Contrada Dafara Galluzzo Etna Rosso from alberelli on small terraces with dry lava-stone walls, some of them old and ungrafted.

Benanti describes the soils as fine, gravelly volcanic material from the 'Ancient Mongibello' phase of the volcano, with a mildly humid north-slope climate: a site for perfumed, medium-bodied Nerello rather than power.
it-etna-dafara-galluzzo-castiglione-di-s.terroir: North slope at Rovittello, above the SS 120 (cadastral sheet 89). Fine-grained gravelly soils from ancient lavas; alberello on terraces.
it-etna-dafara-galluzzo-castiglione-di-s.nerd_note: Benanti's contrada series pairs this north-slope Dafara Galluzzo with Contrada Cavaliere on the south-west slope and Monte Serra on the south-east, a neat way to taste three sides of the mountain from one producer.

it-etna-feudo-di-mezzo-castiglione-di-si.name: Feudo di Mezzo

it-etna-feudo-di-mezzo-castiglione-di-si.summary:
The 'middle fief' is the band of the north slope just below the SS 120 around Passopisciaro, running from the Randazzo border east to the SP 7-III, between the SP 89 below and the state road above. It is one of the names that built the reputation of modern Etna: almost every pioneer of the 2000s bought or rented old bush vines here.

Girolamo Russo farms 1.3 ha of mostly century-old alberelli inherited from his grandfather, in two parcels at 630 and 670 m near the top of the contrada; the two sit on lava from different eruptions, one of them a clay-rich soil from a 17th-century flow, and the wine is juicy and red-fruited. Tenuta delle Terre Nere bottles its Feudo di Mezzo as 'Il Quadro delle Rose', Frank Cornelissen's Munjebel FM comes from here, Calcagno makes a Feudo di Mezzo from its small family holding, and Cottanera bottles both a contrada wine and a single plot, Vigna Iannazzo. Planeta's Etna winery also sits in the contrada.

Lower and a little warmer than the contrade above the road, Feudo di Mezzo tends to give rounder, more generous Nerello Mascalese than Guardiola or Rampante, while keeping the north slope's perfume and fine tannin.
it-etna-feudo-di-mezzo-castiglione-di-si.terroir: North slope, roughly 600 to 700 m, below the SS 120 (cadastral sheet 20). Old lava flows weathered into dark sandy loams with pumice and some clay; mostly south- to north-facing gentle terraces. North-slope climate: wide day-night swings and, according to the disciplinare, the slope's annual rainfall of up to about 1,200 mm on the north and north-east sides.
it-etna-feudo-di-mezzo-castiglione-di-si.nerd_note: Terre Nere's 'Il Quadro delle Rose' and Russo's Feudo di Mezzo come from the same contrada but different lava: Russo has pointed out that his two parcels a few metres apart in altitude sit on soils from separate eruptions, which is exactly why contrada boundaries cannot be read as uniform terroirs.

it-etna-guardiola-castiglione-di-sicilia.summary:
Guardiola is one of the highest and most famous contrade of the north slope, a steep run of terraces between the Guardiola torrent and the Passopisciaro-Collebbasso road, climbing to around 1,000 m. Andrea Franchetti based Passopisciaro here in 2000 (the estate's address is Contrada Guardiola) and bottled its Nerello as 'Contrada G'; his Chardonnay, Passobianco, comes from the same high ground. Tenuta delle Terre Nere also bottles a Guardiola.

Height is everything here: picking comes late, and wines from sites this high tend to be pale, lifted and taut rather than broad.
it-etna-guardiola-castiglione-di-sicilia.terroir: North slope, about 800 to 1,000 m, on cadastral sheet 61 south of the Panebianco-Guardiola road. Loose, sandy volcanic soils on terraces held by dry-stone lava walls; strong day-night swings and harvests that can run to late October.
it-etna-guardiola-castiglione-di-sicilia.nerd_note: Franchetti labelled his single-contrada wines (C, G, P, R, S) as Terre Siciliane IGT rather than Etna DOC, so the most famous Guardiola bottling does not carry the Etna name at all.

it-etna-marchesa-castiglione-di-sicilia.summary:
Marchesa lies above the SS 120 between the Panebianco-Guardiola road and the Marchesa road, next to Guardiola and Rampante in the heart of the high north slope. The disciplinare uses it as a landmark for the DOC's upper edge: the boundary runs along the 800 m contour through the contrade Pino, Sciara Nuova and Marchesa before entering the 1911 lava flow.

So Marchesa is a top-of-the-zone contrada, where Nerello Mascalese ripens late and keeps its acidity; above it the land turns to woods and young lava.
it-etna-marchesa-castiglione-di-sicilia.terroir: North slope, upper band up to the DOC limit at about 800 m (cadastral sheet 61), south of the SS 120. Sandy volcanic soils; cool nights and late harvests.
it-etna-marchesa-castiglione-di-sicilia.nerd_note: The 1911 eruption opened a line of craters on the north flank; its lava now forms the DOC boundary just east of Marchesa.

it-etna-monte-serra-viagrande.summary:
Monte Serra is an extinct cinder cone above Viagrande, on the south-east flank a few kilometres north of Catania, and Benanti's home ground: the family relaunched the Etna DOC from here in the late 1980s and 1990s. Benanti's Contrada Monte Serra Etna Rosso and its long-standing Serra della Contessa come from vines on the cone's terraced slopes of ash and lapilli.

Lower, warmer and drier than the north slope, the south-east side gives Nerello with riper fruit and softer edges, and the cone's sandy soils keep it fragrant.
it-etna-monte-serra-viagrande.terroir: South-east slope, about 450 to 550 m, on the flanks of an extinct cone; loose ash and lapilli; warm, with sea influence.

it-etna-moscamento-castiglione-di-sicili.summary:
Moscamento lies below the SS 120 on the east side of Castiglione, its edges set by the lava flow of 1911, the eruption that opened a line of craters on the north flank. It is a textbook case of how much soil can change inside one contrada: Tenuta di Fessina's parcel, at about 640 m and facing north-east, has thick, iron-rich basaltic soil in the upper part and some 8 m of deep sandy clay lower down.

Fessina's Il Musmeci, its flagship Etna Rosso, comes from vines planted in 1921 and 1932 here; the estate shortened macerations to 12 to 14 days and capped fermentation temperatures for a more transparent style.
it-etna-moscamento-castiglione-di-sicili.terroir: North slope, about 600 to 650 m, below the SS 120 (cadastral sheet 82). Iron-oxide-rich basalt soils above, deep sandy clay below; bordered by the 1911 flow.
it-etna-moscamento-castiglione-di-sicili.nerd_note: Old-vine Moscamento survives a few metres from the 1911 lava, which buried the neighbouring land: on Etna the youngest rock and the oldest vines can share a boundary.

Linguaglossa, the north-east gateway to Etna's pine forests and ski slopes, has ten contrade strung along the Mareneve road (SP 59/IV) between the town at about 550 m and the upper DOC limit; the north and north-east sides are the wettest of the mountain, with up to about 1,200 mm of rain a year according to the disciplinare.

it-etna-rampante-castiglione-di-sicilia.summary:
Rampante ('climbing') is the contrada east of Marchesa above the SS 120, bounded by the Rampante road on the east and south. Its upper vineyards reach roughly 1,000 m, among the highest on the north slope, and many of its bush vines are very old and ungrafted.

Passopisciaro's 'Contrada R' comes from the high Rampante terraces, Pietradolce (whose north-slope vineyards run from 650 to 950 m) bottles a Contrada Rampante, and Tasca d'Almerita's Tascante estate makes one too. High, late-ripening sites like these tend to give pale, high-toned Nerello with firm acidity.
it-etna-rampante-castiglione-di-sicilia.terroir: North slope, upper band from about 750 m to about 1,000 m (cadastral sheet 62), south of the SS 120. Sandy, stony volcanic soils with pumice, very low in clay; terraces with dry-stone lava walls.
it-etna-rampante-castiglione-di-sicilia.nerd_note: Three well-known estates bottle the same name side by side: Passopisciaro (as 'Contrada R', labelled IGT), Pietradolce and Tascante, a ready-made comparative tasting of one contrada.

it-etna-rapilli.summary: 'Lapilli' names the small volcanic gravel that blankets much of Etna; this Biancavilla contrada sits on such loose, coarse tephra on the dry south-west flank. Biancavilla, founded by Albanian refugees in the late 15th century, lies on the south-west flank; its contrade sit in the DOC band between the 600 m and 1,000 m contours, where the disciplinare records the mountain's lowest rainfall (about 600 mm) and late ripening with wide day-night swings.

it-etna-san-lorenzo.summary:
San Lorenzo lies just south of Randazzo village, between the SS 120 and the SP 230, at about 700 to 800 m, the far western end of the classic north-slope vineyards. Its soil is unusual for Etna: calcium-rich, sub-alkaline and pebbly, with mother rock breaking the surface, which Giuseppe Russo attributes to a more explosive eruption.

Russo's San Lorenzo, first bottled in 2005 from vines planted on wide terraces some 80 years ago (his father Girolamo bought them in 1991), is his richest single-contrada wine; he also makes Piano delle Colombe from a 0.6 ha parcel that ripens earlier. Several other producers bottle San Lorenzo, and the lower, middle and upper parts of the contrada give distinctly different wines.
it-etna-san-lorenzo.terroir: North slope, about 700 to 800 m on the outskirts of Randazzo. Pebbly, calcium-rich, sub-alkaline volcanic soils with outcropping rock; wide terraces.
it-etna-san-lorenzo.nerd_note: Russo's 0.6 ha Piano delle Colombe has been bottled separately in only a handful of vintages: a single contrada can hold sub-plots with their own ripening calendar.

it-etna-santo-spirito-castiglione-di-sic.summary:
Santo Spirito climbs from the SS 120 above Feudo di Mezzo toward the high north slope, bounded by the Randazzo border on the west and the Panebianco-Guardiola road on the south and east. It is one of the best-known contrade on north-slope labels.

Tenuta delle Terre Nere made Santo Spirito one of its four original crus, from terraces of old vines. Anima Etnea, bought by the Tuscan Moretti family in 2010, works 1.2 ha of 90-year-old vines on a terrace at about 650 m and 7.5 ha of new plantings at 800 m in a natural amphitheatre formed by a lava flow; its Animantico comes from the old vines, Animardente blends the parcels.

Altitude and the open bowl give slower ripening than in Feudo di Mezzo just below, and wines with more lift and grip.
it-etna-santo-spirito-castiglione-di-sic.terroir: North slope, about 650 to 800 m, above the SS 120 on cadastral sheets 36, 37 and 61. Sandy volcanic soils on terraces and in a lava-formed amphitheatre; cooler nights than the contrade below the road.
it-etna-santo-spirito-castiglione-di-sic.nerd_note: Anima Etnea's upper vineyard is planted inside a bowl left by a lava flow, so the same contrada holds both 90-year-old terraces and a modern amphitheatre 150 m higher.

it-etna-sciara-nuova.summary:
'New lava flow' (sciara is Sicilian for a lava field) is a thin strip at the very top of Randazzo's DOC land, between the 765 m and 800 m contours, from Calderara east to the Castiglione border. The disciplinare uses it as a landmark of the DOC's upper edge.

Andrea Franchetti's Passopisciaro bottles 'Contrada S' from Sciaranuova, and Tasca d'Almerita's Tascante makes a Contrada Sciaranuova. Because the DOC stops at 800 m here, the contrada's legal strip is narrow, but Sciaranuova vineyards continue upslope beyond the line; under the DOCG proposal voted in 2023, contrada wines would face lower yields and minimum vine ages. Randazzo, the medieval lava-stone town at the north-western end of the DOC (about 750 m), has 25 contrade between the Alcantara valley and the 800 m contour that closes the denomination on this side.
it-etna-sciara-nuova.terroir: North slope, 765 to 800 m inside the DOC (vineyards continue higher). Young, coarse lava with thin soils and plenty of stones; cool and late.
it-etna-sciara-nuova.nerd_note: The disciplinare spells it Sciara Nuova, producers write Sciaranuova; either way the name tells you the lava here is younger than in the contrade below.

The name records how long vines have been grown in the valley bottom.
it-etna-vignagrande-castiglione-di-sicil.terroir: Alcantara valley floor and lower slope (cadastral sheet 7); alluvial and older volcanic soils.

it-etna-volpare.summary: A small contrada in Milo village between Via Etnea, Via Mazzini, Via Salice and Via Madonna delle Grazie, south of the Cacocciola stream. (Soave also has a UGA called Volpare; the name, 'fox land', is common in Italy.)
it-etna-volpare.terroir: East slope, Milo village, roughly 700 m.

it-etna-zottorinotto-castiglione-di-sici.name: Zottorinotto
it-etna-zottorinotto-castiglione-di-sici.grapes: Nerello Mascalese (at least 80% in Etna Rosso and Rosato) with Nerello Cappuccio; Carricante (at least 60%, 80% for Bianco Superiore) with Catarratto for the whites
it-etna-zottorinotto-castiglione-di-sici.summary:
Zottorinotto lies on the north slope at Solicchiata, bounded by the SS 120 and the Solicchiata road, with the Malpasso road to the west. It is best known through Cottanera, the Cambria family estate, which owns a 4.5 ha historic vineyard here: ungrafted vines with an average age of about 85 years, at around 800 m on sandy lava. The estate used it as the source of the massal selection for its other plantings, and its Etna Rosso Riserva from the contrada (spelled Zottorinoto on the label), first produced in 2011, is one of the reference long-aged Nerellos of the north slope. Pietradolce also farms vines in the contrada.

Old, ungrafted alberelli on loose lava sand are exactly what made Etna's contrade famous: the vines' genetic material is as much a part of the site as the soil.
it-etna-zottorinotto-castiglione-di-sici.terroir: North slope at Solicchiata (cadastral sheets 42 and 43); sandy lava; Cottanera's vineyard at about 800 m.
it-etna-zottorinotto-castiglione-di-sici.nerd_note: The label spelling Zottorinoto (one t) differs from the disciplinare's Zottorinotto, a common Etna problem: dialect names were written down in several ways before the 2011 list fixed them.

Like its neighbours it offers cool, late-ripening sites for Nerello Mascalese.
it-etna-zucconero-castiglione-di-sicilia.terroir: North slope, above the SS 120 (cadastral sheets 68 and 73); volcanic sands at roughly 750 to 900 m.

it-friuli-colli-orientali-cialla.name: Cialla
it-friuli-colli-orientali-cialla.grapes: Ribolla Gialla, Verduzzo Friulano, Refosco dal Peduncolo Rosso, Schioppettino; Bianco and Rosso blends (Picolit allowed in the Bianco)
it-friuli-colli-orientali-cialla.summary: Cialla is a small, steep, wooded valley in the commune of Prepotto, close to the Slovenian border, and the most demanding subzone in Friuli. It exists largely because of one family: Paolo and Dina Rapuzzi bought land here in 1970, founded Ronchi di Cialla, and helped rescue Schioppettino from near-extinction. The subzone allows only native grapes (Ribolla Gialla, Verduzzo Friulano, Refosco and Schioppettino, plus Bianco and Rosso blends), with yields of 8 t/ha for whites and just 6 t/ha for reds, and long minimum release dates: January of the third year after the harvest for Refosco and Schioppettino. Wines must be bottled in glass of up to 5 litres with cork; Riserva needs four years.
it-friuli-colli-orientali-cialla.terroir: A narrow side valley north of Prepotto, from about 200 m up to the road to Castelmonte; ponca (marl and sandstone flysch) terraces surrounded by woods; cool, wet and late.
it-friuli-colli-orientali-cialla.nerd_note: Cialla's annex is the only one in the Colli Orientali that requires a cork stopper, and it allows small barrels for ageing.
it-friuli-colli-orientali-cialla.classification: Sottozona of Friuli Colli Orientali DOC with its own annex: native varieties only, 6 t/ha for reds and 8 t/ha for whites, small barrels allowed, Riserva after four years from 1 January after the harvest.

it-friuli-colli-orientali-prepotto.name: Schioppettino di Prepotto
it-friuli-colli-orientali-prepotto.grapes: Schioppettino at least 85% (95% for vineyards planted after the rules were published)
it-friuli-colli-orientali-prepotto.summary:
Prepotto, the commune that runs along the Judrio river on the Slovenian border, is Schioppettino's homeland, and this subzone is reserved for that one grape. Schioppettino (Ribolla Nera) gives medium-bodied, peppery, wild-berry reds with fresh acidity; the name may refer to the 'little gunshot' of its crisp berries or of the lively wines once refermented in bottle. The rules exclude the Cialla valley (which has its own subzone) and damp or shady land, require hand harvesting, at least 4,500 vines per hectare, 7 t/ha, 12% potential alcohol and at least 12 months in wood; release is from September of the second year after the harvest, and the Riserva from September of the fourth.

Producers in the commune include Vigna Petrussa, Ronco dei Pini, La Viarte, Grillo Iole and Colli di Poianis.
it-friuli-colli-orientali-prepotto.terroir: Ponca (marl and sandstone flysch) hills along the Judrio valley, about 100 to 300 m; mild, with cool air from the Julian Prealps.
it-friuli-colli-orientali-prepotto.nerd_note: Superiore is explicitly not allowed for Schioppettino di Prepotto, and the wine must go into a dark Bordeaux bottle.
it-friuli-colli-orientali-prepotto.classification: Sottozona of Friuli Colli Orientali DOC for Schioppettino only, from the commune of Prepotto outside Cialla.

it-friuli-colli-orientali-refosco-di-fae.name: Refosco di Faedis
it-friuli-colli-orientali-refosco-di-fae.village: Faedis, Nimis, Attimis, Torreano, Povoletto, Tarcento
it-friuli-colli-orientali-refosco-di-fae.grapes: Refosco Nostrano at least 85% (95% in new vineyards)
it-friuli-colli-orientali-refosco-di-fae.summary: The northern subzone of the Colli Orientali, for Refosco Nostrano, a local Refosco distinct from the more common Refosco dal Peduncolo Rosso, grown in the hills of Faedis, Nimis, Attimis, Torreano, Povoletto and Tarcento under the Julian Prealps. The rules allow 8 t/ha with at least 4,000 vines per hectare, and a Riserva after three years. The wines are deep-coloured, high in acidity and wild-berried.
it-friuli-colli-orientali-refosco-di-fae.terroir: Northern Colli Orientali, ponca and marl hills toward the Prealps; cooler and wetter than the southern hills.
it-friuli-colli-orientali-refosco-di-fae.classification: Sottozona of Friuli Colli Orientali DOC for Refosco Nostrano.

it-friuli-colli-orientali-rosazzo.name: Rosazzo
it-friuli-colli-orientali-rosazzo.village: Manzano, Corno di Rosazzo, San Giovanni al Natisone
it-friuli-colli-orientali-rosazzo.grapes: Pignolo (Pignolo di Rosazzo) or Ribolla Gialla (Ribolla Gialla di Rosazzo), at least 85%
it-friuli-colli-orientali-rosazzo.summary:
Two subzones of the Colli Orientali share one small area around the Abbey of Rosazzo, straddling Manzano, Corno di Rosazzo and San Giovanni al Natisone: Pignolo di Rosazzo and Ribolla Gialla di Rosazzo. The abbey's vineyards are where Pignolo, a dark, tannic and long-lived native red, survived near-extinction in the late 20th century; the rules call it the most aristocratic wine of the denomination, able to live well beyond ten years, and it may only be released from 1 November of the fourth year after the harvest. Ribolla Gialla di Rosazzo is the fresh, citrusy, tightly knit native white of the same hills. Both are capped at 8 t/ha with at least 3,500 vines per hectare.

The separate Rosazzo DOCG, for white blends led by Friulano, covers a wider area around the abbey; Livio Felluga, which manages the abbey's vineyards, Ronco delle Betulle and Le Vigne di Zamò are key names.
it-friuli-colli-orientali-rosazzo.terroir: A compact block of ponca hills around the Abbey of Rosazzo, about 100 to 200 m; well ventilated, warm for the Colli Orientali.
it-friuli-colli-orientali-rosazzo.nerd_note: Two different subzones (one red, one white) share exactly the same boundary, drawn along streams and farm tracks around the abbey.
it-friuli-colli-orientali-rosazzo.classification: Area of the Friuli Colli Orientali sottozone 'Pignolo di Rosazzo' and 'Ribolla Gialla di Rosazzo', each with its own annex; distinct from the Rosazzo DOCG.

it-lago-di-caldaro-classico.name: Lago di Caldaro classico
it-lago-di-caldaro-classico.summary: The classico heartland of Lago di Caldaro (Kalterersee), the light, cherry-scented Schiava that was once the everyday red of the Habsburg empire. The classico zone surrounds the lake and the villages of Kaltern and Eppan; a 'scelto' or 'Auslese' version must reach higher ripeness.
it-lago-di-caldaro-classico.terroir: Morainic gravel and limestone debris around the lake, warm and sheltered. The official boundary, in Appiano/Eppan and Caldaro/Kaltern, reaches from about 210 to 810 m (terrain model).
it-lago-di-caldaro-classico.nerd_note: Schiava (Vernatsch) covered most of Alto Adige's vineyards until the 1980s; it now covers under a tenth.

it-montepulciano-d-abruzzo-alto-tirino.name: Alto Tirino
it-montepulciano-d-abruzzo-alto-tirino.village: Capestrano, Ofena, Villa Santa Lucia degli Abruzzi
it-montepulciano-d-abruzzo-alto-tirino.summary: A small mountain basin in the province of L'Aquila: the plain of Ofena, nicknamed 'the oven of Abruzzo' for its summer heat, ringed by mountains, with surrounding slopes in Capestrano and Villa Santa Lucia. The subzone caps yields at 9 t/ha and requires 12 months of ageing; vineyards must lie between about 300 and 600 m. Hot days and very cold nights give deep colour and fresh acidity.
it-montepulciano-d-abruzzo-alto-tirino.terroir: Intermontane basin of Ofena at 300 to 600 m, below the Gran Sasso; calcareous gravels and clays; extreme day-night swings.
it-montepulciano-d-abruzzo-alto-tirino.nerd_note: Ofena's basin is called 'il forno d'Abruzzo', the oven of Abruzzo, though it lies among the highest mountains of the Apennines.
it-montepulciano-d-abruzzo-alto-tirino.classification: Sottozona of Montepulciano d'Abruzzo DOC with its own annex (version of the rules in force in early 2025). The original five subzones (Casauria, Terre dei Vestini, Alto Tirino, Terre dei Peligni, Teate) allow a base wine and Riserva from tightly drawn areas.

it-montepulciano-d-abruzzo-colline-pesca.name: Colline Pescaresi
it-montepulciano-d-abruzzo-colline-pesca.village: The wine communes of the province of Pescara
it-montepulciano-d-abruzzo-colline-pesca.summary: The provincial subzone for Pescara, covering both the Vestini hills and the Casauria valley. Superiore and Riserva only. The reform built a pyramid: plain Montepulciano d'Abruzzo at the base (released from 1 February after the harvest), subzones with Superiore and Riserva above it, and the separate DOCGs (Colline Teramane, Terre Tollesi or Tullum, and since 2025 Casauria) at the top. Much of Abruzzo's Montepulciano is still trained on the traditional pergola abruzzese (tendone), though espaliers are spreading.
it-montepulciano-d-abruzzo-colline-pesca.terroir: Pescara hills from the coast to the Gran Sasso and Maiella foothills, up to 600 m.
it-montepulciano-d-abruzzo-colline-pesca.classification: Sottozona of Montepulciano d'Abruzzo DOC added in the reform that created three provincial subzones and one communal one, reserved for 'superiore' and 'riserva' wines: at least 90% Montepulciano, vineyards no higher than 600 m, Riserva aged 24 months with six in wood.

it-montepulciano-d-abruzzo-san-martino-s.name: San Martino sulla Marrucina
it-montepulciano-d-abruzzo-san-martino-s.summary: The only communal subzone: the hilltop village of San Martino sulla Marrucina at the foot of the Maiella in the province of Chieti, home of Masciarelli, the estate Gianni Masciarelli founded in 1981 that put modern Abruzzo on the map. Up to 12 t/ha, 12 months of ageing with six in wood, at least 4,000 vines per hectare.
it-montepulciano-d-abruzzo-san-martino-s.terroir: Hills facing the Maiella in the province of Chieti, around 400 m; clay-limestone, with cool air from the mountain.
it-montepulciano-d-abruzzo-san-martino-s.nerd_note: A whole subzone for one small hill village owes much to one estate: Masciarelli, maker of Villa Gemma and the Marina Cvetic range.
it-montepulciano-d-abruzzo-san-martino-s.classification: Sottozona of Montepulciano d'Abruzzo DOC added in the reform that created three provincial subzones and one communal one, reserved for 'superiore' and 'riserva' wines: at least 90% Montepulciano, vineyards no higher than 600 m, Riserva aged 24 months with six in wood.

it-montepulciano-d-abruzzo-teate.name: Teate
it-montepulciano-d-abruzzo-teate.village: About 60 communes of the province of Chieti (Chieti, Ortona, Lanciano, Vasto, Tollo, Guardiagrele and others)
it-montepulciano-d-abruzzo-teate.summary: Teate is the Latin name of Chieti, and the subzone covers about a third of the province, the heart of Abruzzo's wine production: coastal hills from the Foro to the Trigno, then the inner and foothill hills up to the Maiella. At least 90% Montepulciano, 11 t/ha and 21 months of ageing with nine in wood. Chieti province grows most of Abruzzo's Montepulciano, much of it through large cooperatives such as those of Tollo, Ortona and the Frentano coast.
it-montepulciano-d-abruzzo-teate.terroir: Coastal and inland clay-limestone hills of the province of Chieti up to 600 m; warm, with sea breezes and Maiella air.
it-montepulciano-d-abruzzo-teate.classification: Sottozona of Montepulciano d'Abruzzo DOC with its own annex (version of the rules in force in early 2025). The original five subzones (Casauria, Terre dei Vestini, Alto Tirino, Terre dei Peligni, Teate) allow a base wine and Riserva from tightly drawn areas.

it-montepulciano-d-abruzzo-terre-aquilan.name: Terre Aquilane
it-montepulciano-d-abruzzo-terre-aquilan.village: Ofena, Capestrano, Sulmona, Pratola Peligna, Vittorito, Raiano, Fossa and the other wine communes of the province of L'Aquila
it-montepulciano-d-abruzzo-terre-aquilan.summary: The provincial subzone for the mountain province of L'Aquila (also 'Terre de L'Aquila'), joining the Ofena basin of Alto Tirino, the Valle Peligna and the Aterno and Roveto valleys. Superiore and Riserva only. The reform built a pyramid: plain Montepulciano d'Abruzzo at the base (released from 1 February after the harvest), subzones with Superiore and Riserva above it, and the separate DOCGs (Colline Teramane, Terre Tollesi or Tullum, and since 2025 Casauria) at the top. Much of Abruzzo's Montepulciano is still trained on the traditional pergola abruzzese (tendone), though espaliers are spreading.
it-montepulciano-d-abruzzo-terre-aquilan.terroir: Intermontane basins and valleys of L'Aquila province, 300 to 600 m; continental climate with very wide day-night swings.
it-montepulciano-d-abruzzo-terre-aquilan.classification: Sottozona of Montepulciano d'Abruzzo DOC added in the reform that created three provincial subzones and one communal one, reserved for 'superiore' and 'riserva' wines: at least 90% Montepulciano, vineyards no higher than 600 m, Riserva aged 24 months with six in wood.

it-montepulciano-d-abruzzo-terre-dei-pel.name: Terre dei Peligni
it-montepulciano-d-abruzzo-terre-dei-pel.village: Sulmona, Pratola Peligna, Vittorito, Raiano, Corfinio, Prezza, Bugnara, Introdacqua, Pacentro, Pettorano sul Gizio, Roccacasale
it-montepulciano-d-abruzzo-terre-dei-pel.summary: The Valle Peligna around Sulmona, an inland basin between the Maiella and the Velino-Sirente, with vineyards between about 300 and 400 m. Up to 10 t/ha and 24 months of ageing with nine in wood. Cooler and more continental than the coast, it gives firmer, more aromatic Montepulciano. Pietrantonj at Vittorito and Praesidium at Prezza are the reference estates.
it-montepulciano-d-abruzzo-terre-dei-pel.terroir: Intermontane basin of the Valle Peligna, 300 to 400 m (vines up to 600 m); alluvial gravels and clay-limestone slopes; continental climate.
it-montepulciano-d-abruzzo-terre-dei-pel.nerd_note: Sulmona, at the centre of the subzone, was the birthplace of Ovid.
it-montepulciano-d-abruzzo-terre-dei-pel.classification: Sottozona of Montepulciano d'Abruzzo DOC with its own annex (version of the rules in force in early 2025). The original five subzones (Casauria, Terre dei Vestini, Alto Tirino, Terre dei Peligni, Teate) allow a base wine and Riserva from tightly drawn areas.

it-montepulciano-d-abruzzo-terre-dei-ves.name: Terre dei Vestini
it-montepulciano-d-abruzzo-terre-dei-ves.village: Loreto Aprutino, Pianella, Penne, Moscufo, Città Sant'Angelo, Collecorvino, Spoltore and other communes of the province of Pescara
it-montepulciano-d-abruzzo-terre-dei-ves.summary: The coastal and inner hills of the province of Pescara between the Adriatic and the Gran Sasso, named after the ancient Vestini people. Vineyards lie mostly between 200 and 500 m; the subzone allows up to 10 t/ha and requires 18 months of ageing with nine in wood. The area around Loreto Aprutino is one of Abruzzo's most celebrated for Montepulciano: Valentini's legendary cellar is here, and Torre dei Beati is a leading estate.
it-montepulciano-d-abruzzo-terre-dei-ves.terroir: Clay-limestone hills from near the sea to the Gran Sasso foothills, 200 to 500 m.
it-montepulciano-d-abruzzo-terre-dei-ves.nerd_note: Loreto Aprutino's Valentini, perhaps Abruzzo's most famous estate, sits inside Terre dei Vestini but does not use the subzone name.
it-montepulciano-d-abruzzo-terre-dei-ves.classification: Sottozona of Montepulciano d'Abruzzo DOC with its own annex (version of the rules in force in early 2025). it-montepulciano-d-abruzzo-terre-di-casa.name: Casauria
it-montepulciano-d-abruzzo-terre-di-casa.village: Tocco da Casauria, Castiglione a Casauria, Bolognano, Popoli, Torre de' Passeri, Alanno and other communes of the province of Pescara
it-montepulciano-d-abruzzo-terre-di-casa.summary: The inland Pescara valley between the Maiella and the Gran Sasso, around the Benedictine abbey of San Clemente a Casauria (founded 871). As a subzone of the DOC (also called Terre di Casauria) it required 100% Montepulciano, at most 9.5 t/ha, vineyards no higher than 600 m and at least 18 months of ageing with nine in wood. In November 2025 the area became its own DOCG, Casauria, Italy's 79th, so the subzone is being superseded. Tiberio, Zaccagnini and Valle Reale are among the producers within its communes.
it-montepulciano-d-abruzzo-terre-di-casa.terroir: Inland, foothill Pescara valley, about 200 to 600 m; clay-limestone and sandy-clay hills; strong day-night swings from the two massifs.
it-montepulciano-d-abruzzo-terre-di-casa.classification: Sottozona of Montepulciano d'Abruzzo DOC with its own annex (version of the rules in force in early 2025). The original five subzones (Casauria, Terre dei Vestini, Alto Tirino, Terre dei Peligni, Teate) allow a base wine and Riserva from tightly drawn areas. Casauria was promoted to a separate DOCG (EU registration 11 November 2025).

it-montepulciano-d-abruzzo-terre-di-chie.name: Terre di Chieti
it-montepulciano-d-abruzzo-terre-di-chie.village: Chieti, Francavilla al Mare, Tollo, Ortona, Lanciano, Vasto, Guardiagrele and the rest of the province's wine communes
it-montepulciano-d-abruzzo-terre-di-chie.summary: One of the provincial subzones created in the reform, covering the province of Chieti, which grows most of Abruzzo's Montepulciano. Only Superiore (released no earlier than 1 October after the harvest) and Riserva (24 months, six in wood, released from 1 January of the third year) may carry the name. The reform built a pyramid: plain Montepulciano d'Abruzzo at the base (released from 1 February after the harvest), subzones with Superiore and Riserva above it, and the separate DOCGs (Colline Teramane, Terre Tollesi or Tullum, and since 2025 Casauria) at the top. Much of Abruzzo's Montepulciano is still trained on the traditional pergola abruzzese (tendone), though espaliers are spreading.
it-montepulciano-d-abruzzo-terre-di-chie.terroir: Clay-limestone hills from the Adriatic to the Maiella, up to 600 m.
it-montepulciano-d-abruzzo-terre-di-chie.classification: Sottozona of Montepulciano d'Abruzzo DOC added in the reform that created three provincial subzones and one communal one, reserved for 'superiore' and 'riserva' wines: at least 90% Montepulciano, vineyards no higher than 600 m, Riserva aged 24 months with six in wood.

it-roero-anime.terroir: Sandy Pliocene hills of Canale; Roero vineyards lie roughly between 150 and 450 m.
it-roero-anime.classification: Unità geografica aggiuntiva (MGA) of Roero DOCG, listed in Annex 2 of the disciplinare: either one of the 18 communes or one of the named frazioni and località whose cadastral parcels are listed in Annex 2B. The name may appear on Roero, Roero Riserva, Roero Arneis and Arneis Riserva when all the grapes come from it; Roero rosso with a geographical mention is released from 1 July of the second year.

it-roero-renesio.name: Renesio
it-roero-renesio.grapes: Nebbiolo (Roero rosso, at least 95%); Arneis (Roero Arneis, at least 95%)
it-roero-renesio.summary: Renesio is a named locality (MGA) in the commune of Canale, the main town of the Roero, in the Borbore valley at the centre of the zone. Its boundary follows the cadastral parcels listed in Annex 2B of the Roero rules. The hill of Renesio is tied to the oldest record of Arneis: a document of 1478 from Canale mentions vines called 'Ranaysii', and the grape's name is often traced to this place. Malvirà's Roero Arneis Renesio keeps the link alive.
it-roero-renesio.terroir: Sandy Pliocene hills of Canale; Roero vineyards lie roughly between 150 and 450 m.
it-roero-renesio.nerd_note: Renesio is split into four MGAs: Renesio itself and Renesio Incisa, Renesio Montorone and Renesio Valbellina.

Its boundary follows the cadastral parcels listed in Annex 2B of the Roero rules. Valmaggiore is a steep, south-facing amphitheatre of loose sand, the most celebrated Nebbiolo site of the Roero. Bruno Giacosa bottled Nebbiolo d'Alba Valmaggiore for many years and Luciano Sandrone of Barolo still does; because the hill is also inside the Nebbiolo d'Alba DOC, many of its best wines carry that name rather than Roero.

it-romagna-bertinoro.name: Bertinoro
it-romagna-bertinoro.grapes: Sangiovese (at least 95% for a sottozona wine)
it-romagna-bertinoro.summary: Bertinoro, the 'balcony of Romagna', is the hill town above Forlimpopoli whose slopes are built on spungone, a yellowish, fossil-rich calcareous sandstone of marine origin. The sottozona's Sangiovese is warm, powerful and saline. Bertinoro also has its own Pagadebit ('pays the debts', from Bombino Bianco). Fattoria Paradiso, Tenuta La Viola, Giovanna Madonia and Celli are among its producers. Bertinoro was traditionally Albana country, and the disciplinare notes that its Sangiovese, discovered more recently, has an important structure that needs fairly long ageing; the poor, calcareous spungone soils also explain the area's affinity for Albana and Bombino Bianco.
it-romagna-bertinoro.terroir: Hills around Bertinoro above the Via Emilia; spungone (calcareous fossil sandstone) and clays, about 100 to 300 m, with sea influence.
it-romagna-bertinoro.nerd_note: Bertinoro's iron 'column of hospitality' in the main square had rings for each noble family; travellers who tied up their horse were guests of that house.
it-romagna-bertinoro.classification: Sottozona of Romagna DOC, one of 16 now listed (the original 12 of 2011 plus Imola, Coriano, San Clemente and Verucchio; San Vicinio has become Mercato Saraceno). A Romagna Sangiovese with a sottozona name needs at least 95% Sangiovese, at most 9 t/ha and 12.5% potential alcohol (13% for Riserva). The Riserva is released only from 1 September of the third year after the harvest, with two months in bottle documented.

it-romagna-brisighella.name: Brisighella
it-romagna-brisighella.grapes: Sangiovese (at least 95% for a sottozona wine)
it-romagna-brisighella.summary: Parts of Brisighella, Faenza and Casola Valsenio in the Lamone valley, where the Vena del Gesso, a long ridge of gypsum, crosses the Apennine foothills. Its sottozona covers Sangiovese and also a Romagna Bianco, and any form of enrichment is forbidden. According to the disciplinare, its particular microclimate also sustains an important olive-oil tradition (Brisighella has its own DOP oil), and the soils near the gypsum ridge, rich in sandstone and clay, give structured, elegant wines with marked floral and fruity notes and good freshness.
it-romagna-brisighella.terroir: Lamone valley hills: calcareous clays, spungone and gypsum near the Vena del Gesso, about 100 to 500 m.
it-romagna-brisighella.classification: Sottozona of Romagna DOC, one of 16 now listed (the original 12 of 2011 plus Imola, Coriano, San Clemente and Verucchio; San Vicinio has become Mercato Saraceno). A Romagna Sangiovese with a sottozona name needs at least 95% Sangiovese, at most 9 t/ha and 12.5% potential alcohol (13% for Riserva). it-romagna-castrocaro.grapes: Sangiovese (at least 95% for a sottozona wine)
it-romagna-castrocaro.summary: The Montone valley around the spa town of Castrocaro Terme and Terra del Sole (the Medici's 16th-century ideal fortress town), up to Dovadola and Rocca San Casciano, plus a strip of Forlì. Sangiovese and a Romagna Bianco are allowed, with enrichment forbidden. This is the 'Romagna Toscana', long under the Grand Duchy of Tuscany, and the disciplinare admits that the subzone owes more to history and local tradition than to any real difference from neighbouring Oriolo.
it-romagna-castrocaro.terroir: Montone valley hills, clays, marl and sandstone, about 100 to 500 m.
it-romagna-castrocaro.classification: Sottozona of Romagna DOC, one of 16 now listed (the original 12 of 2011 plus Imola, Coriano, San Clemente and Verucchio; San Vicinio has become Mercato Saraceno). it-romagna-cesena.grapes: Sangiovese (at least 95% for a sottozona wine)
it-romagna-cesena.summary: The hills of the commune of Cesena in the Savio valley, a Sangiovese-only sottozona of clays and marl with sea influence. Cesena's wines were cited by classical Latin authors, the disciplinare recalls, and its Sangiovese combines real but never excessive structure with clear ripe-cherry fruit: structure and elegance together.
it-romagna-cesena.terroir: Savio valley hills south of Cesena; clays and marl, about 50 to 300 m.
it-romagna-cesena.classification: Sottozona of Romagna DOC, one of 16 now listed (the original 12 of 2011 plus Imola, Coriano, San Clemente and Verucchio; San Vicinio has become Mercato Saraceno). it-romagna-coriano.name: Coriano
it-romagna-coriano.grapes: Sangiovese (at least 95% for a sottozona wine)
it-romagna-coriano.summary: The commune of Coriano plus a strip of Rimini, in the low hills behind the Riviera. San Patrignano, the rehabilitation community whose winery helped prove the area's potential, is in Coriano. Sangiovese was widely grown in the Rimini area until 1860, then abandoned for its low alcohol and later replanted. Coriano covers the land just behind the sea, and the disciplinare credits its grey clays and good exposure with more structured Sangiovese suited to ageing.
it-romagna-coriano.terroir: Low hills a few kilometres from the Adriatic; clays and sands, warm with sea breezes.

it-romagna-imola.name: Imola
it-romagna-imola.village: Fontanelice, Borgo Tossignano, Casalfiumanese, Dozza, Castel San Pietro Terme, Ozzano dell'Emilia
it-romagna-imola.grapes: Sangiovese (at least 95% for a sottozona wine)
it-romagna-imola.summary: The newest western sottozona, in the Santerno and Sillaro valleys above Imola. Records from the late 18th century already describe Sangiovese as typical here, and an 1880 survey made it the second variety of Imola after Albana. The disciplinare backs the claim with numbers: the 2010 farm census counted 3,932 ha of vineyard in the province of Bologna, 1,039 ha (26%) of them Sangiovese, and 70% of that south of the Via Emilia, in the Imola hills.
it-romagna-imola.terroir: Santerno and Sillaro valley hills south of the Via Emilia; clays, sands and spungone.
it-romagna-imola.nerd_note: Dozza, inside the sottozona, houses the Enoteca Regionale dell'Emilia-Romagna in its medieval fortress.
it-romagna-imola.classification: Sottozona of Romagna DOC, one of 16 now listed (the original 12 of 2011 plus Imola, Coriano, San Clemente and Verucchio; San Vicinio has become Mercato Saraceno). The disciplinare describes warm, rich wines with very evident fruit and good structure, and warns that pushing them toward power sacrifices the natural elegance of grape and place.

it-romagna-marzeno.grapes: Sangiovese (at least 95% for a sottozona wine)
it-romagna-marzeno.summary: The Marzeno valley south of Faenza, between the Lamone and Montone valleys. Fattoria Zerbina, whose Pietramora Riserva helped relaunch Romagna Sangiovese in the 1990s, is the reference estate. The disciplinare notes that Marzeno has the first major outcrop of the spungone, the fossil-rich calcareous sandstone that is interbedded here with the blue Plio-Pleistocene clays: rugged land that gives strong wines in which fruit dominates over flowers.

it-romagna-meldola.grapes: Sangiovese (at least 95% for a sottozona wine)
it-romagna-meldola.summary: The Bidente valley around Meldola, adjoining Predappio to the west. A Sangiovese-only sottozona of clay and sandstone hills. The disciplinare notes that the area was farmed in Roman times and that its main exposure, from north-west to north-east, gives fine Sangiovese with a fruity aromatic profile, an unusual case of a subzone defined partly by cool, north-facing slopes.
it-romagna-meldola.terroir: Bidente valley hills around Meldola; clays and sandstone.

it-romagna-mercato-saraceno.name: Mercato Saraceno
it-romagna-mercato-saraceno.village: Mercato Saraceno, Sarsina, Roncofreddo, Sogliano al Rubicone, Cesena
it-romagna-mercato-saraceno.grapes: Sangiovese (at least 95% for a sottozona wine)
it-romagna-mercato-saraceno.summary: The upper Savio valley around Mercato Saraceno and Sarsina (birthplace of the Roman playwright Plautus), formerly called San Vicinio after the valley's patron saint. Besides Sangiovese it protects Romagna Famoso, an aromatic white grape revived in this area, also as spumante. The disciplinare calls this the fullest expression of the Romagna marnoso-arenacea formation; the calcareous 'Celincordia' soils (Haplic Calcisols), especially below 150 to 200 m, have proved the best for Sangiovese, giving balanced wines with sweet tannins. Famoso's revival started here around 2000 from two old rows of vines.
it-romagna-mercato-saraceno.terroir: Upper Savio valley; marl and sandstone hills, up to about 500 m; cooler and more continental.
it-romagna-mercato-saraceno.nerd_note: The sottozona was renamed from San Vicinio to Mercato Saraceno; old labels with the saint's name come from the same hills.
it-romagna-mercato-saraceno.classification: Sottozona of Romagna DOC, one of 16 now listed (the original 12 of 2011 plus Imola, Coriano, San Clemente and Verucchio; San Vicinio has become Mercato Saraceno).
