it-romagna-modigliana.name: Modigliana
it-romagna-modigliana.grapes: Sangiovese (at least 95% for a sottozona wine)
it-romagna-modigliana.summary:
Modigliana is the highest and coolest of Romagna's sottozone, the whole commune at the head of three valleys (Ibola, Acerreta and Tramazzo) in the Apennine foothills. Until 1923 it belonged to Tuscany, and its Sangiovese has something Tuscan about it: taut, austere and long-lived (the disciplinare speaks of firm structure, power and longevity), from the marnoso-arenacea, the sandstone and marl flysch of the northern Apennines, rather than the clays and spungone further down.

A group of growers (Villa Papiano, Il Pratello, Torre San Martino, Mutiliana and others) has made it the most talked-about name in Romagna. The rules are strict: new vineyards need 4,000 vines per hectare, yields stop at 9 t/ha, normal Modigliana may not be sold before 1 September after the harvest, the Riserva not before 1 September of the third year. There is also a Romagna Bianco Modigliana (Trebbiano with up to 40% Chardonnay and Sauvignon).
it-romagna-modigliana.terroir: The whole commune of Modigliana, vineyards from about 150 to 600 m; marnoso-arenacea flysch (sandstone and marl), poor and well drained; cooler and later than the rest of Romagna.
it-romagna-modigliana.nerd_note: Modigliana's three valleys, Ibola, Acerreta and Tramazzo, are increasingly named on labels as a further level of detail.
it-romagna-modigliana.classification: Sottozona of Romagna DOC, one of 16 now listed (the original 12 of 2011 plus Imola, Coriano, San Clemente and Verucchio; San Vicinio has become Mercato Saraceno). A Romagna Sangiovese with a sottozona name needs at least 95% Sangiovese, at most 9 t/ha and 12.5% potential alcohol (13% for Riserva). The Riserva is released only from 1 September of the third year after the harvest, with two months in bottle documented.

it-romagna-oriolo.name: Oriolo
it-romagna-oriolo.grapes: Sangiovese (at least 95% for a sottozona wine)
it-romagna-oriolo.summary: The hills of Oriolo dei Fichi above Faenza, crowned by the 15th-century hexagonal Torre di Oriolo. Besides Sangiovese, the sottozona protects Centesimino, a local aromatic red grape (also called Savignôn rosso) made as a red, Riserva, passito and sparkling rosé. The disciplinare singles out its yellow sands, which surface among clay or silty-clay soils: depending on exposure and the balance of sand and clay, Oriolo gives either structured wines that need time to soften or fruity, floral wines ready sooner.
it-romagna-oriolo.terroir: Low hills above Faenza between the Lamone and Montone, clays and sands, about 100 to 250 m.
it-romagna-oriolo.nerd_note: Centesimino survived in a single Faenza garden and was named after Pietro Pianori, nicknamed 'Centesimino', who propagated it after phylloxera.
it-romagna-oriolo.classification: Sottozona of Romagna DOC, one of 16 now listed (the original 12 of 2011 plus Imola, Coriano, San Clemente and Verucchio; San Vicinio has become Mercato Saraceno). A Romagna Sangiovese with a sottozona name needs at least 95% Sangiovese, at most 9 t/ha and 12.5% potential alcohol (13% for Riserva). The Riserva is released only from 1 September of the third year after the harvest, with two months in bottle documented.

it-romagna-predappio.name: Predappio
it-romagna-predappio.grapes: Sangiovese (at least 95% for a sottozona wine)
it-romagna-predappio.summary: The whole commune of Predappio in the Rabbi valley, south of Forlì. Its slopes of clay and marl with sandstone layers, and a local long-berried biotype of Sangiovese, give very fruity wines with firm, rather austere tannins, as the disciplinare describes them. Fattoria Nicolucci at Predappio Alta, whose Vigna del Generale is one of Romagna's classic Riservas, and Noelia Ricci at the Pandolfa estate lead.
it-romagna-predappio.terroir: Whole commune of Predappio; clay, marl and sandstone hills of the Rabbi valley, about 150 to 450 m.
it-romagna-predappio.classification: Sottozona of Romagna DOC, one of 16 now listed (the original 12 of 2011 plus Imola, Coriano, San Clemente and Verucchio; San Vicinio has become Mercato Saraceno). A Romagna Sangiovese with a sottozona name needs at least 95% Sangiovese, at most 9 t/ha and 12.5% potential alcohol (13% for Riserva). The Riserva is released only from 1 September of the third year after the harvest, with two months in bottle documented.

it-romagna-san-clemente.name: San Clemente
it-romagna-san-clemente.village: San Clemente, Montescudo-Montecolombo, Misano Adriatico, San Giovanni in Marignano, Montefiore Conca, Gemmano, Morciano di Romagna, Saludecio, Mondaino, Montegridolfo
it-romagna-san-clemente.grapes: Sangiovese (at least 95% for a sottozona wine)
it-romagna-san-clemente.summary: The Conca valley hills south of Rimini, excluding the land below the SS 16 coastal road. A Sangiovese-only sottozona on the border with the Marche. The disciplinare describes San Clemente as the hottest part of the Rimini hills, with gypsum and more colourful clays, giving structured wines that keep good acid tension.
it-romagna-san-clemente.terroir: Conca valley hills; clays and sands, warm, close to the sea.
it-romagna-san-clemente.classification: Sottozona of Romagna DOC, one of 16 now listed (the original 12 of 2011 plus Imola, Coriano, San Clemente and Verucchio; San Vicinio has become Mercato Saraceno). A Romagna Sangiovese with a sottozona name needs at least 95% Sangiovese, at most 9 t/ha and 12.5% potential alcohol (13% for Riserva). The Riserva is released only from 1 September of the third year after the harvest, with two months in bottle documented.

it-romagna-serra.name: Serra
it-romagna-serra.grapes: Sangiovese (at least 95% for a sottozona wine)
it-romagna-serra.summary: The Senio valley between Castel Bolognese and Riolo Terme, at the western end of the Ravenna hills. A Sangiovese-only sottozona. The disciplinare calls Serra a historically prized area with a rather continental climate, little moderated by the distant sea, and wines with delicate floral notes and fresh fruit when the vines are well exposed.
it-romagna-serra.terroir: Senio valley hills; calcareous clays and sands, about 100 to 300 m.
it-romagna-serra.classification: Sottozona of Romagna DOC, one of 16 now listed (the original 12 of 2011 plus Imola, Coriano, San Clemente and Verucchio; San Vicinio has become Mercato Saraceno). A Romagna Sangiovese with a sottozona name needs at least 95% Sangiovese, at most 9 t/ha and 12.5% potential alcohol (13% for Riserva). The Riserva is released only from 1 September of the third year after the harvest, with two months in bottle documented.

it-romagna-verucchio.name: Verucchio
it-romagna-verucchio.village: Verucchio, Santarcangelo di Romagna, Poggio Torriana, Casteldelci, Maiolo, Novafeltria, Pennabilli, San Leo, Sant'Agata Feltria, Talamello
it-romagna-verucchio.grapes: Sangiovese (at least 95% for a sottozona wine)
it-romagna-verucchio.summary: The Marecchia valley from Santarcangelo up to the high Montefeltro. Seven of its communes (including San Leo and Pennabilli) moved from the Marche to Emilia-Romagna in 2009 after a referendum, so the sottozona includes land that was in another region until recently. On the Valmarecchia slopes, the disciplinare says, Sangiovese gives easier-drinking, more immediate wines than in the other Rimini sottozone.
it-romagna-verucchio.terroir: Marecchia valley: low hills near Santarcangelo and Verucchio, steeper, cooler Montefeltro uplands above.
it-romagna-verucchio.nerd_note: Verucchio was the cradle of the Malatesta family, lords of Rimini.
it-romagna-verucchio.classification: Sottozona of Romagna DOC, one of 16 now listed (the original 12 of 2011 plus Imola, Coriano, San Clemente and Verucchio; San Vicinio has become Mercato Saraceno). A Romagna Sangiovese with a sottozona name needs at least 95% Sangiovese, at most 9 t/ha and 12.5% potential alcohol (13% for Riserva). The Riserva is released only from 1 September of the third year after the harvest, with two months in bottle documented.

it-santa-maddalena.name: Santa Maddalena
it-santa-maddalena.summary: The hillside vineyards around the little church of St. Magdalena on the north-eastern edge of Bolzano make Alto Adige's classic Schiava: pale ruby, fragrant with violets, almond and cherry, a touch of Lagrein for colour. Local lore holds that in the 1930s it was ranked among Italy's three great reds, alongside Barolo and Barbaresco. The Classico core is on the steep slopes of Rencio and St. Magdalena.
it-santa-maddalena.terroir: Morainic and porphyry slopes rising behind Bolzano, very warm and sunny.
it-santa-maddalena.nerd_note: The UGAs inside the classico area include St. Justina, Leitach, Rentsch and Prazöll, all small hillside hamlets of Bolzano.

it-santa-maddalena-classico.name: Santa Maddalena classico
it-santa-maddalena-classico.summary: The classico zone of Santa Maddalena (St. Magdalener), the steep hill north-east of Bolzano around the little church of St. Magdalena. Its Schiava-based reds, often with up to 15 percent Lagrein, are the most structured expression of the grape, with cherry, almond and violet.
it-santa-maddalena-classico.terroir: Morainic sands and gravel over quartz porphyry on very steep, south-facing pergola slopes. The official boundary, in Bolzano/Bozen, reaches from about 270 to 860 m (terrain model).
it-santa-maddalena-classico.nerd_note: In the 1930s Mussolini's government is said to have ranked Santa Maddalena among Italy's three great wines with Barolo and Barbaresco.

it-soave-brognoligo.name: Brognoligo
it-soave-brognoligo.grapes: Garganega (at least 70%), Trebbiano di Soave, up to 30% together with other white grapes
it-soave-brognoligo.summary:
One of the most historic parts of the Classico, the frazione of Brognoligo in Monteforte d'Alpone has an ancient tradition of drying grapes (appassimento) for concentrated Recioto. The soils are purely basaltic, silty clay with crushed basalt in the first metre, but slopes range from gentle pergola ground to 45% gradients worked entirely by hand, and some vines are a century old on Rupestris du Lot rootstock.

It is among the driest UGAs (under 800 mm a year over 20 years) and sensitive to drought.
it-soave-brognoligo.terroir: 75.5 ha in total, 52.7 ha of vines (70%); slopes facing south and south-east, 50 to 160 m.
it-soave-brognoligo.nerd_note: Centenarian Garganega on Rupestris du Lot, one of the earliest American rootstocks used after phylloxera, survives in Brognoligo.
it-soave-brognoligo.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Soave: one of 33 named areas in Annex A of the Soave DOC rules, approved in 2019 (usable from that vintage). The same names may be used for Soave DOC, Soave Superiore DOCG and Recioto di Soave DOCG when all the grapes come from inside the UGA. A place name, not a quality rank.

it-soave-broia.name: Broia
it-soave-broia.grapes: Garganega (at least 70%), Trebbiano di Soave, up to 30% together with other white grapes
it-soave-broia.summary: One of three UGAs in the limestone west of the Soave DOC, outside the Classico, in the commune of Mezzane di Sotto. It sits on the terraced alluvial fans of the Mezzane torrent at about 120 m, almost flat, with extremely calcareous, moderately alkaline soils. Cool air from the Lessinia mountains moderates temperatures, but rainfall is low and the soils hold little water, so relief irrigation matters. The name may derive from the Celtic 'brolo', a walled garden or orchard.
it-soave-broia.terroir: 372.8 ha in total, 52.7 ha of vines (14%); foot of slope facing south, about 100 to 120 m. Calcareous alluvial fans.
it-soave-broia.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Soave: one of 33 named areas in Annex A of the Soave DOC rules, approved in 2019 (usable from that vintage). The same names may be used for Soave DOC, Soave Superiore DOCG and Recioto di Soave DOCG when all the grapes come from inside the UGA. A place name, not a quality rank.

it-soave-ca-del-vento.name: Ca' del Vento
it-soave-ca-del-vento.grapes: Garganega (at least 70%), Trebbiano di Soave, up to 30% together with other white grapes
it-soave-ca-del-vento.summary: The smallest UGA, once also called Monticello, is the last spur of the Classico hills in Monteforte d'Alpone. Its basalt soils are dark brown, silty clay and neutral at the surface, redder and weakly acid below, with altered to compact basalt between 50 and 100 cm. 'House of the wind' describes its exposure to air from the upper Alpone valley.
it-soave-ca-del-vento.terroir: 31.3 ha in total, 9.8 ha of vines (31%); low summits and slopes facing south and east, 30 to 45 m.
it-soave-ca-del-vento.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Soave: one of 33 named areas in Annex A of the Soave DOC rules, approved in 2019 (usable from that vintage). The same names may be used for Soave DOC, Soave Superiore DOCG and Recioto di Soave DOCG when all the grapes come from inside the UGA. A place name, not a quality rank.

it-soave-campagnola.name: Campagnola
it-soave-campagnola.grapes: Garganega (at least 70%), Trebbiano di Soave, up to 30% together with other white grapes
it-soave-campagnola.summary: A UGA on the Soave side of the Classico hills, mid-slope and facing south to south-west.
it-soave-campagnola.terroir: 61.9 ha in total, 24.8 ha of vines (40%); summits and slopes facing south and south-west, 100 to 180 m.
it-soave-campagnola.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Soave: one of 33 named areas in Annex A of the Soave DOC rules, approved in 2019 (usable from that vintage). The same names may be used for Soave DOC, Soave Superiore DOCG and Recioto di Soave DOCG when all the grapes come from inside the UGA. A place name, not a quality rank.

it-soave-carbonare.name: Carbonare
it-soave-carbonare.grapes: Garganega (at least 70%), Trebbiano di Soave, up to 30% together with other white grapes
it-soave-carbonare.summary: The name points to charcoal, or perhaps a lignite pit, or simply to the very dark soil, among the most purely volcanic in Soave. Slopes are moderate to very steep, but the soils are deep and stone-free to 60 or 70 cm, with low permeability and limited water reserves. Facing mainly east at medium altitude, well ventilated, it has below-average daytime temperatures. Suavia's Monte Carbonare made the name known.
it-soave-carbonare.terroir: Slopes facing east and north-east, 120 to 280 m; deep, stoneless basaltic clay.
it-soave-carbonare.nerd_note: The consorzio's map gives Carbonare the same area figures as Colombara, almost certainly a copying slip, so treat its hectares with caution.
it-soave-carbonare.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Soave: one of 33 named areas in Annex A of the Soave DOC rules, approved in 2019 (usable from that vintage). The same names may be used for Soave DOC, Soave Superiore DOCG and Recioto di Soave DOCG when all the grapes come from inside the UGA. A place name, not a quality rank.

it-soave-casarsa.name: Casarsa
it-soave-casarsa.grapes: Garganega (at least 70%), Trebbiano di Soave, up to 30% together with other white grapes
it-soave-casarsa.summary: Casarsa is the third tongue of hill, after Duello and Costalunga, that runs out over the Alpone valley. Its summit shows lava flows of different periods that produced substrates of different mineral make-up; soils deepen down the slope. The shape allows one of the highest shares of vineyard in the Classico. Rainfall is among the lowest of the zone, but temperatures are mild and the day-night swing during ripening is wide.
it-soave-casarsa.terroir: 66.0 ha in total, 40.7 ha of vines (62%); facing south, east and north, 40 to 70 m.
it-soave-casarsa.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Soave: one of 33 named areas in Annex A of the Soave DOC rules, approved in 2019 (usable from that vintage). The same names may be used for Soave DOC, Soave Superiore DOCG and Recioto di Soave DOCG when all the grapes come from inside the UGA. A place name, not a quality rank.

it-soave-castelcerino.name: Castelcerino
it-soave-castelcerino.grapes: Garganega (at least 70%), Trebbiano di Soave, up to 30% together with other white grapes
it-soave-castelcerino.summary:
The big hill north of Soave, crowned by the hamlet of Castelcerino, is one of the most important UGAs and, in the consorzio's words, a synthesis of the whole Soave system. Toward Fittà in the east the soils are volcanic, basalt on the summits with very steep flanks; on the western side slopes of 10 to 30% carry deep, very calcareous clay loams. It is one of the rainier corners of the zone, with mild temperatures, so the wines are fresh and finely drawn rather than broad.

Filippi, the organic estate based at Castelcerino, makes single-vineyard Soave from these heights.
it-soave-castelcerino.terroir: 891.6 ha in total, 268 ha of vines (30%); summits and slopes facing south, 110 to 380 m, the highest of the Classico. Basalt to the east, calcareous clay loam to the west.
it-soave-castelcerino.nerd_note: Castelcerino reaches 380 m, the top of the Classico, and its low vine cover (30%) shows how much of the hill is still wood.
it-soave-castelcerino.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Soave: one of 33 named areas in Annex A of the Soave DOC rules, approved in 2019 (usable from that vintage). The same names may be used for Soave DOC, Soave Superiore DOCG and Recioto di Soave DOCG when all the grapes come from inside the UGA. A place name, not a quality rank.

it-soave-castellaro.name: Castellaro
it-soave-castellaro.grapes: Garganega (at least 70%), Trebbiano di Soave, up to 30% together with other white grapes
it-soave-castellaro.summary: Castellaro is a volcanic cone at the northern edge of the Classico, the most explicit trace of the eruptions that built these hills, with moderately fine soils full of basaltic gravel. The name may refer to a ruined castle, but more likely to a castellarium, the palisaded enclosure of an early settlement. Rainfall is above the Soave average and day-night swings are moderate.
it-soave-castellaro.terroir: 50.2 ha in total, 21.1 ha of vines (42%); summits and slopes facing south, east and west, 140 to 260 m. Basaltic skeleton throughout.
it-soave-castellaro.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Soave: one of 33 named areas in Annex A of the Soave DOC rules, approved in 2019 (usable from that vintage). The same names may be used for Soave DOC, Soave Superiore DOCG and Recioto di Soave DOCG when all the grapes come from inside the UGA. A place name, not a quality rank.

it-soave-classico.name: Soave Classico
it-soave-classico.grapes: Garganega (at least 70%), Trebbiano di Soave, up to 30% together with other white grapes
it-soave-classico.summary:
The historic heart of Soave: the hills of Soave and Monteforte d'Alpone recognised in October 1931 as the first delimited zone for a 'vino tipico' in Italy, after a first protection measure in 1924 and the founding of the producers' consortium. That 1931 line, starting and ending at the Verona gate of Soave's medieval walls, became the Soave Classico DOC zone in 1968. A plaque on Soave's Palazzo di Giustizia dated 1375 already regulated the town's wine.

Twenty-eight of the 33 UGAs lie inside it, from the limestone slopes of Costeggiola and Pigno near the town to the basalt hills of Foscarino, Froscà, Monte Grande and Brognoligo toward the Alpone. The Castelvero fault splits the zone into a calcareous west and a volcanic east, and the Veronese pergola still dominates. Classico wines must be made and bottled inside the zone (with exceptions for the province of Verona).

Pieropan (Calvarino, La Rocca), Inama, Gini, Prà, Suavia, Coffele, Filippi, Ca' Rugate and Cantina del Castello are among the defining producers; the Cantina di Soave cooperative handles a large share of the grapes.
it-soave-classico.terroir: Hills of Soave and Monteforte d'Alpone between about 40 and 380 m; Eocene basalts and tuffs east of the Castelvero fault, marine limestone to the west; mild climate with high rainfall in the north.
it-soave-classico.nerd_note: Soave claims the first legally delimited wine zone in Italy: the ministerial decree of 23 October 1931, published in the Gazzetta Ufficiale of 16 December 1931.
it-soave-classico.classification: 'Classico' mention of the Soave DOC (and of Soave Superiore and Recioto di Soave DOCG), reserved for the zone of the 1931 decree in the communes of Soave and Monteforte d'Alpone.

it-soave-colli-scaligeri.name: Soave Colli Scaligeri
it-soave-colli-scaligeri.village: San Martino Buon Albergo, Lavagno, Mezzane di Sotto, Illasi, Colognola ai Colli, Cazzano di Tramigna, Montecchia di Crosara, Roncà and others
it-soave-colli-scaligeri.grapes: Garganega (at least 70%), Trebbiano di Soave, up to 30% together with other white grapes
it-soave-colli-scaligeri.summary: The hillside subzone of Soave outside the Classico: the slopes of the Lessini foothills from Marcellise (San Martino Buon Albergo) east through Lavagno, the Mezzane and Illasi valleys, Colognola ai Colli and on toward the Alpone, drawn along the line where hill meets plain. The name honours the Scaligeri, the della Scala lords of Verona whose castles crown Soave and other hill towns. Colli Scaligeri wines must be vinified inside the delimited zone (with some exceptions within the province), carry a vintage, and come from lower yields than plain Soave (14 t/ha). Several UGAs (Monte di Colognola, Broia, Paradiso, Duello, Roncà-Monte Calvarina) lie in or next to it.
it-soave-colli-scaligeri.terroir: Hills from about 50 to 600 m on limestone in the west and basalt in the east (Roncà, Montecchia), above the alluvial plain of the Adige tributaries.
it-soave-colli-scaligeri.classification: Sottozona of the Soave DOC ('Soave' Colli Scaligeri) with its own delimitation in article 3 of the disciplinare.

it-soave-colombara.name: Colombara
it-soave-colombara.grapes: Garganega (at least 70%), Trebbiano di Soave, up to 30% together with other white grapes
it-soave-colombara.summary: Colombara gathers several historic sub-areas along the south- and west-facing coast of the Soave hills, from Sengialta down to the medieval town. Almost 100 ha, nearly all vineyard: volcanic clay loams in the north and east, with slopes above 25%, and compact stratified limestone to the south around Mondello, where gradients ease to 5 to 15%.
it-soave-colombara.terroir: About 96.5 ha in total; slopes facing west, 45 to 140 m. Basalt in the north, limestone in the south.
it-soave-colombara.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Soave: one of 33 named areas in Annex A of the Soave DOC rules, approved in 2019 (usable from that vintage). The same names may be used for Soave DOC, Soave Superiore DOCG and Recioto di Soave DOCG when all the grapes come from inside the UGA. A place name, not a quality rank.

it-soave-corte-del-durlo.name: Corte del Durlo
it-soave-corte-del-durlo.grapes: Garganega (at least 70%), Trebbiano di Soave, up to 30% together with other white grapes
it-soave-corte-del-durlo.summary:
A small UGA in Monteforte d'Alpone that separates the frazioni of Brognoligo and Costalunga. The name records land of the Montanari nobles bought in the early 1800s by Domenico Durlo of Terrossa. The soils are entirely volcanic (basalts and basaltic breccias); north-east-facing slopes are close to 'heroic' viticulture, while south and south-west slopes run at a gentler 15 to 25%.

The traditional pergola on contour terraces dominates, though Guyot rows planted down the slope appear on the northern side.
it-soave-corte-del-durlo.terroir: 42.7 ha in total, 23.4 ha of vines (55%); summits and slopes facing south and north, 40 to 200 m.
it-soave-corte-del-durlo.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Soave: one of 33 named areas in Annex A of the Soave DOC rules, approved in 2019 (usable from that vintage). The same names may be used for Soave DOC, Soave Superiore DOCG and Recioto di Soave DOCG when all the grapes come from inside the UGA. A place name, not a quality rank.

it-soave-costalta.name: Costalta
it-soave-costalta.grapes: Garganega (at least 70%), Trebbiano di Soave, up to 30% together with other white grapes
it-soave-costalta.summary: As the name ('high slope') suggests, Costalta has long been one of the most sought-after sites for its exposure and height. Its soils are deep basalt, clayey and stone-free to 60 or 70 cm, with low permeability; slopes are not steep and the land is a patchwork of small pergola plots. The consorzio notes early budbreak and a long ripening season.
it-soave-costalta.terroir: 72.4 ha in total, 55.0 ha of vines (76%); slopes facing south, 40 to 150 m.
it-soave-costalta.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Soave: one of 33 named areas in Annex A of the Soave DOC rules, approved in 2019 (usable from that vintage). The same names may be used for Soave DOC, Soave Superiore DOCG and Recioto di Soave DOCG when all the grapes come from inside the UGA. A place name, not a quality rank.

it-soave-costalunga.name: Costalunga
it-soave-costalunga.grapes: Garganega (at least 70%), Trebbiano di Soave, up to 30% together with other white grapes
it-soave-costalunga.summary: Costalunga, a frazione of Monteforte d'Alpone, is a long tongue of hill (hence the name) that runs east into the Alpone valley. Basalt is everywhere, in the soil and in the dry-stone walls and houses; the slopes are gentle and the soils fairly deep, loamy to clay loam. It has long been a reference point for quality estates in the Classico.
it-soave-costalunga.terroir: 121.6 ha in total, 82.2 ha of vines (68%); facing south, south-east and north-east, 40 to 140 m.
it-soave-costalunga.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Soave: one of 33 named areas in Annex A of the Soave DOC rules, approved in 2019 (usable from that vintage). The same names may be used for Soave DOC, Soave Superiore DOCG and Recioto di Soave DOCG when all the grapes come from inside the UGA. A place name, not a quality rank.

it-soave-coste.name: Coste
it-soave-coste.grapes: Garganega (at least 70%), Trebbiano di Soave, up to 30% together with other white grapes
it-soave-coste.summary: Coste, now including the area formerly called Boschetti, is a very homogeneous, north- to north-east-facing slope and, despite that aspect, one of the most densely planted parts of the Classico. The soils are wholly volcanic, silty clay and pH-neutral, on gentle gradients, and the many groves of native trees show that vines arrived here relatively recently. The northern aspect gives particularly fresh, lively wines, and the pergola makes Coste an icon of the Soave landscape.
it-soave-coste.terroir: 88.4 ha in total, 59.0 ha of vines (67%); slopes facing north and north-east, 90 to 180 m.
it-soave-coste.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Soave: one of 33 named areas in Annex A of the Soave DOC rules, approved in 2019 (usable from that vintage). The same names may be used for Soave DOC, Soave Superiore DOCG and Recioto di Soave DOCG when all the grapes come from inside the UGA. A place name, not a quality rank.

it-soave-costeggiola.name: Costeggiola
it-soave-costeggiola.grapes: Garganega (at least 70%), Trebbiano di Soave, up to 30% together with other white grapes
it-soave-costeggiola.summary: Costeggiola, a frazione of Soave, is clearly limestone country: steep upper slopes with compact limestone within a metre, clay loam over clay, and rich, deeper colluvial soils at the foot. The Veronese pergola dominates, mostly on contour terraces. Over the last 20 years it has been one of the wettest areas, close to 1,000 mm a year.
it-soave-costeggiola.terroir: 291.4 ha in total, 104.8 ha of vines (36%); summits and slopes facing south and south-west, 30 to 180 m. Calcareous.
it-soave-costeggiola.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Soave: one of 33 named areas in Annex A of the Soave DOC rules, approved in 2019 (usable from that vintage). The same names may be used for Soave DOC, Soave Superiore DOCG and Recioto di Soave DOCG when all the grapes come from inside the UGA. A place name, not a quality rank.

it-soave-croce.name: Croce
it-soave-croce.grapes: Garganega (at least 70%), Trebbiano di Soave, up to 30% together with other white grapes
it-soave-croce.summary: A small UGA of the Classico on the lower slopes and foot of the hills, facing south and south-west.
it-soave-croce.terroir: 42.7 ha in total, 26.4 ha of vines (62%); slope and foot facing south and south-west, 70 to 120 m.
it-soave-croce.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Soave: one of 33 named areas in Annex A of the Soave DOC rules, approved in 2019 (usable from that vintage). The same names may be used for Soave DOC, Soave Superiore DOCG and Recioto di Soave DOCG when all the grapes come from inside the UGA. A place name, not a quality rank.

it-soave-duello.name: Duello
it-soave-duello.grapes: Garganega (at least 70%), Trebbiano di Soave, up to 30% together with other white grapes
it-soave-duello.summary: Monte Duello rises in the middle of the Val d'Alpone east of the Classico, a very homogeneous and historic area with views back over the eastern Classico and across to the volcanic cones of Monte Crocetta and Monte Calvarina at Roncà. Its soils are entirely volcanic, deep, greyish-brown silty clay on moderately steep slopes, and strong ventilation even in summer widens the day-night swing and keeps grapes healthy.
it-soave-duello.terroir: 306.8 ha in total, 110.3 ha of vines (36%); slopes facing south and south-west, 60 to 200 m.
it-soave-duello.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Soave: one of 33 named areas in Annex A of the Soave DOC rules, approved in 2019 (usable from that vintage). The same names may be used for Soave DOC, Soave Superiore DOCG and Recioto di Soave DOCG when all the grapes come from inside the UGA. A place name, not a quality rank.

it-soave-fitta.name: Fittà
it-soave-fitta.grapes: Garganega (at least 70%), Trebbiano di Soave, up to 30% together with other white grapes
it-soave-fitta.summary:
Fittà is the volcanic heart of the hills north-east of Soave: steep slopes with fractured basalt within the first metre, fine-textured soils with basaltic stones, neutral to slightly alkaline. Much of the area is wood and scarp, rich in biodiversity, with vineyards facing mainly south and south-west on gradients of 10 to 32%. The consorzio's 20 years of weather data make it one of the rainiest and also one of the warmest parts of Soave.

The name probably comes from land given in rent (affitto). Suavia, the estate of the Tessari sisters, is based in Fittà.
it-soave-fitta.terroir: 436.8 ha in total and 131.6 ha of vines (30%) on the consorzio map (its own text gives 190 ha and 75 ha for an earlier outline); 64 to 325 m, facing south, east and west. Basalt throughout.
it-soave-fitta.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Soave: one of 33 named areas in Annex A of the Soave DOC rules, approved in 2019 (usable from that vintage). The same names may be used for Soave DOC, Soave Superiore DOCG and Recioto di Soave DOCG when all the grapes come from inside the UGA. A place name, not a quality rank.

it-soave-foscarino.name: Foscarino
it-soave-foscarino.grapes: Garganega (at least 70%), Trebbiano di Soave, up to 30% together with other white grapes
it-soave-foscarino.summary:
Monte Foscarino is the most famous name in Soave Classico, three volcanic cones between Monteforte d'Alpone and Soave: Foscarinetto (282 m), Boccara (292 m) and Foscarino itself (295 m). Steep slopes, moderately deep soils with crushed basalt in the first metre, and rainfall and temperatures right on the Soave average make it, for the consorzio, the best synthesis of the denomination.

The name may come from fuscus, dark thickets, or from the places where vine poles were cut. Inama built its reputation on Foscarino, including the Vigneto du Lot from old vines grafted on Rupestris du Lot.
it-soave-foscarino.terroir: 187.1 ha in total, 100.6 ha of vines (54%); summits and slopes facing south, east and west, 80 to 290 m. Purely volcanic.
it-soave-foscarino.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Soave: one of 33 named areas in Annex A of the Soave DOC rules, approved in 2019 (usable from that vintage). The same names may be used for Soave DOC, Soave Superiore DOCG and Recioto di Soave DOCG when all the grapes come from inside the UGA. A place name, not a quality rank.

it-soave-frosca.name: Froscà
it-soave-frosca.grapes: Garganega (at least 70%), Trebbiano di Soave, up to 30% together with other white grapes
it-soave-frosca.summary: One of the most historic crus of Soave Classico, almost surrounded by other UGAs. Its soil is mainly volcanic with some limestone outcrops, brownish-yellow to greyish-brown clay with scattered basalt; vines on small terraces held by dry-stone walls or ciglioni on slopes of 10 to 30% include very old plants, some 90 to 100 years. Gini's Soave Classico La Froscà, from about 6 ha owned in the cru, is the reference.
it-soave-frosca.terroir: 42.2 ha in total, 33.5 ha of vines (79%, the highest share of any UGA); summits and slopes facing south and south-east, 40 to 160 m.
it-soave-frosca.nerd_note: Froscà has the highest proportion of land under vine of all 33 UGAs, 79%.
it-soave-frosca.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Soave: one of 33 named areas in Annex A of the Soave DOC rules, approved in 2019 (usable from that vintage). The same names may be used for Soave DOC, Soave Superiore DOCG and Recioto di Soave DOCG when all the grapes come from inside the UGA. A place name, not a quality rank.

it-soave-menini.name: Menini
it-soave-menini.grapes: Garganega (at least 70%), Trebbiano di Soave, up to 30% together with other white grapes
it-soave-menini.summary: A UGA of the Classico hills with two pedological souls, as the consorzio describes it: basalt and steeper ground to the east, compact limestone within a metre of the surface to the west, with clay-loam topsoil over clay. Vines occupy the northern parts; the steeper southern slopes are mostly wooded.
it-soave-menini.terroir: 66.8 ha in total, 25.1 ha of vines (38%); slopes facing south and south-east, 180 to 280 m.
it-soave-menini.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Soave: one of 33 named areas in Annex A of the Soave DOC rules, approved in 2019 (usable from that vintage). The same names may be used for Soave DOC, Soave Superiore DOCG and Recioto di Soave DOCG when all the grapes come from inside the UGA. A place name, not a quality rank.

it-soave-monte-di-colognola.name: Monte di Colognola
it-soave-monte-di-colognola.grapes: Garganega (at least 70%), Trebbiano di Soave, up to 30% together with other white grapes
it-soave-monte-di-colognola.summary: A large UGA covering the hills of Colognola ai Colli in the west of the DOC, including the Colli Scaligeri subzone. On the slopes the soils are deep and formed on stratified marine limestone, clayey and moderately alkaline; on the hilltops everything changes to basalt-derived clay over sandier subsoil. Rainfall is below average, temperatures normal, with wider day-night swings near harvest.
it-soave-monte-di-colognola.terroir: 1,808 ha in total, 434 ha of vines (24%); summits and foot slopes facing south-west to east, around 100 m and above.
it-soave-monte-di-colognola.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Soave: one of 33 named areas in Annex A of the Soave DOC rules, approved in 2019 (usable from that vintage). The same names may be used for Soave DOC, Soave Superiore DOCG and Recioto di Soave DOCG when all the grapes come from inside the UGA. A place name, not a quality rank.

it-soave-monte-grande.name: Monte Grande
it-soave-monte-grande.grapes: Garganega (at least 70%), Trebbiano di Soave, up to 30% together with other white grapes
it-soave-monte-grande.summary: Statistically the most planted UGA of all, Monte Grande lies wholly within Monteforte d'Alpone: a hill sheltered from northern winds and frost, facing mainly south-east, with slopes gentle enough to be planted almost entirely. Its deep, rich, neutral volcanic soils hold moisture even in dry seasons. Graziano Prà's Soave Classico Monte Grande is the best-known bottling.
it-soave-monte-grande.terroir: 64.6 ha in total, 48.2 ha of vines (75%); summits and slopes facing south and south-east, 60 to 190 m.
it-soave-monte-grande.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Soave: one of 33 named areas in Annex A of the Soave DOC rules, approved in 2019 (usable from that vintage). The same names may be used for Soave DOC, Soave Superiore DOCG and Recioto di Soave DOCG when all the grapes come from inside the UGA. A place name, not a quality rank.

it-soave-paradiso.name: Paradiso
it-soave-paradiso.grapes: Garganega (at least 70%), Trebbiano di Soave, up to 30% together with other white grapes
it-soave-paradiso.summary: A western, non-Classico UGA on the terraced fans of the Lessinia torrents, among channel deposits. The soils are extremely calcareous to about 50 cm, dark yellowish brown and gravelly, becoming very stony with depth; permeability is high and water reserves poor, and rooting depth is limited to 50 to 100 cm by the stones. It is the clearest case in Soave of a gravel terroir rather than a hillside one.
it-soave-paradiso.terroir: 156.8 ha in total, 43.9 ha of vines (28%); flat land facing south-west, about 100 m. Calcareous alluvial gravels.
it-soave-paradiso.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Soave: one of 33 named areas in Annex A of the Soave DOC rules, approved in 2019 (usable from that vintage). The same names may be used for Soave DOC, Soave Superiore DOCG and Recioto di Soave DOCG when all the grapes come from inside the UGA. A place name, not a quality rank.

it-soave-pigno.name: Pigno
it-soave-pigno.grapes: Garganega (at least 70%), Trebbiano di Soave, up to 30% together with other white grapes
it-soave-pigno.summary: Pigno, entirely in the commune of Soave, is the Classico in miniature: steep, sometimes excessive slopes split into small vineyards by dry-stone walls and ciglioni, with vines covering about half the land among cherry trees, hedges and woods. Basalt dominates to the west, with some limestone outcrops to the east; the soils are silty clay or loam with almost no stones. A cypress and a wayside shrine (capitello) at the crossroads of footpaths mark its skyline.
it-soave-pigno.terroir: 80.9 ha in total, 40.8 ha of vines (50%); summits and slopes facing south and south-east, 60 to 150 m.
it-soave-pigno.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Soave: one of 33 named areas in Annex A of the Soave DOC rules, approved in 2019 (usable from that vintage). The same names may be used for Soave DOC, Soave Superiore DOCG and Recioto di Soave DOCG when all the grapes come from inside the UGA. A place name, not a quality rank.

it-soave-ponsara.name: Ponsara
it-soave-ponsara.grapes: Garganega (at least 70%), Trebbiano di Soave, up to 30% together with other white grapes
it-soave-ponsara.summary: The name evolved from 'pontara', dialect for a climb. Ponsara links the flat floor of the Val Ponsara with the slopes of Foscarino, Pigno and Froscà in a harmonious amphitheatre facing north-east and south-east, with gentle gradients of 5 to 20%. Dark volcanic clay loam over redder silty loam; sheltered by Foscarino to the north and Froscà to the south, it is cool and relatively rainy.
it-soave-ponsara.terroir: 110.5 ha in total, 63.5 ha of vines (58%); slope and foot facing south and south-east, 40 to 130 m.
it-soave-ponsara.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Soave: one of 33 named areas in Annex A of the Soave DOC rules, approved in 2019 (usable from that vintage). The same names may be used for Soave DOC, Soave Superiore DOCG and Recioto di Soave DOCG when all the grapes come from inside the UGA. A place name, not a quality rank.

it-soave-pressoni.name: Pressoni
it-soave-pressoni.grapes: Garganega (at least 70%), Trebbiano di Soave, up to 30% together with other white grapes
it-soave-pressoni.summary: One of the smallest UGAs of the Classico, almost at its centre between Monteforte and Soave. Early 20th-century records show winemakers paying top prices for grapes from the 'Praisoni', and the name means 'little meadow', a sign of how finely the land was divided. The soils are deep, workable clay with very few stones, exclusively basaltic, on low slopes with mediocre drainage. Cantina del Castello bottles a Soave Classico Pressoni.
it-soave-pressoni.terroir: 27.2 ha in total, 12.0 ha of vines (44%); slopes facing south and south-east, 80 to 190 m.
it-soave-pressoni.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Soave: one of 33 named areas in Annex A of the Soave DOC rules, approved in 2019 (usable from that vintage). The same names may be used for Soave DOC, Soave Superiore DOCG and Recioto di Soave DOCG when all the grapes come from inside the UGA. A place name, not a quality rank.

it-soave-ronca-monte-calvarina.name: Roncà - Monte Calvarina
it-soave-ronca-monte-calvarina.grapes: Garganega (at least 70%), Trebbiano di Soave, up to 30% together with other white grapes
it-soave-ronca-monte-calvarina.summary: The largest UGA by total area and by vineyard, in the commune of Roncà at the eastern end of the DOC. It faces almost entirely south-west and its vineyards climb past 600 m on the slopes of the Calvarina volcano, the highest in Soave. All the soils come from basalts of various kinds, but depth and slope vary so much that producers get very different wines from similar rock. Fattori, based at Terrossa di Roncà, is a leading estate.
it-soave-ronca-monte-calvarina.terroir: 1,617.6 ha in total, 406.5 ha of vines (25%); summits and slopes facing south and south-west, 90 to 600 m.
it-soave-ronca-monte-calvarina.nerd_note: At up to 600 m, Monte Calvarina holds the highest vineyards of Soave, more than 200 m above anything in the Classico.
it-soave-ronca-monte-calvarina.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Soave: one of 33 named areas in Annex A of the Soave DOC rules, approved in 2019 (usable from that vintage). The same names may be used for Soave DOC, Soave Superiore DOCG and Recioto di Soave DOCG when all the grapes come from inside the UGA. A place name, not a quality rank.

it-soave-rugate.name: Rugate
it-soave-rugate.grapes: Garganega (at least 70%), Trebbiano di Soave, up to 30% together with other white grapes
it-soave-rugate.summary: Perhaps the most striking amphitheatre of vines in the Classico, soft and enclosing, with exposures to the south-east and north-east. The name seems to come from the rugged, wrinkled look of its rocks. The soil is entirely volcanic, arranged on ciglioni (grassy banks) and small terraces held by dry-stone walls, clayey on the surface and siltier below; summer ventilation is good. Ca' Rugate, the Tessari family estate, takes its name from the area.
it-soave-rugate.terroir: 47.3 ha in total, 29.2 ha of vines (62%); slopes facing south-east, 70 to 218 m.
it-soave-rugate.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Soave: one of 33 named areas in Annex A of the Soave DOC rules, approved in 2019 (usable from that vintage). The same names may be used for Soave DOC, Soave Superiore DOCG and Recioto di Soave DOCG when all the grapes come from inside the UGA. A place name, not a quality rank.

it-soave-sengialta.name: Sengialta
it-soave-sengialta.grapes: Garganega (at least 70%), Trebbiano di Soave, up to 30% together with other white grapes
it-soave-sengialta.summary: Sengialta is the first slope on the right as the road climbs from Soave toward Castelcerino. It is crossed by the Castelvero fault, which divides the volcanic and calcareous halves of Soave, and its name carries its identity: 'sengia' is a basalt stone. The soils are moderately deep, silty clay or clay loam, with basalt often showing at the surface.
it-soave-sengialta.terroir: 46.5 ha in total, 24.7 ha of vines (53%); slopes facing south and east, 50 to 160 m. Mainly volcanic.
it-soave-sengialta.nerd_note: The Castelvero fault running through Sengialta is the geological seam of the Classico: basalt on one side, marine limestone on the other.
it-soave-sengialta.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Soave: one of 33 named areas in Annex A of the Soave DOC rules, approved in 2019 (usable from that vintage). The same names may be used for Soave DOC, Soave Superiore DOCG and Recioto di Soave DOCG when all the grapes come from inside the UGA. A place name, not a quality rank.

it-soave-tenda.name: Tenda
it-soave-tenda.grapes: Garganega (at least 70%), Trebbiano di Soave, up to 30% together with other white grapes
it-soave-tenda.summary: A large UGA in the Classico hills, mostly summits and upper slopes facing south and west.
it-soave-tenda.terroir: 271.7 ha in total, 93.3 ha of vines (34%); summits and slopes facing south and west, 70 to 170 m.
it-soave-tenda.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Soave: one of 33 named areas in Annex A of the Soave DOC rules, approved in 2019 (usable from that vintage). The same names may be used for Soave DOC, Soave Superiore DOCG and Recioto di Soave DOCG when all the grapes come from inside the UGA. A place name, not a quality rank.

it-soave-tremenalto.name: Tremenalto
it-soave-tremenalto.grapes: Garganega (at least 70%), Trebbiano di Soave, up to 30% together with other white grapes
it-soave-tremenalto.summary:
Tremenalto closes the Classico zone of Monteforte d'Alpone to the north; the name probably means 'high boundary' (termine alto), where it meets Montecchia di Crosara. Its deep, fertile volcanic soils are dark brown to dark red, calcareous and slightly alkaline, on steep slopes of 20 to 35% facing north and north-east.

Cool air coming down the upper Alpone valley keeps summer temperatures lower, so the wines are notably fresh and easy to drink, an advantage in hot vintages.
it-soave-tremenalto.terroir: 153.1 ha in total, 84.9 ha of vines (55%); slopes facing east and north, 57 to 230 m. Volcanic, calcareous soils.
it-soave-tremenalto.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Soave: one of 33 named areas in Annex A of the Soave DOC rules, approved in 2019 (usable from that vintage). The same names may be used for Soave DOC, Soave Superiore DOCG and Recioto di Soave DOCG when all the grapes come from inside the UGA. A place name, not a quality rank.

it-soave-volpare.name: Volpare
it-soave-volpare.grapes: Garganega (at least 70%), Trebbiano di Soave, up to 30% together with other white grapes
it-soave-volpare.summary: One of the smallest UGAs, historically linked to Froscà and similar in soil and altitude, but facing more to the south-west and dotted with groves, olive and cherry trees. The name comes from caves in the limestone that sheltered foxes (volpi), which are returning to the Classico. Monte Riondo dominates the view; temperatures are average and rainfall modest.
it-soave-volpare.terroir: 28.3 ha in total, 13.4 ha of vines (47%); summits and slopes facing south and south-east, 40 to 160 m.
it-soave-volpare.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Soave: one of 33 named areas in Annex A of the Soave DOC rules, approved in 2019 (usable from that vintage). The same names may be used for Soave DOC, Soave Superiore DOCG and Recioto di Soave DOCG when all the grapes come from inside the UGA. A place name, not a quality rank.

it-soave-zoppega.name: Zoppega
it-soave-zoppega.grapes: Garganega (at least 70%), Trebbiano di Soave, up to 30% together with other white grapes
it-soave-zoppega.summary: The name perhaps describes the limping, up-and-down skyline of the hill seen from the south (zoppo, lame); Zoppega marks the edge of the Classico on this side. Deep silty-clay soils are basaltic to the east and increasingly calcareous to the west, where dry-stone walls multiply. Paleontologists have long studied traces of prehistoric communities here. Its almost exclusively southern aspect weighs on the wines in very hot years.
it-soave-zoppega.terroir: 96.7 ha in total, 51.8 ha of vines (54%); summits and slopes facing south and south-east, 30 to 100 m.
it-soave-zoppega.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Soave: one of 33 named areas in Annex A of the Soave DOC rules, approved in 2019 (usable from that vintage). The same names may be used for Soave DOC, Soave Superiore DOCG and Recioto di Soave DOCG when all the grapes come from inside the UGA. A place name, not a quality rank.

it-valle-d-aosta-arnad-montjovet.name: Arnad-Montjovet
it-valle-d-aosta-arnad-montjovet.village: Arnad, Montjovet, Hône, Issogne, Champdepraz, Verrès, Challand-Saint-Victor
it-valle-d-aosta-arnad-montjovet.summary: The lower valley's second Nebbiolo subzone, between Hône and Montjovet, at least 70% Nebbiolo (locally Picotendro) with local reds. The wines are firm and fragrant, lighter than Donnas. Arnad is also famous for its lard (Lard d'Arnad DOP), cured in chestnut-wood tubs. La Kiuva, the Arnad cooperative, is the main producer.
it-valle-d-aosta-arnad-montjovet.terroir: Both banks between Hône and Montjovet, up to 600 m on the right and 700 m on the left; granite-gneiss terraces.
it-valle-d-aosta-arnad-montjovet.classification: Sottozona of the Valle d'Aosta / Vallée d'Aoste DOC, one of seven historic names (each with its own grape rules and delimitation in the disciplinare) that may follow the regional denomination on the label.
it-valle-d-aosta-arnad-montjovet.nerd_note: Arnad is also famous for its lard (Lardo d'Arnad DOP), cured in chestnut-wood tubs.

it-valle-d-aosta-blanc-de-morgex-et-de-l.name: Blanc de Morgex et de La Salle
it-valle-d-aosta-blanc-de-morgex-et-de-l.summary:
The highest subzone of the valley and one of the highest vineyards in Europe, on the left bank of the Dora Baltea in Morgex and La Salle, below Mont Blanc, where the DOC zone runs up to 1,300 m. Prié Blanc, an ancient local white, ripens in barely five months, and many vines are on their own roots, trained on low pergolas (topie) held up by stone pillars so the grapes catch heat from the ground. The wines are pale, light and saline, with green apple and alpine herbs, and are also made as metodo classico.

Cave Mont Blanc, the cooperative of Morgex, makes most of it; Ermes Pavese is the leading independent grower.
it-valle-d-aosta-blanc-de-morgex-et-de-l.terroir: Left bank of the Dora Baltea from the La Salle-Avise boundary to Pré-Saint-Didier, up to 1,300 m (vines mostly 900 to 1,200 m); sandy, stony morainic soils; long winters and frost risk.
producers: Cave Mont Blanc de Morgex et La Salle
it-valle-d-aosta-blanc-de-morgex-et-de-l.nerd_note: Prié Blanc is one of the few European varieties still commonly grown ungrafted: phylloxera never thrived in Morgex's cold, sandy soils.
it-valle-d-aosta-blanc-de-morgex-et-de-l.classification: Sottozona of the Valle d'Aosta / Vallée d'Aoste DOC, one of seven historic names (each with its own grape rules and delimitation in the disciplinare) that may follow the regional denomination on the label.

it-valle-d-aosta-chambave.name: Chambave
it-valle-d-aosta-chambave.village: Chambave, Châtillon, Pontey, Saint-Vincent, Saint-Denis, Verrayes, Montjovet
it-valle-d-aosta-chambave.grapes: Petit Rouge at least 70% (red); Moscato Bianco (Chambave Muscat)
it-valle-d-aosta-chambave.summary: Chambave, in the central valley, is best known for its Moscato: Chambave Muscat, dry and aromatic, and Chambave Muscat Flétri, a sweet wine from dried grapes, one of the great Alpine stickies. The red is at least 70% Petit Rouge. La Crotta di Vegneron and La Vrille are leading names; the late Ezio Voyat made the Flétri famous.
it-valle-d-aosta-chambave.terroir: Both banks around Chambave, up to 700 m on the right and 750 m on the left; warm, dry, sunny central valley.
it-valle-d-aosta-chambave.classification: Sottozona of the Valle d'Aosta / Vallée d'Aoste DOC, one of seven historic names (each with its own grape rules and delimitation in the disciplinare) that may follow the regional denomination on the label.
it-valle-d-aosta-chambave.nerd_note: Chambave's Moscato Flétri was historically served to the Savoy kings when they hunted in the valley.

it-valle-d-aosta-donnas.name: Donnas
it-valle-d-aosta-donnas.summary: The gateway subzone from Piedmont and the valley's first DOC (1971), in Donnas, Pont-Saint-Martin, Perloz and Bard. Nebbiolo (at least 85%) grows on pergolas over granite terraces that continue straight into Carema; the wines are pale, firm and perfumed and age at least two years. The Caves Coopératives de Donnas, founded in 1971, make almost all of it.
it-valle-d-aosta-donnas.terroir: Left-bank hillsides above the SS 26 up to 700 m, plus the Valbona alluvial fan in Donnas on the right bank; granite and gneiss terraces with stone pillars and pergolas.
it-valle-d-aosta-donnas.nerd_note: The Roman road to Gaul passes through Donnas, cut into the rock, with a carved milestone still in place among the vineyards.
it-valle-d-aosta-donnas.classification: Sottozona of the Valle d'Aosta / Vallée d'Aoste DOC, one of seven historic names (each with its own grape rules and delimitation in the disciplinare) that may follow the regional denomination on the label.

it-valle-d-aosta-enfer-d-arvier.name: Enfer d'Arvier
it-valle-d-aosta-enfer-d-arvier.summary: 'Arvier's hell' is a tiny, sun-trapping amphitheatre of terraces above the village of Arvier, on both banks of the Dora Baltea at the mouth of the Valgrisenche, where the rock walls reflect so much heat that it feels infernal in summer. The wine is at least 85% Petit Rouge: deep ruby, with violets, wild cherries and a hint of almond. The Co-Enfer cooperative makes most of it.
it-valle-d-aosta-enfer-d-arvier.terroir: Terraced slopes in the commune of Arvier (Monbet, Bouse, Sorpier and the left-bank slope toward Saint-Nicolas), roughly 750 to 900 m; south-facing, warm, rocky.
it-valle-d-aosta-enfer-d-arvier.nerd_note: Enfer d'Arvier is one of Italy's smallest subzones: a single commune's sunniest terraces.
it-valle-d-aosta-enfer-d-arvier.classification: Sottozona of the Valle d'Aosta / Vallée d'Aoste DOC, one of seven historic names (each with its own grape rules and delimitation in the disciplinare) that may follow the regional denomination on the label.

it-valle-d-aosta-nus.name: Nus
it-valle-d-aosta-nus.grapes: Vien de Nus and Petit Rouge at least 70% (Vien de Nus at least 40%); Nus Malvoisie from Pinot Grigio
it-valle-d-aosta-nus.summary: Nus, east of Aosta, has two curiosities. The red must contain at least 40% of the rare Vien de Nus. The white, Nus Malvoisie, is made from Pinot Grigio (known here as Malvoisie) and is famous as a passito (flétri) from grapes dried after harvest, amber, honeyed and long.
it-valle-d-aosta-nus.terroir: Left bank from the Verrayes-Nus boundary to Aosta, up to 850 m, plus the Fénis right bank up to 650 m; sunny, dry slopes.
it-valle-d-aosta-nus.nerd_note: 'Malvoisie' in Nus is Pinot Grigio, not Malvasia: an old case of a borrowed name.
it-valle-d-aosta-nus.classification: Sottozona of the Valle d'Aosta / Vallée d'Aoste DOC, one of seven historic names (each with its own grape rules and delimitation in the disciplinare) that may follow the regional denomination on the label.

it-valle-d-aosta-torrette.name: Torrette
it-valle-d-aosta-torrette.village: Saint-Pierre, Villeneuve, Aymavilles, Sarre, Aosta, Quart and others
it-valle-d-aosta-torrette.summary: The largest red subzone of the valley, around Aosta from Quart to Villeneuve and Introd. Petit Rouge (at least 70%) gives supple, fragrant reds with cherry and violet; the best, from Les Crêtes, Grosjean and Elio Ottin, often labelled Torrette Supérieur, have real depth.
it-valle-d-aosta-torrette.terroir: Both banks of the Dora Baltea around Aosta, up to 800 m on the right bank and 1,000 m on the left; morainic and alluvial-fan soils, sunny and dry.
it-valle-d-aosta-torrette.classification: Sottozona of the Valle d'Aosta / Vallée d'Aoste DOC, one of seven historic names (each with its own grape rules and delimitation in the disciplinare) that may follow the regional denomination on the label.
it-valle-d-aosta-torrette.nerd_note: The name comes from the Torrette hamlet near Saint-Pierre, close to the medieval castle of Saint-Pierre.

it-valpolicella-classico.name: Classico
it-valpolicella-classico.village: Fumane, Marano di Valpolicella, Negrar di Valpolicella, San Pietro in Cariano, Sant'Ambrogio di Valpolicella
it-valpolicella-classico.grapes: Corvina and Corvinone (45 to 95%), Rondinella (5 to 30%), other local reds
it-valpolicella-classico.summary:
The original Valpolicella: the five communes of Fumane, Marano, Negrar, San Pietro in Cariano and Sant'Ambrogio, from the gorge of the Adige at Ceraino east to Negrar, a fan of valleys running down from the Lessini mountains to the plain. The 'Classico' mention is reserved to wine from this oldest zone, for Valpolicella and Superiore and also for Amarone and Recioto, and vinification must take place inside it (with limited exceptions).

Its valleys each have a character: Fumane's steep, cool slopes (Allegrini, Monte dei Ragni), Marano's high hills, Negrar's broad amphitheatre (Quintarelli, Bussola, Bertani's Novare estate at Arbizzano), and the gentler, warmer land of San Pietro in Cariano and Sant'Ambrogio (Speri, Tedeschi, Zýmē, Masi at Gargagnago). The marogne, dry-stone terrace walls of local limestone, hold many of the vineyards.
it-valpolicella-classico.terroir: Limestone and marl of the Lessini foothills, with some volcanic basalt; valleys between about 150 and 500 m opening south toward the Adige plain and Lake Garda's influence.
it-valpolicella-classico.nerd_note: Masi's Serego Alighieri estate at Gargagnago has belonged to descendants of Dante since 1353, when his son Pietro bought land in the Classico zone.
it-valpolicella-classico.classification: Geographic mention 'Classico' of the Valpolicella DOC (and of Amarone and Recioto della Valpolicella DOCG): the five historic communes defined in the disciplinare.

it-valpolicella-valpantena.name: Valpantena
it-valpolicella-valpantena.grapes: Corvina and Corvinone (45 to 95%), Rondinella (5 to 30%), other local reds
it-valpolicella-valpantena.summary:
The Valpantena is the valley that runs north from the city of Verona toward Grezzana, east of the Classico zone, and has the right to its own geographic mention on Valpolicella, Amarone and Recioto labels. Its wines are often described as lighter-bodied and more fragrant than the Classico's, from a valley open to cool air from the Lessini.

Bertani was founded in 1857 at Quinto di Valpantena and still bottles a Valpantena range; the Cantina di Valpantena cooperative and Tezza are other names here.
it-valpolicella-valpantena.terroir: A north-south valley of limestone and marl hills reaching about 500 m on its flanks, with alluvial ground on the floor.
it-valpolicella-valpantena.classification: Geographic mention 'Valpantena' of the Valpolicella DOC and of Amarone and Recioto della Valpolicella DOCG, with its own delimitation in the disciplinare.

it-valtellina-superiore-grumello.name: Grumello
it-valtellina-superiore-grumello.summary:
Grumello lies just east of Sondrio on the slopes of Montagna in Valtellina, named after the ruined Castel Grumello, a 13th-century double castle on a rocky spur now cared for by the FAI. Deeper soils and a slightly cooler position than Sassella give wines often described as softer and rounder, with a gentle, earthy charm.

ArPePe (whose Buon Consiglio and Rocca de Piro come from here) and Rainoldi are leading names.
it-valtellina-superiore-grumello.terroir: South-facing terraces east of Sondrio, about 300 to 600 m; sandy granite-gneiss soils, somewhat deeper than Sassella's.
it-valtellina-superiore-grumello.classification: Historic sottozona of Valtellina Superiore DOCG, delimited in the disciplinare. Rules as for the DOCG (8 t/ha, 24 months of ageing with 12 in wood, 36 for Riserva, counted from 1 December), but grapes for a sottozona wine need 11.5% potential alcohol instead of 11%. Wine aged or bottled in Switzerland as "Stagafassli" may not name a sottozona.

it-valtellina-superiore-inferno.name: Inferno
it-valtellina-superiore-inferno.summary:
The smallest of the classic eastern subzones and the most dramatic: a steep amphitheatre of rock above Poggiridenti and Tresivio, between the Davaglione stream and the Valeriana road. The name, 'hell', is usually explained by the heat that the bare rock walls reflect in summer and by the hellish work of tending the terraces. The wines are among the most powerful and long-lived of Valtellina.

ArPePe's Fiamme Antiche, Nino Negri and Rainoldi make benchmark Inferno.
it-valtellina-superiore-inferno.terroir: Very steep, rocky south-facing terraces, about 300 to 600 m; thin sandy soils over granite, with high reflected heat.
it-valtellina-superiore-inferno.classification: Historic sottozona of Valtellina Superiore DOCG, delimited in the disciplinare. Rules as for the DOCG (8 t/ha, 24 months of ageing with 12 in wood, 36 for Riserva, counted from 1 December), but grapes for a sottozona wine need 11.5% potential alcohol instead of 11%. Wine aged or bottled in Switzerland as "Stagafassli" may not name a sottozona.

it-valtellina-superiore-maroggia.name: Maroggia
it-valtellina-superiore-maroggia.summary: The smallest and westernmost of the five historic subzones, around the hamlet of Maroggia in Berbenno di Valtellina. The disciplinare draws it from the Valle Serada and the Regoledo-Monastero road down through Maroggia village and the contrade of Ere, Valdorta, Pedemonte, Gatti and Camp Fop to the Valeriana road. It is rarely seen on labels.
it-valtellina-superiore-maroggia.terroir: South-facing terraces on an alluvial fan (conoide) and the slope above it at the western end of the Valtellina Superiore zone; granite and gneiss sands.
it-valtellina-superiore-maroggia.classification: Historic sottozona of Valtellina Superiore DOCG, delimited in the disciplinare. Rules as for the DOCG (8 t/ha, 24 months of ageing with 12 in wood, 36 for Riserva, counted from 1 December), but grapes for a sottozona wine need 11.5% potential alcohol instead of 11%. Wine aged or bottled in Switzerland as "Stagafassli" may not name a sottozona.

it-valtellina-superiore-sassella.name: Sassella
it-valtellina-superiore-sassella.summary:
Sassella runs from the sanctuary of the Madonna della Sassella, a church on a rocky spur above the Stelvio road, east to the edge of Sondrio. It is the most famous and often the most refined of the subzones: terraces on steep, rocky slopes facing due south, with bare granite outcrops that soak up heat ('sasso' means rock). The wines are perfumed and finely structured, with red fruit, roses and a stony length.

ArPePe's Rocce Rosse and Stella Retica, Nino Negri's Le Tense, Rainoldi and Mamete Prevostini make some of the reference bottlings.
it-valtellina-superiore-sassella.terroir: Steep south-facing terraces between about 300 and 600 m west of Sondrio; thin sandy soils over granite and gneiss, much of it carried up by hand.
it-valtellina-superiore-sassella.nerd_note: The sanctuary of the Madonna della Sassella marks the western end of the subzone in the disciplinare: the boundary starts on the Stelvio road just below the church.
it-valtellina-superiore-sassella.classification: Historic sottozona of Valtellina Superiore DOCG, delimited in the disciplinare. Rules as for the DOCG (8 t/ha, 24 months of ageing with 12 in wood, 36 for Riserva, counted from 1 December), but grapes for a sottozona wine need 11.5% potential alcohol instead of 11%. Wine aged or bottled in Switzerland as "Stagafassli" may not name a sottozona.

it-valtellina-superiore-valgella.name: Valgella
it-valtellina-superiore-valgella.summary: The largest and easternmost subzone, from the Rogna stream at Chiuro east through the slopes below Teglio to Tresenda, where the road to the Aprica pass leaves the valley. Higher and cooler on average than Sassella, Valgella gives fresh, lively, aromatic Nebbiolo. Nino Negri's winery is in the 15th-century Castello Quadrio at Chiuro, and Sandro Fay at San Giacomo di Teglio makes the reference single-vineyard Valgella (Ca' Morèi, Carterìa).
it-valtellina-superiore-valgella.terroir: South-facing terraces from Chiuro to Tresenda, roughly 400 to 700 m; granite and gneiss sands; cooler than the central subzones.
it-valtellina-superiore-valgella.nerd_note: Teglio, above Valgella, is traditionally said to have given the whole valley its name: Val Tellina.
it-valtellina-superiore-valgella.classification: Historic sottozona of Valtellina Superiore DOCG, delimited in the disciplinare. Rules as for the DOCG (8 t/ha, 24 months of ageing with 12 in wood, 36 for Riserva, counted from 1 December), but grapes for a sottozona wine need 11.5% potential alcohol instead of 11%. Wine aged or bottled in Switzerland as "Stagafassli" may not name a sottozona.

it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-ascianel.name: Ascianello
it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-ascianel.grapes: Sangiovese (Prugnolo Gentile) at least 85%, the rest only Canaiolo Nero, Ciliegiolo, Colorino or Mammolo
it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-ascianel.summary: Ascianello lies north of the town of Montepulciano and extends south from Badia. The consorzio's study describes fine sands over silty clay, with deeper soils in the lower valley near the Salarco stream, which also shapes the local microclimate. De' Ricci, the historic house with Renaissance cellars under the town, has released Pieve Ascianello from the 2022 and 2023 vintages; the 2022 has been described as concentrated and luxurious.
it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-ascianel.terroir: North of the town; fine sands over silty clay, deeper soils toward the Salarco valley floor.
it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-ascianel.classification: Pieve: one of 12 unità geografiche aggiuntive of Vino Nobile di Montepulciano DOCG, named after historic parish churches and approved in the rules published by the EU in May 2025 (valid from the 2021 vintage). A "Vino Nobile di Montepulciano Pieve" must be at least 85% Sangiovese with only native partners, from the bottler's own vines at least 15 years old inside one Pieve, at no more than 7 t/ha, aged three years (one in wood, one in bottle).

it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-badia.name: Badia
it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-badia.grapes: Sangiovese (Prugnolo Gentile) at least 85%, the rest only Canaiolo Nero, Ciliegiolo, Colorino or Mammolo
it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-badia.summary: Badia takes its name from an ancient Benedictine abbey (badia) in the north of the zone. Its slopes are of clay and sand, with fluvio-lacustrine terraces of small siliceous pebbles toward the valley floor, a reminder that the Val di Chiana was once a lake basin.
it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-badia.terroir: North of the town; clay and sand slopes over fluvio-lacustrine terraces with siliceous pebbles.
it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-badia.classification: Pieve: one of 12 unità geografiche aggiuntive of Vino Nobile di Montepulciano DOCG, named after historic parish churches and approved in the rules published by the EU in May 2025 (valid from the 2021 vintage). A "Vino Nobile di Montepulciano Pieve" must be at least 85% Sangiovese with only native partners, from the bottler's own vines at least 15 years old inside one Pieve, at no more than 7 t/ha, aged three years (one in wood, one in bottle).

it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-caggiole.name: Caggiole
it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-caggiole.grapes: Sangiovese (Prugnolo Gentile) at least 85%, the rest only Canaiolo Nero, Ciliegiolo, Colorino or Mammolo
it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-caggiole.summary: Caggiole lies in the north of the zone toward the Val di Chiana and has its own parish. The consorzio describes coarse sands with lens-shaped cobble layers, calcareous sands in the north and browner sandy soils downslope; Poliziano describes its parcel as tuff, clay, stone and Pliocene sands. The first Pieve releases were dense and weighty: Podere Tiberini's dark, meaty and peppery, Poliziano's broad and slowly unfolding, with Crociani also bottling one.
it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-caggiole.terroir: North, toward the Val di Chiana; coarse and calcareous sands with cobble lenses, some tuff and clay.
it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-caggiole.classification: Pieve: one of 12 unità geografiche aggiuntive of Vino Nobile di Montepulciano DOCG, named after historic parish churches and approved in the rules published by the EU in May 2025 (valid from the 2021 vintage). A "Vino Nobile di Montepulciano Pieve" must be at least 85% Sangiovese with only native partners, from the bottler's own vines at least 15 years old inside one Pieve, at no more than 7 t/ha, aged three years (one in wood, one in bottle).

it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-cerliana.name: Cerliana
it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-cerliana.grapes: Sangiovese (Prugnolo Gentile) at least 85%, the rest only Canaiolo Nero, Ciliegiolo, Colorino or Mammolo
it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-cerliana.summary: Cerliana lies north-east of the town, its soils shaped by the alluvial terraces of the Salcheto and Ciarliana streams: clayey-silty with sandy layers, deeper toward the valley floor. Critics of the first releases noted a chalky, mineral tannin; La Ciarliana's 2021 is dense and extracted, Antico Colle's of medium weight, Tenuta Valdipiatta's 2022 the most restrained.
it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-cerliana.terroir: North-east; clay-silt with sandy layers on the terraces of the Salcheto and Ciarliana streams.
it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-cerliana.classification: Pieve: one of 12 unità geografiche aggiuntive of Vino Nobile di Montepulciano DOCG, named after historic parish churches and approved in the rules published by the EU in May 2025 (valid from the 2021 vintage). A "Vino Nobile di Montepulciano Pieve" must be at least 85% Sangiovese with only native partners, from the bottler's own vines at least 15 years old inside one Pieve, at no more than 7 t/ha, aged three years (one in wood, one in bottle).

it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-cervogna.name: Cervognano
it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-cervogna.grapes: Sangiovese (Prugnolo Gentile) at least 85%, the rest only Canaiolo Nero, Ciliegiolo, Colorino or Mammolo
it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-cervogna.summary: Cervognano lies south-east of the town toward the Val di Chiana: silty soils over compact sands on the hills, and flat terraces of clay and sand with small siliceous pebbles near the Salcheto and Ciarliana streams. It produced the largest group of first Pieve releases (2021), typically dark and black-fruited: Marchesi Frescobaldi, Le Bèrne (restrained after a very long maceration), Fattoria Svetoni, Guidotti and Vecchia Cantina di Montepulciano.
it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-cervogna.terroir: South-east; silts over compact sands, with clay-sand terraces near the streams.
it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-cervogna.classification: Pieve: one of 12 unità geografiche aggiuntive of Vino Nobile di Montepulciano DOCG, named after historic parish churches and approved in the rules published by the EU in May 2025 (valid from the 2021 vintage). A "Vino Nobile di Montepulciano Pieve" must be at least 85% Sangiovese with only native partners, from the bottler's own vines at least 15 years old inside one Pieve, at no more than 7 t/ha, aged three years (one in wood, one in bottle).

it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-graccian.name: Gracciano
it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-graccian.grapes: Sangiovese (Prugnolo Gentile) at least 85%, the rest only Canaiolo Nero, Ciliegiolo, Colorino or Mammolo
it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-graccian.summary: Gracciano lies north of the town on fluvio-lacustrine terraces: sands with small siliceous pebbles and a loamy-sandy clay texture. Tenuta di Gracciano della Seta, the best-known estate of the parish, released a refined, fruit-forward 2021 with orange zest and cinnamon notes; Fassati also bottles a Pieve Gracciano.
it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-graccian.terroir: North; sandy, pebbly fluvio-lacustrine terraces with loamy-sandy clay.
it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-graccian.classification: Pieve: one of 12 unità geografiche aggiuntive of Vino Nobile di Montepulciano DOCG, named after historic parish churches and approved in the rules published by the EU in May 2025 (valid from the 2021 vintage). A "Vino Nobile di Montepulciano Pieve" must be at least 85% Sangiovese with only native partners, from the bottler's own vines at least 15 years old inside one Pieve, at no more than 7 t/ha, aged three years (one in wood, one in bottle).

it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-le-grazi.name: Le Grazie
it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-le-grazi.grapes: Sangiovese (Prugnolo Gentile) at least 85%, the rest only Canaiolo Nero, Ciliegiolo, Colorino or Mammolo
it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-le-grazi.summary: Le Grazie lies on the northern outskirts of the town: sands and fine sands on the upper slopes, deep, calcareous clay on the more irregular lower ground. Talosa's 33 ha of vines in the Pietrose area, at 330 to 400 m facing mainly south-west on Pliocene soils still full of marine fossils, are its best-known; its Pieve Le Grazie comes from Vigna Chiusino, the estate's oldest vineyard, planted in 1969 on sandy clay and aged two years in used tonneaux.
it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-le-grazi.terroir: North, outer edge of the town; sands above, deep calcareous clay below; Talosa's vineyards at 330 to 400 m, south-west facing.
it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-le-grazi.classification: Pieve: one of 12 unità geografiche aggiuntive of Vino Nobile di Montepulciano DOCG, named after historic parish churches and approved in the rules published by the EU in May 2025 (valid from the 2021 vintage). A "Vino Nobile di Montepulciano Pieve" must be at least 85% Sangiovese with only native partners, from the bottler's own vines at least 15 years old inside one Pieve, at no more than 7 t/ha, aged three years (one in wood, one in bottle).

it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-san-biag.name: San Biagio
it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-san-biag.grapes: Sangiovese (Prugnolo Gentile) at least 85%, the rest only Canaiolo Nero, Ciliegiolo, Colorino or Mammolo
it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-san-biag.summary: San Biagio lies west of the town, below the Renaissance temple of the Madonna di San Biagio by Antonio da Sangallo the Elder, where the Pieve wines were launched. Sandy loams on the upper slopes give way to silty, calcareous clays on the undulating lower ground, bounded by the Fosso dei Grilloni. Le Bertille released a 2021.
it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-san-biag.terroir: West, below the town; sandy loam above, silty calcareous clay below.
it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-san-biag.classification: Pieve: one of 12 unità geografiche aggiuntive of Vino Nobile di Montepulciano DOCG, named after historic parish churches and approved in the rules published by the EU in May 2025 (valid from the 2021 vintage). A "Vino Nobile di Montepulciano Pieve" must be at least 85% Sangiovese with only native partners, from the bottler's own vines at least 15 years old inside one Pieve, at no more than 7 t/ha, aged three years (one in wood, one in bottle).

it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-sant-alb.name: Sant'Albino
it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-sant-alb.grapes: Sangiovese (Prugnolo Gentile) at least 85%, the rest only Canaiolo Nero, Ciliegiolo, Colorino or Mammolo
it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-sant-alb.summary: Sant'Albino lies south of the town, midway toward Chianciano, around the thermal springs that bear its name. The upper slopes near the town have sandy, often reddish-brown soils; lower down are sandy clays, silts and clay, opening onto a wide valley to the east. Carpineto's releases are lighter and high-toned, with bright acidity.
it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-sant-alb.terroir: South, toward Chianciano; reddish sands above, sandy clays and silts below.
it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-sant-alb.classification: Pieve: one of 12 unità geografiche aggiuntive of Vino Nobile di Montepulciano DOCG, named after historic parish churches and approved in the rules published by the EU in May 2025 (valid from the 2021 vintage). A "Vino Nobile di Montepulciano Pieve" must be at least 85% Sangiovese with only native partners, from the bottler's own vines at least 15 years old inside one Pieve, at no more than 7 t/ha, aged three years (one in wood, one in bottle).

it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-sant-ila.name: Sant'Ilario
it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-sant-ila.grapes: Sangiovese (Prugnolo Gentile) at least 85%, the rest only Canaiolo Nero, Ciliegiolo, Colorino or Mammolo
it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-sant-ila.summary: One of the twelve Pievi named in the 2025 rules. The first releases (2021 and 2022) were reserved and tannic: Fattoria del Cerro, Tenuta Poggio alla Sala (black cherry and stony minerality) and Vecchia Cantina di Montepulciano, in an old-school, austere style. Like all twelve Pievi it lies within the single commune of Montepulciano, and a Pieve wine must come entirely from the bottler's own vines inside it.
it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-sant-ila.nerd_note: A 2022 draft of the scheme listed an area called Argiano that is not among the final twelve names; Sant'Ilario appears in the approved list instead.
it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-sant-ila.classification: Pieve: one of 12 unità geografiche aggiuntive of Vino Nobile di Montepulciano DOCG, named after historic parish churches and approved in the rules published by the EU in May 2025 (valid from the 2021 vintage). A "Vino Nobile di Montepulciano Pieve" must be at least 85% Sangiovese with only native partners, from the bottler's own vines at least 15 years old inside one Pieve, at no more than 7 t/ha, aged three years (one in wood, one in bottle).

it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-valardeg.name: Valardegna
it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-valardeg.grapes: Sangiovese (Prugnolo Gentile) at least 85%, the rest only Canaiolo Nero, Ciliegiolo, Colorino or Mammolo
it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-valardeg.summary: Valardegna lies just south-east of the town: coarse sands with lens-shaped pebble layers and a sandy-loam texture above, clayier soils lower down. Il Molinaccio di Montepulciano's 2021 was one of the most praised first Pieve wines, pure, spicy, saline and long.
it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-valardeg.terroir: South-east, next to the town; coarse sands with pebble lenses, clayier below.

it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-valiano.name: Valiano
it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-valiano.grapes: Sangiovese (Prugnolo Gentile) at least 85%, the rest only Canaiolo Nero, Ciliegiolo, Colorino or Mammolo
it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-valiano.summary: Valiano is the odd one out, east of the Val di Chiana and described by one critic as 'an island apart from the rest of Montepulciano': hilly land of fluvio-lacustrine origin with hazelnut-coloured sandy clays and calcium-carbonate nodules. Tenuta Trerose's 2021 is floral, fresh and supple with silky tannins, a sandy-soil expression of Sangiovese.
it-vino-nobile-di-montepulciano-valiano.terroir: East of the Val di Chiana; sandy clays with carbonate nodules on lake-basin hills.
